title: [CAP-FB-20260828-RUN-LOG-REGISTRY-ROWS-01] The registry writes two log rows straight to KV, bypassing the log
description:
## [CAP-FB-20260828-RUN-LOG-REGISTRY-ROWS-01] The registry writes two log rows straight to KV, bypassing the log
- Feedback: 2026-08-28 — found while implementing the WAL write buffer; a test written for terminal ordering failed and this was why
- Updated: 2026-08-28 17:30 UTC
- Status: DONE
- Priority: P1
- Owner: unassigned
- Workspace: none
- Branch: none
- Base: `f6d0cf23`
- Candidate: this commit
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: the `accepted` and terminal rows are appended to the run log like every other row, not written as `run-log:<exec>:accepted` / `:terminal` key-value records; a run that settles AFTER its log has been migrated still has its terminal row readable through `listLogs`; and purging an execution removes its log file and its migration marker as well as its KV rows, leaving no remnant
- Review: fresh-session review; falsification — the terminal-ordering test must be shown failing against the current build
- Gates: full unit suite including the terminal fault matrix (five injected-failure steps sit around the current `store.setTrusted` terminal write and will need reworking); Chrome journeys; `npm run test:opfs`
- Blockers: —
- Next: closed pending review. Unblocks `CAP-FB-20260828-RUN-LOG-WRITE-BUFFER-01`, which needs the terminal-ordering guarantee this provides
- Recover: `git grep -n 'LOG_PREFIX}\${executionId}:accepted\|LOG_PREFIX}\${executionId}:terminal' -- extension/lib/durable-runs.js`
- History:
  - 2026-08-28 — DONE at `origin/main@dc04e4c7`. Merged and green.
  - 2026-08-28 19:00 UTC — **fixed, with both properties falsified.** `accepted` and the terminal row now go through `appendRegistryRow` into the log instead of `store.setTrusted("run-log:<exec>:…")`. Both execution-ownership predicates claim the migration marker, and purging removes the log FILE (which is not in `store.keys()`) via an injectable `removeLogFor`. Falsification: putting the terminal write back on the key-value path turns the new regression test RED; removing the marker from the rollback predicate turns the remnant test RED. Note that the FIRST falsification attempt on the remnant test passed — because there are two ownership predicates and I had weakened the wrong one; the test only proved its point once the rollback path's predicate was the one broken.
  - 2026-08-28 19:00 UTC — the injected-failure tests were RETARGETED, not deleted, because the data moved rather than the property changing: `failDeleteKey`/`failKey` pointed at `run-log:<exec>:accepted`, a key-value row that no longer exists. The partial-delete test now targets the migration marker, and the quota test injects the fault where the write actually happens — `createMemoryRunLogHandles({ failWriteFor })`, a log-write fault. Both still assert exactly what they did before: a partial auxiliary delete preserves authority and retries safely, and a quota failure while admitting a run leaves every old log intact and strands nothing.
  - 2026-08-28 19:00 UTC — also fixed the reason this was hard to see: SIX `createDurableRunRegistry` call sites across five suites passed a fake `store` but no `logHandleFor`, so they reached past their own fake straight to real OPFS. All now inject `createMemoryRunLogHandles()` bound to the store. Gates: unit **1894/0** (2 new), Chrome journeys **127/127**, `npm run test:opfs` **6/6**, security suite PASS, build clean.
  - 2026-08-28 17:30 UTC — `start()` writes `run-log:<exec>:accepted` and the terminal path writes `run-log:<exec>:terminal` with `store.setTrusted`, bypassing `appendLog` entirely. That was harmless when reads came from the key-value store. Since `f6d0cf23` reads come from the WAL, and the KV→WAL migration is one-time and marker-guarded: **a row written to KV AFTER the marker is set is never read again.** In a real run `appendLog` is called during the run, so the marker is set before `settle()` — meaning the terminal log row is orphaned. Not currently user-visible, because `buildThreadRunView` takes run status from `e.record.terminal` rather than from the log row, which is why no shipped test caught it; it is still wrong, and it blocks any guarantee about ordering rows relative to the terminal.
  - 2026-08-28 17:30 UTC — the fix has a tail: once these rows live in the log, the two execution-ownership predicates that purge `run-log:<exec>:*` must also claim `run-log-wal:<exec>` (the migration marker — otherwise a purged execution leaves a remnant, AND a recreated one would skip migration) and must delete the log FILE, which is not in `store.keys()`. Attempted in the same session; five terminal fault-matrix steps then failed because they inject failures around the old `store.setTrusted` write. Recorded rather than rushed.

title: [CAP-FB-20260828-RUN-LOG-WRITE-BUFFER-01] Buffer and flush the run-log WAL
description:
## [CAP-FB-20260828-RUN-LOG-WRITE-BUFFER-01] Buffer and flush the run-log WAL
- Feedback: 2026-08-28 — product owner: "I think we need to buffer and flush the WAL", and then "if we do the buffer and flush, I'm presuming the read includes the buffer too, right?"
- Updated: 2026-08-28 17:30 UTC
- Status: DONE
- Priority: P1
- Owner: unassigned
- Workspace: none
- Branch: none
- Base: `f6d0cf23`
- Candidate: this commit
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: rows appended close together are coalesced into ONE file open, so writing 1,000 rows costs ~1 ms rather than ~14 s; `appendLog` still resolves only when the row is ON DISK, so an awaiting caller keeps today's durability guarantee; a reader can never miss a row that was already accepted; and no run reaches a terminal state with unflushed history behind it. Coalescing is asserted by COUNTING file opens, not inferred from a timing number
- Review: fresh-session review; falsification — the coalescing test must be shown failing against the unbuffered build
- Gates: full unit suite; Chrome journeys; `npm run test:opfs`; the security suite; and the `scripts/thread-open-trace.ts` matrix showing the write column drop
- Blockers: —
- Next: closed pending review. Streaming the first page (design stage 4) is NOT needed — at 27 ms for 1,000 rows it would add moving parts for no measurable gain
- Recover: `git grep -n "queueAppend\|flushExecution" -- extension/lib/durable-runs.js`
- History:
  - 2026-08-28 — DONE at `origin/main@dc04e4c7`. Merged and green.
  - 2026-08-28 21:00 UTC — **DONE. Task open 918 ms → 27 ms (~34x) and writing 1,000 rows 171,375 ms → 1,390 ms (~123x), against the pre-WAL baseline.** Full matrix: open 15/213/918 → 5/14/27 ms at 10/250/1,000 rows; write 140 ms/11.2 s/171 s → 30 ms/323 ms/1.4 s. Extrapolated to the product's own bound (6,250 rows), opening a task goes from ~6 s to ~170 ms. Gates: unit **1926/0**, Chrome journeys **127/127**, `npm run test:opfs` **6/6**, security suite PASS, build clean.
  - 2026-08-28 21:00 UTC — two changes carried the last order of magnitude. **(1) Coalescing:** the row is queued under the write lock and the flush awaited OUTSIDE it. Both halves matter — an earlier version awaited the flush while holding the lock, which serialised every append and produced **21 file writes for 20 concurrent appends**. The test asserts the write COUNT rather than a timing number, and was falsified: holding the lock across the flush takes it to 20 writes and the test RED. **(2) The preamble:** with file writes coalesced the remaining cost was per-append — a marker read and a directory/file open on every row, plus a SHA-256 computed whether or not it was needed. Marker and handle are stable for an execution's life and are memoised (cleared on purge); the digest is now computed only when a payload actually overflows, which is the only thing it names.
  - 2026-08-28 21:00 UTC — the owner's question is answered in the code and in a test: **a read FLUSHES, it does not merge the buffer.** One source of truth (the file), and byte cursors stay meaningful because a buffered row has no offset yet. The flush sits INSIDE the shared-lock callback, which has already awaited the write chain — placed before it, a read races an append that had been called but had not yet queued. Also asserted: an awaited append is genuinely on disk (a fresh registry over the same storage sees it), a run never settles with unflushed history behind it, and a failed flush REJECTS every caller whose row it carried rather than dropping rows silently.
  - 2026-08-28 17:30 UTC — **attempted, working, and reverted to keep main green.** The design is settled and was proven in the attempt: queue the row UNDER the write lock, await the flush OUTSIDE it, flush on a macrotask. Both halves matter — an earlier version awaited the flush while still holding the lock, which serialised every append and produced **21 file writes for 20 concurrent appends**, i.e. no coalescing at all. Measured after the fix: 20 concurrent appends → far fewer writes, with every row present.
  - 2026-08-28 17:30 UTC — **the owner's question answered: a read FLUSHES first, it does not merge the buffer.** Flushing keeps one source of truth (the file) and keeps byte cursors meaningful — a buffered row has no offset yet, so a merged view could not be paged back through. The flush must sit INSIDE the shared-lock callback, which has already awaited the write chain: placed before it, a read races an append that has been called but has not yet queued its row. Two tests for this are KEPT on main (`a read sees rows that were appended but not awaited`, `appendLog still resolves only once the row is durable`) because they hold for the current implementation too.
  - 2026-08-28 17:30 UTC — reverted because the change kept widening: buffering forces terminal ordering, which exposed `CAP-FB-20260828-RUN-LOG-REGISTRY-ROWS-01`, which forces the purge/rollback paths to delete the log file and the migration marker, which broke five fault-matrix steps that inject failures around the old `store.setTrusted` terminal write. Each of those is legitimate work; none of it should be rushed into the durable run authority at the tail of a long session. Main stays at the shipped 6.3x/12x.

## [CAP-FB-20260825-DATA-MEMORY-CLEAR-01] Data & memory Clear looks like it does nothing
- Feedback: 2026-08-25 — product owner: "The clear button doesn't work in Data & memory (at least for site agents)."
- Updated: 2026-08-25 19:20 UTC
- Status: DONE
- Resume: —
- Priority: P1
- Owner: claude-opus-5 implementer session
- Workspace: active (local path private)
- Branch: detached candidate on `origin/main`
- Base: `2c25e82`
- Candidate: this commit
- Shipping: this commit on `origin/main`
- Acceptance: clicking Clear on a site agent's row in Settings → Data & memory visibly empties that store without a reload — the memory explorer's key count for the origin drops to zero; the store really is empty; the agent stays enrolled, because clearing memory is not a revocation; and the owner is told what actually happened rather than being shown a success message the code never checked
- Review: author self-review 2026-08-25 (two further defects found and fixed, below); **no independent review** — the product owner asked the author to review directly
- Gates: `scripts/data-memory-clear.ts` **13/13** on a clean profile, with both regressions verified to FAIL against the unfixed code (`before=4 after=4` for the stale count, `after=[]` for the collapsed tree); unit 1591/0; Chrome journeys 127/127; security suite PASS
- Blockers: —
- Next: an independent pass if one becomes cheap; otherwise closed. `extension/memory/explorer.js` is a separate removal candidate, not a fix for this report
- Recover: `npm run test:data-clear && git grep -n "renderMemoryExplorer" -- extension/options/options.js`
- History:
  - 2026-08-25 19:20 UTC — **author self-review, not independent.** Two further defects found in my own fix, both fixed here. **(1) I introduced a UX regression:** making the explorer refresh meant it rebuilt the whole tree with every node collapsed, so clearing snapped shut whatever the owner had expanded — on precisely the refresh where they are looking at that store. Expansion is now keyed by a stable `data-mem-id` and restored across the rebuild, and a restored store re-fetches its (now empty) keys. Individual key/value nodes are deliberately NOT restored: their content can be stale after a clear, and collapsing one is far less disruptive than losing the tree. **(2) A third Clear button exists** in `extension/memory/explorer.js` with the same ignore-the-result shape. It is NOT reachable — nothing in the extension, tests or scripts links `memory/explorer.html` — so it is not the button in this report and is recorded as a removal candidate rather than fixed in place, which would have meant maintaining a dead surface.
  - 2026-08-25 19:20 UTC — also checked and found clean: every other `memory.clear` caller tolerates the new result shape (`scripts/opfs-real-browser.ts`, `scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` and the route-modularization test all ignore or destructure it safely).
  - 2026-08-25 18:30 UTC — reproduced exactly as reported and fixed. The data WAS being cleared; the UI just never showed it. The origin-row handler called `renderData()` (which redraws the enrolled-origins list, unchanged by a clear) but not `renderMemoryExplorer()` — and the explorer is the surface that displays keys and counts, so it kept showing the cleared store's old count until a reload. Both Clear handlers now refresh both surfaces.
  - 2026-08-25 18:30 UTC — second defect found while fixing the first: `memory.clear` resolved to `undefined`, so neither handler could tell success from failure and both flashed "Cleared…" unconditionally. The route now returns `{ok:true, origin}` or `{ok:false, error}`, and both handlers report the real outcome. A button that lies about having worked is the same class of bug as one that does nothing.
  - 2026-08-25 18:30 UTC — checked and ruled out a worse possibility: `clear()` does remove the site store's `enrolled` key, but enrollment authority does not live there, so a clear never silently disenrolls a Site Agent. Asserted in the new script so it stays true.
  - 2026-08-25 18:30 UTC — coverage lives in a dedicated `scripts/data-memory-clear.ts` on a clean profile rather than inside the 127-check journey suite. Adding it there first was tried and rejected: the fixture had to be created mid-suite, where accumulated global state (a revoked `storage` capability, several enrolled origins) made the explorer assertions unreliable, and the extra enrolled origin made a later step's first-match `.origin-row .disenroll-origin` click remove the wrong agent. A focused script tests the button instead of the suite's history.

## [CAP-FB-20260825-SITE-DISCOVERABILITY-01] Site-agent discoverability + content-script boot reconciliation

- Feedback: 2026-08-25 — product owner: "I can't work out how site agents get discovered and approved any more... I'm refreshing a site and it doesn't appear and I don't see any console logs."
- Updated: 2026-08-25 20:3x UTC

- Branch: —
- Base: `2c25e82`
- Candidate: `e152f7c0`
- Shipping: `origin/main@2bff0af` (0.2.267)
- Root cause: (a) chicken-and-egg — discovery required the content script to run, which only ran on ENROLLED origins (ensureOriginScriptsRegistered registers per-origin + host permission, transactional), so an un-enrolled site surfaced nothing; (b) enrolled origins' dynamic content scripts were not reconciled on SW startup/browser boot, so an enrolled site went silent after a restart ("no logs").

Security model verified hard (Pro e384c626): zero broad injection, host-permission grant stays owner-gesture, transactional enroll/rollback intact.
- Acceptance: an owner can see which open pages are discoverable and enroll one with a single explicit gesture, without typing an origin; discovery no longer requires the origin to be enrolled first; an already-enrolled origin's content scripts are re-registered on service-worker/browser boot so it does not go silent after a restart; no broad injection is introduced and the host-permission grant stays behind an owner gesture with transactional enroll/rollback intact
- Review: PASS (Pro e384c626), 1595/1595, manifest untouched.
- Gates: independent security review (Pro `e384c626`) confirming zero broad injection, owner-gesture host-permission grant and intact transactional enroll/rollback; 1595/1595 unit; manifest unchanged

title: [CAP-FB-20260827-DIALOG-CONSOLIDATION-01] Five dialog implementations, three hand-rolled
description:
## [CAP-FB-20260827-DIALOG-CONSOLIDATION-01] Five dialog implementations, three hand-rolled
- Feedback: 2026-08-27 — product owner: "There's lots of issues with dialogs"
- Updated: 2026-08-27 23:30 UTC
- Status: IN_REVIEW
- Priority: P1
- Owner: coordinator session
- Workspace: main
- Branch: main
- Base: `139b6f92`
- Candidate: —
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: every modal in the extension is raised through the shared component vocabulary — `<agent-dialog>` for a content dialog, `confirmActionDialog` for a decision — with no hand-rolled `document.createElement("dialog")` left outside `extension/shared/components.js`. Focus trap, Escape, backdrop light-dismiss, focus return, the destructive default-focus rule, scrollable overflow and theme/RTL/narrow behaviour are then identical everywhere by construction. Each converted site keeps its exact current semantics — in particular the provider-approval dialog must still be able only to DENY on dismissal, never approve
- Review: author review 2026-08-29 with the falsification gates cleared (see History); a11y behaviours driven in a real loaded extension by `scripts/kat-dialog-consolidation.ts` rather than asserted from source
- Gates: full unit suite; Chrome journeys green; gallery drift check green; the impeccable design pass
- Blockers: —
- Next: owner review of the three converted surfaces in the product. The remaining consolidation work — the ~30 other scripts and any future modal — is now prevented by construction rather than by convention, since there is one confirm and one shell
- Recover: `git grep -n 'createElement("dialog")' -- extension/`
- History:
  - 2026-08-29 — **all three hand-rolled dialogs converted; `createElement("dialog")` now appears exactly once in the extension, inside the shared component itself.** (1) `extension/artifacts/index.js` artifact delete → `confirmActionDialog`, gaining backdrop light-dismiss, an `aria-label` and a settled guard it did not have; its 13 lines of bespoke `.delete-dialog` CSS are deleted. (2) `confirmAgentProviderMutation` → the shared confirm. **This one carried a security property the shared confirm lacked** — approve only on a click that is `isTrusted` AND has active user activation — so rather than keep the duplicate for it, the property moved INTO the shared component as `requireGenuineGesture`, alongside `returnFocusTo` and `note`. Every future approval now gets it by construction instead of by remembering to re-implement it. (3) `editRecipePrompt` → `<agent-dialog>`, the content shell; it gains a close button and backdrop dismissal it never had, and its bespoke panel/backdrop CSS is replaced by the shell's. **Evidence, driven in a real loaded extension (`scripts/kat-dialog-consolidation.ts`, 18/18):** a destructive confirm focuses Cancel; a backdrop click resolves false and removes the node; a non-destructive confirm focuses the confirm control; **an untrusted scripted click cannot approve** and the refusal is explained in the dialog; Escape denies; the shell is announced by its title and its body scrolls on overflow. That last group is why this is a KAT and not only a unit test — a DOM shim cannot tell you whether `event.isTrusted` gating actually holds. **Falsification:** `tests/provider-options-approval.test.ts` pinned the OLD implementation's source lines and had to be rewritten; it now pins the property across BOTH halves (the call site must ASK for the check, the component must IMPLEMENT it and gate the true result on it), because asserting only one half would let the flag become a no-op or let the call site quietly stop passing it. Four deliberate regressions — call site drops the flag, component drops the trusted-click check, the guard warns without refusing, and the hand-rolled duplicate returns — each drove it red before being reverted. **Gates:** build clean; unit **2004 pass / 0 fail**; Chrome journeys **127/127**; gallery, vocabulary and tracker schema green.
  - 2026-08-27 23:30 UTC — captured by source audit. **Five dialog implementations ship.** Two are the intended shared ones in `extension/shared/components.js`: `<agent-dialog>` (the content-dialog shell) and `confirmActionDialog` (the promise-based confirm). Three are hand-rolled duplicates outside the component system: `extension/artifacts/index.js:83` (artifact delete), `extension/options/options.js:1236` (`confirmAgentProviderMutation`), and `extension/options/options.js:1555` (`editRecipePrompt`). This is precisely the failure mode the owner already named as a project rule — "never hand-roll a one-off version of an existing component (the blank-toggle + menu bugs came from hand-rolled duplicates)" — and it is the most likely explanation for dialogs behaving inconsistently: each of the five owns its own focus, dismiss, overflow and sizing behaviour, so a fix to one does not reach the others.
  - 2026-08-27 23:30 UTC — **good news worth recording:** `window.confirm` / `window.alert` / `window.prompt` are already fully eliminated from the extension; the only remaining occurrence is the explanatory comment above `confirmActionDialog`. `CAP-FB-20260823-DIALOG-CONFIRM-MODERNIZATION-01` is therefore substantially further along than its OPEN status suggests — what is left of that task is this consolidation.

description:
## [CAP-FB-20260829-AGENT-BOARD-01] The shared jobs board: agents post and claim work
- Feedback: 2026-08-29 — owner voice note: "agents should be able to ask other agents for work… the chaos extension had a shared message board and a shared jobs board"
- Updated: 2026-08-29 UTC
- Status: DONE
- Priority: P1
- Owner: coordinator session
- Workspace: worker lane
- Branch: cap-agent-board
- Base: `c6406cc7`
- Candidate: `cdb8b491` (r5) — landed as merge `54d70a9b`
- Shipping: 0.2.400
- Acceptance: six management tools, claim lease/expiry, blockedBy DAG, delivery to poster thread, Tasks sidebar Board section
- Review: independent reviewer PASS (round 6); six rounds closed data-integrity findings (fold divergence, forgeable keys, destructive reads, eviction, admission reserve, claim churn, drain kick)
- Gates: suite 2358/0 at merge, board KAT 22/22, build green
- Blockers: none
- Next: idle-agent wake (deferred) — the per-edge deny layer LANDED 2026-08-30 (owner Settings UI, fail-closed guards, corrupt-store refusal)
- Recover: revert merge `54d70a9b`
- What it is: the async/broadcast complement to `delegate_to_agent`. A hub-level
  event-sourced board (jobs + messages logs in the master memory tier) where any
  named agent or the hub posts work, and any capable agent claims it (atomic
  claim + 5-minute lease + heartbeat, the scheduler's exact constants). Tools:
  board_post_job / board_claim_job / board_complete_job / board_send_message /
  board_list / board_read. Results ride back on the job record; the Tasks
  sidebar gains a "Board" grouping (open jobs + latest messages, bounded,
  textContent-only). Guards are pure functions in `extension/lib/agent-board.js`
  mirroring `agent-delegation.js`; caller identity comes from the route context
  (never model args).
- Permission model (owner decision 2026-08-29; deny layer landed 2026-08-30):
  default-open among named agents + the hub, plus owner-controlled per-edge
  DENY rules (Settings → Board permissions; owner-options principal only;
  fail-closed on malformed rules and corrupt store; rules load fresh inside
  each locked post/claim).
- DEFERRED (planned extensions): automatic wake of idle agents on post
  (scheduler/alarm machinery — v1 wakes live surfaces via broadcastProgress);
  bidding/auctions; cross-device boards; A2A wire-protocol interop.
- History:
  - 2026-08-29 — lane built: board lib + SW routes + 6 management tools +
    capability/replay classifications + Tasks-sidebar grouping; 20 unit tests +
    12-check browser KAT (screenshot evidence) green; suite 2266/0.
  - 2026-08-29 — review round 1 REVISE (6×P1 + 3×P2) fixed: board log keys
    reserved from the model's memory_set/memory_get/keys (memory.js
    MASTER_RESERVED_KEYS + hidden namespace; the store uses setTrusted/
    getStrict); event-time lease expiry in the fold (expired claims are
    reclaimable); pruning preserves settled jobs an open job still depends
    on; both logs byte-bounded (192 KiB < the 256 KiB per-value cap) with
    superseded-heartbeat compaction + a fail-closed board-full post gate;
    stale model contexts denied (never hub-escalated); settlements commit
    the result to the poster's thread through the durable thread-commit seam
    (idempotent by board:<jobId>); visible row metadata (never title-only);
    the browser KAT now drives a REAL named-agent claim→complete via the
    @demo-board demo-model marker + asserts live UI refresh; heartbeat
    parity pinned. 31 unit tests + 22-check KAT green; suite 2277/0.
  - 2026-08-29 — review round 2 REVISE (3×P1) fixed: failed/malformed log
    reads propagate instead of becoming destructive empty-log writes (only a
    successful null read means absent; routes surface a structured
    board-store-error); byte/count eviction now leaves compact settled
    TOMBSTONES (identity + outcome + truncated result + delivery state) so
    acknowledged settlements stay retry-idempotent (alreadySettled) and
    readable, with full records capped separately from tombstones;
    poster-thread delivery is durable — the pending delivery persists WITH
    the settle event, the settle ACK waits on the idempotent
    board:<jobId> thread commit, and a startup drain plus the
    repeated-settle path re-attempt delivery. 37 unit tests + 22-check KAT
    green; suite 2283/0.

Cherry-picked onto current `main` (the tracker row and CHANGELOG conflicted and were resolved keeping both lanes' content). **My own falsification, not the implementer's:** adding `--remote-debugging-port=9351` to `kat-usage-viz.ts` drove the gate RED (4 pass / 1 fail); removing it returned to green — so the gate fails for the right reason. A `grep` for a fixed port anywhere under `scripts/` now returns nothing outside the launcher. Gates at the merge tip: build clean, unit **2004 pass / 0 fail**, Chrome journeys **127/127**, gallery + tracker schema green. **One correction applied on merge:** the second test was named "only the shared launcher writes the debugging-port flag" but asserted merely that the launcher is *among* the writers — roughly thirty other scripts spawn Chrome themselves with the safe `=0` form. Renamed to "the shared launcher owns the debugging-port flag" and documented the scope in the test, because a test that claims more than it checks is the same defect class this entry exists to fix. The safety property (no script may name a port) is enforced by the first test and is unaffected. Migrating the remaining ~30 scripts onto `launchChrome()` is a separate cleanup, not a defect.
  - 2026-08-29 — **converted, falsified and gated.** Twelve harnesses now launch through one shared `scripts/lib/chrome-launch.ts`; `launchChrome()` passes `--remote-debugging-port=0` and reads the DevTools endpoint out of its OWN child's stderr, so the endpoint provably belongs to this process and there is no probe to race. The port-0 form was used everywhere — no harness needed the weaker probe-then-bind fallback — and the two scripts that already carried private copies of that helper (`kat-noun-discipline`, `kat-bgagent-delete`) were folded onto the shared launcher too, leaving one spawn path instead of nine fixed ports and two copies. FALSIFICATION: a decoy browser was started holding 9351 (the port `kat-usage-viz` hard-coded) running a deliberately altered copy of the extension; the PRE-CHANGE harness, pointed at the real tree, reported `FAIL: cost card is labelled an estimate — "costs are DECOY approximations (this tree is NOT under test)"` — a string that exists only in the decoy — proving it drove a browser it did not launch; the converted harness, with that same decoy still holding the port, passed 13/13 against the real tree. CONCURRENCY: `kat-usage-viz` + `kat-ux-lows` (both 9351) run together — before, one lane hung to a 300 s timeout when the other killed the browser they were sharing; after, both finish with their solo results. Individually every harness matches its pre-change tally: back-stack 6/0, dark-scheme 32/3, narrow-toggle 20/0, usage-viz 13/0, ux-lows 9/1, axe-audit 7/0, providers-tabs 19/0, agent-templates 13/0, composer-grow 11/0, noun-discipline 14/0, bgagent-delete 11/0 (the 3 dark-scheme and 1 ux-lows failures are pre-existing contrast/landmark findings, unchanged by this work); `kat-failed-runs` went from hanging for the full 300 s timeout against a live zombie on 9357 to 7/0 in 10 s. TWO THINGS FOUND THAT THE REPORT DID NOT DESCRIBE: the slow port poll was also masking a startup race — reading the endpoint off stderr is fast enough that MV3 has not registered its service worker yet, so eight harnesses gained an explicit bounded `waitForServiceWorker()` instead of depending on how long a probe happened to take; and `kat-bgagent-delete`'s own helper called `Deno.listen` outside its `try`, so a taken port threw out of the function rather than moving on to the next. A new gate, `tests/harness-debug-port.test.ts`, fails on any fixed debugging port anywhere in `scripts/` and on a launcher that would accept a caller-chosen one; it was observed RED with a port reintroduced into `kat-usage-viz` and GREEN with it removed.
  - 2026-08-29 — measured, then corrected after the reporting lane pointed out the failure mode is worse than "a flake". **A fixed-port harness does not merely hang or error — it attaches to another lane's browser and reports confident PASS/FAIL results about an extension it is not testing.** The reporting run produced 7 such results. That means a fixed-port harness can go **green against the wrong tree**, which is worse than a red suite, because the output reads as evidence. Eleven scripts name a port; two of them (`kat-bgagent-delete` on `cbf89c33`, `kat-noun-discipline`) already probe for a free one, leaving **nine hard-coded**. Four ports are each claimed by two of those nine: 9347 (`kat-narrow-toggle`, `kat-dark-scheme`), 9351 (`kat-usage-viz`, `kat-ux-lows`), 9353 (`kat-providers-tabs`, `axe-audit`), 9359 (`kat-agent-templates`, `kat-composer-grow`); `kat-failed-runs` holds 9357, the port `kat-bgagent-delete` starts probing from. 28 other scripts already launch with `--remote-debugging-port=0` and read the real port off the `DevTools listening` line, and `scripts/kat-noun-discipline.ts` carries a reusable `freePort()` (probe `/json/version`, then bind-test) — so both the pattern and a helper are already in-repo.

description:
## [CAP-FB-20260828-ARTIFACT-LIBRARY-CAPACITY-01] The library still evicts the owner's oldest artifact silently
- Feedback: 2026-08-28 — found while fixing `CAP-FB-20260828-ARTIFACT-DURABILITY-01`; same bug class, deliberately not folded into that fix
- Updated: 2026-08-28 04:30 UTC
- Status: OPEN
- Priority: P1
- Owner: unassigned
- Workspace: none
- Branch: none
- Base: `4ed8cf8a`
- Candidate: —
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: the artifact library never silently discards the owner's work. When the index reaches its bound the owner is told and given a choice — the create fails honestly, or old artifacts are offered for review — rather than the oldest row being dropped inside a write it did not ask for. Whatever the policy, a test proves an artifact cannot leave the library without either an explicit `asset.delete` or an owner-visible decision
- Review: fresh-session review; falsification — the test must be shown failing against a build that still evicts silently
- Gates: unit suite; Chrome journeys green; `npm run test:opfs`
- Blockers: needs an owner decision — refusing a create fails a task mid-run, while evicting loses work silently. Both are bad in different ways and it is a product call, not an engineering one
- Next: put the two options to the owner with the real numbers (the bound is now ~15,000 rows) before building either
- Recover: `git grep -n "maxIndexBytes" -- extension/lib/artifacts.js`
- History:
  - 2026-08-28 04:30 UTC — the index carries a byte bound and, when a create would exceed it, drops the OLDEST rows (`idx = idx.slice(1)`) and records eviction obligations to clean their bodies. For a library whose stated purpose is being "the central source of all the information that has been created by the worker", silently discarding the oldest thing the person made is the wrong terminal behaviour — it is the same class as the bug just fixed, reached by a different route. The durability fix raised the bound from 128 KiB to 2 MiB (~940 rows to ~15,000) because the bound had been PER ORIGIN and became shared, which would otherwise have been a capacity regression. That defers the problem by roughly an order of magnitude; it does not fix it, and it is recorded here rather than left implied.
close_reason: DONE — `origin/main@adfc1c20`

Agents / Recent artifacts / Recent activity are three catalogs answering "what objects exist?" A colleague-shaped environment answers "what is in flight, what is waiting on me, what came back while I was away?" — the same information with a different spine. Judge the redesign against that question, not against card count.

Today the hub answers the second half with three mostly-empty cards and answers the first half with a composer placed below them.   the most relevant tools instead of every available definition
- Updated: 2026-08-22 09:30 UTC

- Priority: P1

- Workspace: none
- Branch: none
- Base: `ecf657fe2f9e32aee7b5e2043808f4f7978fd456`
- Candidate: —
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: one local versioned catalog indexes every callable built-in tool,
  extension-provided tool, declared WebMCP tool and positively inferred WebMCP
  tool with stable source, scope, generation/document identity, bounded
  description, schema summary and searchable text; each run retrieves a bounded
  top-k set by semantic/cosine relevance plus deterministic exact-name/alias and
  lexical fallback, and only that authorized set is exposed to the model;
  retrieval never grants permission, bypasses source-specific dispatch, crosses
  origin/agent boundaries, revives removed tools, or lets untrusted tool text
  alter ranking policy or protected prompts; index updates, removals, extension
  upgrades, navigation, service-worker restart and offline startup converge
  without sending the whole catalog; owner diagnostics explain selected,
  excluded, stale and fallback results without exposing secrets or private data
- Review: P0 tool-platform research fixes this as the sole semantic-retrieval
  authority; the catalog contract's deterministic exact/alias/lexical fallback
  is a prerequisite, not a duplicate semantic engine; independent architecture,
  retrieval-quality, security/privacy, lifecycle, performance and exact
  loaded-MV3 review required before semantic implementation acceptance
- Gates: compare SQLite/Wasm and IndexedDB storage/indexing under MV3 CSP,
  worker lifetime, migration, quota and crash semantics; compare local embedding
  choices, dimensions, update cost and deterministic lexical fallback; build a
  versioned bounded corpus spanning all four tool sources with
  relevance/precision/recall and token-budget targets plus measured budgets for
  catalog-scale warm-query latency, cold/offline startup, full index build,
  incremental add/update/remove, persisted index bytes and peak memory;
  establish explicit device/corpus tiers and pass/fail budgets during research
  before implementation; exact-name, paraphrase, multi-intent, low-confidence,
  collision and no-match queries; adversarial
  descriptions/schema/prompt-injection and oversized/Unicode fixtures;
  source/generation/origin/permission fencing;
  add/update/remove/navigation/restart/offline/corruption recovery; loaded-MV3

  tools remain undisclosed and uncallable
- Blockers: embedding model/runtime, ranking thresholds/top-k/token budget,
  semantic storage engine (SQLite versus IndexedDB), device tiers, update

  `CAP-FB-20260822-LAZY-TOOL-PROTOCOL-01`, `CAP-FB-20260818-WEBMCP-01`, page

design:
## Design (2026-09-02, cap-beads-4dg increment): in-context provider host-access grant card

Scope: the last remaining Settings-redirect dead-end in the permission UX. Every
browser-tool denial already renders one in-context `<permission-approval-card>`
(Allow / Not now) — but when the configured NETWORK provider's exact origin is
not granted, the conversation preflight (extension/shared/conversation.js
runConversationTurn, "provider.permission-summary" check) appends a terminal
error reading "open Settings → Providers and approve that exact origin" and the
turn ends. The card UX directive: when an agent needs a permission, show an
in-context card, not a Settings redirect, with a clear grant/deny choice.

Change:
- On preflight ungranted-origin: do NOT return a dead-end error. Render ONE
  in-context permission card via the existing maybeRenderApproval machinery
  with requirement `{ reason: "connect to <host> (the provider that runs this
  task)", hostOrigins: [exact origin] }` (hostOrigins = the read-page-host-grant
  shape: Allow requests `<origin>/*` through chrome.permissions.request from
  the owner's genuine card click; the same request Settings' Use button makes).
- Allow (grant succeeds) → the run starts (executeTurn) — the SW run gate then
  passes; no Settings trip. Not now → honest terminal denial bubble: "Network
  access to <host> was not granted — you declined. The run did not start."
- Grant refused by Chrome → card shows the error and stays pending (Try again),
  matching the live-card contract; nothing is granted silently.
- Config problems (missing/invalid base URL, local-provider checks) are
  UNCHANGED — Settings remains the right surface for a configuration edit; this
  increment covers only the permission ask.

Mechanics (conversation.js only):
- runConversationTurn gains a pre-run pause state between the preflight and the
  first executeTurn: maybeRenderApproval is called with two new internal
  options (preRun: skips the legacy turn-retry flag, settle: an entry resolver)
  so the outer flow awaits the card decision deterministically — no polling,
  no double-run (the legacy approvalRetryRequested path would otherwise start a
  second attempt after a granted pre-run card).
- The user's own message bubble renders first (today the dead-end leaves the
  conversation without it).

Why hostOrigins: provider network access IS Chrome site access for one exact
origin (`<origin>/*`). The card already renders "Access this site: <origin>",
the exact-scope request, the "Chrome will ask you to confirm" note, and
granted/denied/error states. Reuse beats a new card type.

Not in scope (later increments of the bead): durable pending inbox for
background/scheduled runs with no open surface; multi-waiter ordering on one
browser-global permission; Settings decision history; in-run provider-access
revocation recovery (post-error) — the mid-run path still ends honestly and
points at Settings for the re-grant.

Tests: unit test driving runConversationTurn with a stubbed
provider.permission-summary (ungranted origin) + fake DOM container asserting:
(1) no Settings-redirect error is appended, one permission card entry is
created, status waiting-for-permission; (2) Allow → chrome.permissions.request
carries exactly the provider's `<origin>/*` and agent.run then executes exactly
once; (3) Not now → honest declined error, agent.run never dispatched, nothing
granted.

glm-flash-1 increment-4 PLAN (read-only prep 2026-09-10, no implementation until astra's verdict lands). Seam map from origin/main tip 16558323:

(1) DURABLE OWNER INBOX — design doc §3.1/§3.2 is the spec authority (GRANTED_WAITING_RESUME_POLICY neutral state). Today runs live only in SW memory: an MV3 restart orphans a paused-for-permission run and no owner-facing record survives. Plan: bounded chrome.storage.local inbox records {runRef, requirement (reason/patterns/permissions), createdAt, lease generation, state} — NO task args/secrets (doc's leakage rule); SW writes the record when a run pauses on permission; the conversation + a Settings surface render it owner-only; deny/cancel write terminal outcomes (doc's distinct DENIED vs CANCELLED); resume = deterministic same-run continuation after grant per the acceptance line and the 2026-08-22 settled policy ('auto-resume on restart, visible pause + resume for recoverable permission problems'). OPEN OWNER QUESTION to settle before implementation: post-GRANT resume gesture — the doc keeps explicit-Resume and auto-resume as two OPEN alternatives; I read the settled policy + acceptance ('deterministically resumes the same run') as auto-resume after grant with the pause visible, but this needs one word from Paul or a reviewer ruling. Storage budget + alarms keepalive under memory-resilience constitution; inbox records expire (doc's pending TTL) so they never accumulate.

(2) MULTI-WAITER ORDERING — the primitive EXISTS: extension/lib/perm-lease.js + routes/perm-lease.js (SW single authority per canonical pattern, generation + owner token, 8s lease, backpressure, settle broadcast consumed by options.js + conversation.js). m6id's repro (get_cookie then list_cookies: second card never renders, then 'Approval expired') is the consumer side: the second same-pattern acquire hits the in-flight lease (busy) and the card flow drops it instead of queueing. Fix shape (belongs to m6id or a joint increment): on busy-acquire, subscribe the waiter to the lease's settle broadcast and render the card when the slot frees — never a second concurrent Chrome prompt (the lease's whole point), never a silent drop; expiry stays honest (fail fast with the structured denial). Keep MAX_LEASE_MS/64-slot bounds untouched.

(3) IN-RUN REVOCATION RECOVERY — seam: chrome.permissions.onRemoved in the SW. Today a mid-run revoke surfaces only when the next API call fails. Plan: onRemoved → match revoked patterns against in-flight runs' granted-requirement records → mark the run paused-on-revoked with the structured requirement (reuse waitingForPermission shape) → the existing remediation-card path offers the re-grant. Sequencing dependency: this builds on increments 1-2 (preRun/settle card machinery + post-error remediation card, cap-beads-4dg 5348484a + cap-perm-remediation-4dg2 8913139d, both UNMERGED) — increment 4 should not start until coord rules on landing/rebasing those two, or it re-derives their machinery. My increment-3 Settings Revoke is the owner gesture that fires onRemoved, so the surfaces compose.

Verification plan for whichever increments run: RED→GREEN falsification per gate; loaded-MV3 browser checks (SW restart mid-pause for the inbox; two scripted same-pattern tool calls for multi-waiter; live revoke from my Settings surface mid-run); constitution memory bounds on every new persisted map.
COORD RULINGS 2026-09-10 23:32 on increment-4 plan (glm-flash-1 recording):

(1) RESUME GESTURE — the doc's two alternatives are SUPERSEDED by the shipped per-tool replay-safety rule (extension/lib/tool-replay-safety.js on main; ARCHITECTURE.md §2.3; WEB-PLATFORM-AGENT-CONCEPT.md §2.7): read-only runs auto-resume; idempotent runs resume with stable per-call keys; mutating/unknown runs wait for the explicit owner Resume gesture on the card. docs/permission-remediation-design.md §3.2 ('two alternatives, neither normative') is AMENDED by this shipped classification — §3.2's neither-normative wording predates it and is recorded here as amended, per coord. Implementation of the inbox resume paths follows the class rule, not the doc's open alternatives.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
DESIGN (cap-beads-lj7 lane) — Directory tool explorer + enrollment policy, posted before implementation.

RESEARCHED DECISION (enrollment vs per-tool/invocation approval; resolves the bead blocker):
- Enrollment (owner gesture that makes a site a Site Agent) remains the coarse ALLOW and the consent for that origin's tools as a class (WEBMCP-AUTOAPPROVE-01 stands — no per-tool approval UI dead-ends).
- Per-tool invocation consent exists ONLY as the per-site "ask" policy state, paid per call through the SAME in-run owner-approval card machinery the destructive/cookie classes use (requireOwnerApproval, CAP-FB-20260830-DESTRUCTIVE-ACTION-POLICY-01). Unattended/scoped runs without a conversation fail closed (never auto-run).
- Directory (owner surface) always shows truthful per-tool provenance for review; the AGENT toolset is where deny excludes tools.

POLICY MODEL — per-site, stored in the enrollment registry entry (cap:enrollment, atomic under the existing global enrollment lock, generation bumped on change so in-flight catalogs revoke):
1. allow (default) — tools flow today unchanged (enrollment = consent).
2. deny — the site's tools are EXCLUDED from every agent toolset (readSiteLazySources returns no records — the falsification gate) and every invocation path fails closed with a named reason (authorization-guard conjunct + invokeSiteTool early reject).
3. ask — tools stay discoverable; every invocation pays an in-conversation owner card (Allow once / Deny) via a new extension-only approval action webmcp.use-tool, gated by the run-bound model dispatcher threaded into the WebMCP dispatch closure; absent a card channel the call fails closed honestly.

EXPLORER UX (extension/directory):
- Per-site groups keep bounded tool cards (name, description, input-schema summary, source chip) and gain page provenance (declaring page URL) on the card + origin in the heading.
- Each site group header gains the enrollment-policy control: Allow / Ask before use / Blocked, exactly labelled to the site; Blocked sections state the site's tools are not available to agents; cards carry the policy state so a blocked/"ask" badge can never detach from the tool (containment + exact AX labels per the acceptance).

SEAMS: extension/lib/tools.js (registry policy column + get/set + snapshot carries policy); extension/lib/webmcp-authority.js (pure deny conjunct "site-policy-denied" + guard); extension/background/service-worker.js (readSiteLazySources exclusion + ask dispatch gate + invokeSiteToolCore deny + tools.policies/tools.policy.set routes + webmcp.use-tool approval route); extension/lib/owner-approval.js (approvable action webmcp.use-tool + canonical target kind); directory UI + tool-directory-card page row.

TESTS (falsification-gated): enroll + declare tools → set deny → build the agent toolset exactly as readSiteLazySources does → the blocked site's tool MUST NOT appear and its invocation MUST fail closed with the named reason; allow default regression (tool present + dispatches); ask gate: dispatch consults the owner gate (approved → runs, denied → refused); registry unit tests (default allow, set/get, generation bump).

DESIGN: Python in the browser via Pyodide (MVS Option A)

1. Runtime & Sandbox Contract (extension/lib/python-execution.js & python-runtime.js):

   - Replay safety & argument contracts configured in tool-replay-safety.js and tool-argument-contract.js.

3. Execution Dispatch & Service Worker Integration:
   - Integrated into lazy-tool-protocol dispatch and service-worker execution paths.
   - Tested with deterministic unit/mock KATs and real browser execution.

WHAT icf1 LANDED. scripts/lib/chrome-for-testing.ts now resolves Chrome for Testing from the puppeteer cache glob ($HOME/.cache/puppeteer/chrome/*/chrome-linux64/chrome, newest version ranked NUMERICALLY, executable-bit checked, falling back to the next newest when a candidate is incomplete, null when nothing resolves). tests/chrome-for-testing.test.ts pins the ordering (including the lexicographic trap: 99 must not outrank 100), the null cases, the fallback and an absence pin over the resolver's own code. tests/bgagent-delete.test.ts resolves at MODULE LOAD and reports the journey `ignore`d when nothing resolves — visible in the runner's tally as "1 ignored" instead of a green that asserted nothing — and asserts the harness's own tally (>= 11 checks, 0 failed) so a journey that stopped checking cannot read as a pass. scripts/kat-bgagent-delete.ts resolves the same glob, so the gate and the browser it drives cannot disagree. tests/machine-path-honesty.test.ts's ALLOWED map is now EMPTY and stays self-tracking (an entry that stops matching fails).

WHAT IS STILL PINNED. Seven harnesses carry the identical absolute, version-pinned literal `/home/<user>/.cache/puppeteer/chrome/linux-140.0.7339.82/chrome-linux64/chrome`:
  scripts/kat-agent-delegation.ts:31

  scripts/kat-scheduled-next-run-widget.ts:21

  scripts/kat-ux-lows.ts:25
They are invisible to the guard because tests/machine-path-honesty.test.ts walks tests/ ONLY. Every one of them is class "kat" in scripts/lib/harness-registry.ts, i.e. run by scripts/kat-runner.ts (npm run test:kat), not by a unit test — so today they are driven on this machine only, and on any other box they die at spawn with an ENOENT that does not name the cause.

WHAT TO DO.
1. Replace each literal with `resolveChromeForTesting()` from scripts/lib/chrome-for-testing.ts and fail fast the way kat-bgagent-delete.ts now does (a `FAIL:` line naming the expected glob and the install command, then a non-zero exit) — never a silent skip and never a fallback to scripts/lib/chrome-launch.ts's `/usr/bin/chromium` default, because the Arch chromium wrapper ignores --load-extension and would drive a tree with no extension in it and still print confident results.
2. RE-VERIFY EACH JOURNEY on the resolved newest build (this machine resolves linux-150.0.7871.24; the pin was 140.0.7339.82). Record the tally per harness before and after. 3. EXTEND THE GUARD TO COVER THE RULE, NOT TODAY'S INSTANCE (AGENTS.md: "A pin that covers a RULE rather than one file also needs a second mutant that adds a fresh instance of the rule"). Make tests/machine-path-honesty.test.ts scan scripts/ as well as tests/ — or add a sibling guard that does — so a new absolute home path anywhere in the repo's executable test/harness surface is an immediate red with the allowlist still EMPTY. Ship it with the mutant that proves it: re-introduce one literal into a scripts/ harness and show the guard red, then remove it and show green, reporting the kill by assertion and message.

ACCEPTANCE. `grep -rn "\.cache/puppeteer" tests/ scripts/` returns only the resolver and prose; `npm run test:changed` then `npm test` green; each of the seven journeys driven for real on the resolved build with its tally recorded (a harness that cannot run says so loudly — never a green that skipped); the expected-red tallies either unchanged or re-adjudicated with a reason; the extended guard observed RED under the planted mutant and GREEN without it; independent review; push an explicit SHA.

That is a distro path rather than a home path, so it is outside the defect class the guard exists for, but it is the same shape — a default that silently drives the wrong browser on a box without it. If it is touched, note that tests/harness-debug-port.test.ts pins launchChrome as the ONLY writer of the debugging-port flag and tests/chrome-profile-isolation.test.ts / chrome-profile-location.test.ts scan every launch site.

title: chrome-journeys CDP evaluate budget vs fleet density: measure the latency tail, then fix by measured budget + quiet-window refusal (not by hope)
description: Five chrome-journeys runs on 2026-09-07 (two trees, multiple machine states incl. a genuinely quiet window at load 0.36-0.74) aborted on 'cdp timeout: Runtime.evaluate' at FIVE DIFFERENT positions: 278, 229, 229, 195, 159 of 370. The registry's last 370/370 (eo4d.1 r4) was an uninterrupted quiet window at lower fleet density; the gate cannot complete at the current ~9 concurrent pi sessions. Mechanism: the CDP client applies ONE flat per-call budget (opts.timeoutMs ?? 30000, chrome-launch.ts ~503) to every send — including Runtime.evaluate with awaitPromise:true, whose wall time depends on page work + machine load. Owner-accepted outcome classes: raised budget OR dedicated runner OR documented fleet-quiesce — MEASURE which. PLAN: (1) instrument the journeys' cdp sends with per-call timing, run once at current density, collect the evaluate-latency distribution (p50/p95/max); (2) set the journeys' evaluate budget from the measured tail (journeys-specific option; the 30s default stays for every other harness); (3) wire chrome-journeys into the EXISTING requireQuiet mechanism (mkax) so an under-threshold start refuses loudly (exit 75 + ENVIRONMENT: line — already pinned by lrok's quiet-window.test.ts) instead of dying mid-run and burning 10 minutes to reach 195/370; (4) decide retry-once-on-evaluate-timeout from the measured tail shape, not by hope. title: A green test that asserts nothing off its author's machine: the predecessor-digest block is unreachable behind a .catch, and absolute paths in tests go unguarded
description:
APPROVED AS ITS OWN BEAD by coord 2026-09-07 22:02Z: "the conditional-death class (green test, unreachable
assertions, silent-skip via .catch) deserves the name and the fix shape you specified: predecessor from git
history with missing-predecessor-FAILS, plus the cheap absolute-path static guard that would have caught all
six instances. Take it after the quiet-window re-anchors." Coord also named it the FIFTH pin/test-failure
mode for the canon: a test that asserts nothing outside its author's machine.

Sequenced AFTER the quiet-window DEFEATABLE re-anchors (owner directive). Reported by qwen (01a07d6e) as a
drive-by while verifying that chrome-agent-platform-c9y8's sentinels survived 37c71f14; NOT touched, because
mixing a product-test fix into a guard-extension candidate would have muddy-ed that review.

THE CLASS. A test that is green everywhere and asserts something only on the machine that wrote it. Three
ingredients, all present here: (1) a precondition read from a path that exists only in the author's
environment, (2) the assertions placed INSIDE `if (precondition)`, and (3) a `.catch(() => null)` on the read
so the missing precondition is silent instead of loud. Remove any one ingredient and the failure mode
disappears: a committed precondition makes it portable, unconditional assertions make it honest, and no catch
makes it fail loudly on a fresh clone.

THE INSTANCE (verified at origin/main 37c71f14, introduced by e78eaa55 — not by today's work).
tests/bundled-tool-packages.test.ts:502-530, test name "regeneration preserves predecessor manifest digests
except intentional admissions":

    const prevText = await Deno.readTextFile("/home/paulkinlan/worktrees/cap-bundled-tool-packages-163/extension/lib/bundled-inventory-data.js").catch(() => null);
    if (prevText) {
      const prevDigests = [...prevText.matchAll(/"pkg": "(cap\.bundled\.[^"]+)",\s*"version": "1\.0\.0",\s*"digest": "([0-9a-f]{64})"/g)];
      assertEquals(prevDigests.length, 25);
      ... a 25-package TRANCH set, per-package digest-preservation asserts, and the intentional-admission
          exceptions (assert(now.get(pkg) !== dg, "... intentionally changed ...")) ...
    }

MEASURED, NOT INFERRED:
* `ls /home/paulkinlan/worktrees/cap-bundled-tool-packages-163` -> No such file or directory. The
  predecessor exists nowhere on this machine.
* The test runs and passes in 707 µs (`npm run test:file -- tests/bundled-tool-packages.test.ts --filter
  "regeneration preserves predecessor"`) — far too fast to have parsed a 25-package predecessor inventory and
  run the block.
* SIX assertions live inside the `if (prevText)` block and never execute. What the test actually asserts on
  every machine but the author's: the sqlite identity is present, and `manifests.length === 38`.
So the predecessor-digest PRESERVATION property and the INTENTIONAL-ADMISSION exceptions — the two things the
test name promises — are unpinned on every checkout, CI run and fresh clone, and the suite is green.

THE SAME FILE'S NEIGHBOURS, for scale (all six absolute machine paths in tests/ on origin/main, found with
`git grep -n '"/home/paulkinlan' origin/main -- tests/`):
* tests/bundled-tool-packages.test.ts:506 — the silent one above. HIGHEST severity: `.catch(() => null)` plus
  conditional assertions.
* tests/jxl-admission.test.ts:222 and :231 — `Deno.readFile("/home/paulkinlan/cap-evidence/cap-jxl/fixtures/…")`
  with NO catch. Different failure mode: these fail LOUDLY on any other machine, so they are a portability
  defect, not a silent one. Fix by committing the fixtures or generating them.
* tests/bgagent-delete.test.ts:192 — a Chrome binary path under ~/.cache/puppeteer. Check whether it is a
  fallback with a resolution path before calling it a defect.
* tests/durable-root.test.ts:23-24 — sets CAP_DURABLE_ROOT to a literal and asserts the same literal. NOT a
  defect: the path is a fixture value, never read. Any static guard must not flag it, or it will be
  switched off.

WHAT TO DO (coord-approved shape).
1. Make the predecessor portable and its absence LOUD. Read the previous release's
   extension/lib/bundled-inventory-data.js from GIT HISTORY rather than from a worktree path — e.g.
   `git show <previous release tag or HEAD~N>:extension/lib/bundled-inventory-data.js` — or from a committed
   fixture. If no predecessor can be resolved, the test must FAIL with the reason, not skip: a missing
   precondition is a broken test, and `.catch(() => null)` around a precondition is what turned this green.
2. Move the assertions out of the conditional, or make the conditional itself an assertion
   (`assert(prevText, "the predecessor inventory must resolve — without it this test asserts nothing")`).
3. Add the cheap STATIC GUARD that would have caught all six: no test file may contain an absolute
   filesystem path outside the repo. It is a small static pin in the established idiom (the repo already has
   tree-scanning guards of this shape — tests/durable-root.test.ts, tests/harness-debug-port.test.ts, and
   tests/substring-pin-honesty.test.ts). Requirements, learned from the census work:
   * allowlist by intent, not by file: the durable-root fixture literal must stay legal, so the rule is
     "an absolute path passed to a READ/WRITE call", not "an absolute path in a string";
   * name the offending file, line and path in the failure message, and say which of the two fixes applies
     (commit the fixture / resolve from git history, or make the absence fail loudly);
   * prove it with a probe: plant a temporary absolute-path read, confirm the guard names it, remove the
     probe and keep the log. A net that is not itself proven is the same sin the substring class catches.
4. Decide the jxl fixtures and the bgagent Chrome path explicitly (fix, allowlist with a reason, or leave
   with a note) — do not let the new guard red them into an emergency allowlist.

ACCEPTANCE.
* The predecessor-digest test asserts its six assertions on a checkout where the author's worktree does not
  exist — demonstrated by running it after the fix and showing the digest-preservation and
  intentional-admission assertions actually execute (e.g. a temporary perturbation of one digest must fail
  the test; restore, re-hash, empty git status).
* A missing predecessor FAILS the test with a reason naming what could not be resolved.
* The static guard is green on the fixed tree, names all remaining absolute-path instances deliberately
  (fixed or allowlisted with a reason), and is probe-proven.
* Repo gates: `npm run build:production` BEFORE `npm run test:changed` in a fresh worktree (the store-map
  tests in this very file read the STORE dist.complete marker; a developer-only build leaves it stale and
  they fail with "marker indexed source authority is stale" — environment, not coverage), then `npm test`
  once before push. Post-commit re-run `npm run check:changelog` and
  `npm run test:file -- tests/changelog.test.ts` — the bump hook writes the changelog entry AFTER the gates.
* CAUTION: this file is in the SERIAL phase (it asserts the shipped CAS bytes and races with rebuilds), and
  a concurrent lane running Chrome KATs can red tests/security-suite-custody.test.ts through the
  machine-global /tmp/cap-serialized-chrome-acceptance.lock. That failure is NOT a kill; re-run at rest.
* Independent review by a different model; push an explicit SHA.

FOR THE CANON (coord: the fifth mode). The four already recorded: a substring satisfied by a comment
(PROSE-ONLY), a substring satisfied by an import binding whose call site is gone (IMPORT-ONLY), a pin whose
token is computed so it can never occur verbatim (INTERPOLATED), and a pin satisfied by a shadow while a
live occurrence exists elsewhere (DEFEATABLE). The fifth: CONDITIONAL DEATH — the assertions are reachable
only on the author's machine, so the test is green and empty everywhere else. Detection is cheap and does not
need mutation: time the test, count the assertions that can execute, and ask what the `.catch` is swallowing.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED, PROBES PROVEN, GATES GREEN — CANDIDATE f16c9b81 on cap-beads-ne8u (qwen, 01a07d6e, 2026-09-07). Committed locally, NOT pushed; needs an independent reviewer (different model). Base e72af3c3 (origin/main at branch time). Worktree /home/paulkinlan/worktrees/cap-ne8u, clean. Setup npm ci + deno install + build + build:production all rc=0.

FILES (12 in the commit, 5 authored + the standard 0.3.323 bump set):
* tests/bundled-tool-packages.test.ts (+81/-…) — the conditional-death block replaced.
* tests/fixtures/bundled-inventory-baseline.json (NEW, 222 lines) — the committed predecessor: 38 package digests, 38 CAS blob shas, takenAt e72af3c3 with its subject, and an empty intentionalReadmissions list. Its header records when to re-take it and why a rolling git walk was rejected.
* tests/fixtures/jxl/{small8,lossy-1mp}.jxl (NEW, 31 KB + 101 KB) and tests/jxl-admission.test.ts — the loud variant fixed by committing the fixtures and reading them repo-relative.
* tests/machine-path-honesty.test.ts (NEW, 254 lines) — the guard: no test may pass an absolute path under a USER HOME to a filesystem call, directly or through a const that reaches one. Scoped on the CALL, not the string, which is what keeps durable-root.test.ts's env fixture legal. One allowlist entry with a reason (bgagent-delete's documented Deno.stat probe for Chrome for Testing), keyed by path, plus a stale-entry check.

PART 1 LOUDNESS, as approved: the baseline's takenAt commit must exist in history (git cat-file -e) so an invented provenance fails; a baseline package must still ship; a digest may only change when declared with a reason >20 chars; a declaration whose digest still matches the baseline also fails, so the exception list cannot rot into a blanket waiver; every baseline CAS blob must still ship. Re-taking the baseline is required ONLY for a reviewed digest change — adding a package does not require it, which is what stops the fixture being regenerated blindly on every admission.

MEASUREMENT THAT CHANGED THE APPROVED SHAPE (recorded because it contradicts the bead's "predecessor from git history" read literally): a rolling walk is not viable. Over the last 300 commits touching extension/lib/bundled-inventory-data.js: 9 transitions changed a shared package's digest, 12 added packages, and 4 showed packages REMOVING and re-appearing through branch topology rather than any decision — 13 historical adjudications, several of them merge artifacts, and vacuous on a clean checkout. Separately, the bump hook rewrites that file's `release` field on EVERY commit, so "the parent of the last commit that touched it" differs only by that string: measured 38/38 packages identical at e72af3c3. Hence a committed baseline WITH git provenance (the sha is verified to exist, so it is still git-anchored and cannot be invented) instead of a runtime walk. Flagged to coord as a deviation from the literal wording with the measurement attached.

GUARD SCOPE ALSO MEASURED, not guessed: flagging EVERY absolute path produced four legitimate hits — a per-run /tmp/pv-fixture-${Date.now()} the test creates itself, the machine-global /tmp/cap-chrome-slot-POISON marker the custody suite deliberately shares, and "/bin/sleep" used to generate load. /tmp and /bin exist on every unix machine; a path under someone's home cannot exist anywhere else, which is the actual defect class. RESIDUAL LIMITATION stated in the file rather than hidden: a read of a hardcoded /tmp/fixture.json the test did not create would still slip through — catching that needs create-vs-expect dataflow, not worth the false positives.

PROBES (every net proven; all restored and sha256-verified):
1. perturb one digest in extension/lib/bundled-inventory-data.js -> FAILS "manifest digests changed without a declared intentional re-admission". The six unreachable assertions now have teeth. Product file restored to 611769fb9a973ff0e731e60b2d963961c0211da8368b4f49d6546340e248ac87.
2. set the baseline's takenAt to a nonexistent commit -> FAILS "the baseline's provenance commit deadbeef… does not exist in this history — re-take the baseline from a real commit instead of editing the fixture".
3. add a ghost package to the baseline -> FAILS "a package in the baseline no longer ships — a removal is an owner decision, not a regeneration side effect". Fixture restored and sha256-verified after each.
4. revert one jxl read to its absolute path -> the new guard FAILS naming "jxl-admission.test.ts:227 [direct] /home/…/small8.jxl". The guard catches the defect it was written for.
5. synthetic probes inside the guard cover both directions: literal read, const-to-fs-call, template-literal path (fire); env fixture value, file:// URL, new URL(..., import.meta.url), ${ROOT} idiom, a comment recording a past defect, and a const that never reaches a fs call (all legal).

TRAP HIT AND FIXED (second instance of the same trap today, worth the book): test-partition-guard.test.ts inherits the hazard class of every `tests/…` path a file merely MENTIONS (DRIVER_REF_RE reads and concatenates it), so naming a serial-phase file inside my allowlist key reddened the partition with "spawns build.mjs or the bundled-tool generator". Fixed by assembling every named path at runtime (tp("bgagent-delete.test.ts")) — the partition guard's own convention and the one c9y8 landed under — so NO exemption is taken and the partition stays strict for every other file.

GATES: rewritten predecessor test 1/0 in 2ms executing all six assertions · jxl-admission 7/0 · new guard 3/0 in 35ms · test-partition-guard 8/0 with it · npm run test:changed rc=0 (426 files) · npm test rc=0 (serial 15 files 154/0 in 84s, parallel 411 files 4022/0 in 29s, 426 files total, wall 113s) · post-commit npm run check:changelog "changelog in sync" and npm run test:file -- tests/changelog.test.ts 9/0 · bump 0.3.322 -> 0.3.323.

FOLLOW-UP LEFT OPEN ON PURPOSE, recorded in the allowlist entry: resolve the Chrome-for-Testing binary from the puppeteer cache glob (~/.cache/puppeteer/chrome/*) instead of pinning a version directory, then delete that entry. Not done here — it is a change to a test this bead does not otherwise touch, and mixing it in would muddy the review.

REVIEW SURFACE: `git diff e72af3c3..f16c9b81` minus the bump set. Cheapest falsifications: probe 1 (perturb a digest — one character in extension/lib/bundled-inventory-data.js) and probe 4 (revert one jxl read to an absolute path) each take seconds and kill a named assertion; the durable-root scoping question is the one to attack if you want to find over-reach, since that is the entry that decides whether this guard is a nuisance.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
FIXED & VERIFIED on cap-beads-7spn @ fb1e8cc0:

Root cause analysis:
1. ScreenshotStrip loading="lazy" deferred dimension computation: Unlike ScreenshotThumb which explicitly avoided loading="lazy" (due to being inside details elements) and used decoding="async", ScreenshotStrip used loading="lazy" on its thumbnail images. In headless Chrome, deferred lazy images retain naturalWidth=0 until scrolled, failing the post-reopen assertion '(stripInfo.natural ?? 0) > 0'. Replacing loading="lazy" with decoding="async" allows the in-memory data/blob URLs to decode immediately, producing naturalWidth=1200 / naturalHeight=813.
2. Double-subscription in ntp.js: When runThreadTurn executed runConversationTurn on threadConversation, subscribeRunRegistry simultaneously ran projectSurfaceRunTranscript which attached renderRunTranscript to the same conversation. Both listeners processed progress events, generating duplicate approval cards for the same permission pause. When the allow button was clicked, one card was granted while the sibling remained pending in the DOM, leaving pendingCount()=1 and causing subsequent tasks to be sent as steer messages to the un-settled turn rather than starting new runs. Added a guard in projectSurfaceRunTranscript to skip attaching renderRunTranscript if liveClientRunId is actively driving the open conversation.
3. Async ownerApprovalStore clearing race on SW boot: durableRecoveryReady.then() was calling clear() on ownerApprovalStore asynchronously after boot, racing incoming approval registrations and wiping pending approvals. Removed the redundant clear calls.
4. Inline approval resolution in wireReplayApprovals: Forwarded requestId through c.appendApproval to wireReplayApprovals so that inline approvals can be cleanly resolved via run.resolve-inline-approval.
5. Store bundle budget maintenance: Extracted shared parseStandardStreamArgs and applyToolResultToCard helpers, keeping the store SW bundle at 2,999,974 bytes (<= 3,000,000 bytes budget).

Evidence:
- Tests: 425 files total, 4,008 passed, 0 failed (npm run test:changed).
- Pin: tests/permission-approval-in-context.test.ts updated with 7spn regression tests.
