title: Load-sensitive Chrome gates need a quiet-window scheduler, not a lock (environmental-red class)
description:
Filed from chrome-agent-platform-uzik with the coordinator's approval: locking cannot fix machine load, and uzik proved the lock was never what excluded it.

PROBLEM
The journey gate (scripts/chrome-journeys.ts, 370 sequential CDP round-trips over minutes) fails environmentally under machine load. chrome-agent-platform-eo4d.1's own run history is the evidence: r1 reached 59/370 then died on 'cdp timeout: Runtime.evaluate' with machine load >7 from concurrent imageops/esbuild and Rust/Wasm compilation; r2 same; r3 reached 250/370 then the same transport timeout; r4 passed 370/370 only in an uninterrupted quiet window on a free canonical slot. The failure mode is a CDP transport timeout caused by CPU starvation of the browser or the harness, not a product defect — a red that says nothing about the tree, and it burns a whole gate run each time.

WHAT UZIK ALREADY DID (and why it is not enough)
uzik moved 98 harnesses off the machine-wide exclusive flock onto a bounded-concurrency semaphore (CAP_CHROME_MAX_CONCURRENT, default 4) and let the load-sensitive journey suite opt into exclusivity via launchChrome({canonicalLock:true}). Exclusivity excludes other CAP browsers. It does NOT exclude other lanes' esbuild/rustc/imageops, which is what actually killed eo4d.1 r1-r3. Concurrency also slightly increases total load. So the environmental-red class is still open.

ACCEPTANCE
1. A declared, checkable quiet-window mechanism for load-sensitive gates: before a run that opts in, the runner measures machine load (loadavg, and ideally the count of heavy compilers/build processes) and either waits for a quiet window (bounded, honest, printed) or refuses with an explicit 'environment: load too high' verdict that is NOT counted as a product red.
2. The wait/refusal is bounded and loud — same honesty rules as the browser gate: a run that cannot get a quiet window FAILS visibly as environmental, never silently skips and never turns green.
3. Load-sensitive gates declare themselves (harness registry field or launcher option) rather than being hardcoded in a runner; chrome-journeys.ts is the first declarant.

title: Beads pre-commit hook cds to the PRIMARY checkout from a linked worktree: dirties the shared checkout and stages its export into the worktree's commit
description:
Found during chrome-agent-platform-y6z6 (commit 5faced0b in the linked worktree ~/worktrees/cap-y6z6). .git/hooks/pre-commit (the beads export.auto hook) does `cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.."` before `bd export > .beads/issues.jsonl; git add .beads/issues.jsonl`. Hooks live in the COMMON git dir, so from a linked worktree $0 is ~/chrome-agent-platform/.git/hooks/pre-commit and the cd lands in the PRIMARY checkout — the shared checkout AGENTS.md says no session may dirty. Result: (1) the fresh export is written into the primary's working tree, which shows `M .beads/issues.jsonl` after every worktree commit and can block a merge in the primary that touches that file; (2) `git add`, running with the worktree's GIT_DIR but the primary's cwd, stages the primary's on-disk blob into the WORKTREE's index, so the worktree's own on-disk issues.jsonl is never refreshed and reads as modified against HEAD afterwards. The post-commit hook's `bd dolt push` block has the same cd (harmless there).

OBSERVED (y6z6): HEAD:.beads/issues.jsonl = 512 lines (fresh export, = bd info issue count); the worktree's on-disk copy = the untouched 481-line base blob from 5b128f12 (git status M, `git diff --quiet 5b128f12 -- .beads/issues.jsonl` identical); the primary showed `M .beads/issues.jsonl` with mtime at the commit instant and no session had edited it.

REPRO: in any linked worktree, change a bead (bd create/update), commit, then `git status` in the worktree AND in ~/chrome-agent-platform.

ACCEPTANCE: a commit made in a linked worktree exports into and stages from THAT worktree (git already runs hooks at the worktree root — drop the cd, or `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"`), leaves the primary checkout untouched, and the worktree's on-disk issues.jsonl equals HEAD after the commit. If beads regenerates .git/hooks from its own template, the fix goes into the bd hook config/template and the install step is documented in AGENTS.md next to the post-commit instructions; a reference copy lands in scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit. Out of y6z6's lane — filed, not fixed.

title: Installable JavaScript modules in the script sandbox (split from 4p7j)
description:
Split out of chrome-agent-platform-4p7j by owner decision (Paul, 2026-09-06): 'JS modules: split out to a separate bead, yes.' Analysis §8 of /home/paulkinlan/cap-evidence/claude/4p7j-analysis.md is the design sketch.

WHY SEPARATE: the Python side has a PAYLOAD problem (no wheels ship; the loaders exist). The JS side has a RESOLUTION problem (the substrate exists; module identity does not). Mixing them produces a design that serves neither.

THE SUBSTRATE ALREADY EXISTS: extension/sandbox/script-sandbox.html is declared in the manifest sandbox key — an opaque origin, no chrome.*, no same-origin, no storage, and a CSP permitting the eval a normal extension page forbids. Agent scripts already run there with a HOST-BRIDGED fetch (the host performs the request, URL-validated). script-sandbox.js even redefines storage APIs so a script reaching for localStorage gets an error that TEACHES rather than failing mutely.

Worth noting because it inverts the intuition: the JS lane already has the isolation the Python lane lacked — its network is mediated by the host rather than ambient. Python is only now getting the equivalent (4p7j S0/S0.5).

SO THE WORK IS module resolution inside that sandbox: ESM import from blob: URLs built out of stored module text, with an import map naming the installed set. The CSP already carries frame-src 'self' about: blob: data:.

ACCEPTANCE: an owner-installed JS module is importable by name from an agent-generated script in the sandbox, persists across runs, is listed and removable in Settings, and the host-bridged fetch boundary is unchanged — a module must not widen what a script can reach.
DEPENDS ON: the shared owner-blob store (chrome-agent-platform-9ux7.1 / CAP-FB-20260905-USER-WASM-STORE-01) — wheels, Wasm modules and JS modules are all owner-supplied blobs with owner-written metadata and should share ONE store rather than three.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
2026-09-05 DESIGN v1 (cap-wasm-catalogue lane, implementing).

ABI SURVEY (measured): hash-wasm@4.12.0 modules export a purpose-built embedding ABI: memory + Hash_GetBuffer/Hash_Init/Hash_Update/Hash_Final/Hash_GetState/Hash_Calculate + STATE_SIZE global — a pure-wasm harness needs NO package JS. awasm-noble's modules export only raw primitives (compressParents/processBlocks/reset) — the friendly API lives in its JS glue; pure-wasm harnessing those means reimplementing the driver loop (deferred). PILOT: hash-wasm blake3.

DESIGN:
- Manifest: executables[] gains an OPTIONAL callExport member (reviewed authority change, exactKeys extended): { entry: 'Hash_Calculate', inputBuffer: 'Hash_GetBuffer', digestBytes: 32 } — declaring the ABI. auditWasmBinary extends: verify ZERO imports, memory32, declared memory max, and that the declared exports EXIST with function kind.
- Harness (CAP-authored, no package JS ever runs): offscreen worker (same singleton as the stream host): instantiate the CAS bytes, inputBuffer() for the input pointer, write the (base64-decoded) input, entry(ptr, len), read digestBytes from the state pointer, return hex/base64. Bounded: wall deadline, worker terminate, exact-key envelopes, authority fences identical to the stream lane (owner/run refs, sealed OPFS in/out where large).
- Tool surface: one toolId per algorithm ('hash_blake3' pilot): args { data: base64 } -> { hash: hex }. Dispatch: SW route beside dispatchBundledWasmStream -> offscreen call-export host.
- Admission pipeline: the package's .wasm lands in CAS by extracting the base64 blob from the npm tarball at evidence-build time (extract script committed; tarball sha512 + blob offset pinned; CAS sha256 pinned; reproducibility = re-extraction byte-equality, NOT a rebuild).

EXPLICITLY NOT v1: awasm-noble (raw-primitive ABI), streaming Hash_Init/Update (one-shot Calculate only), threads/SAB, any package JS execution (that would be a policy change — running reviewed JS in an extension worker — and needs Paul separately).

FALSIFICATION: (1) admission rejects a module with ANY import (RED->GREEN by adding a dummy import to a fixture module); (2) admission rejects a manifest declaring a non-existent export; (3) a tampered CAS byte fails the pin; (4) the pilot tool hashes a known vector live in the loaded extension.

title: [CAP-FB-20260905-EMSCRIPTEN-LINK-01] Fence eager Emscripten side-module linking to the admitted graph
description:
Intent: support necessary native side modules without letting dlopen turn data/paths into executable authority. Requires A0 compiler proof, A1 schema and A2 host (transitive dependencies). If no-eval side linking is unsupported, leave this stage blocked rather than building a custom linker or weakening CSP.

Reuse the pinned Emscripten linker, supplying a CAP closed-world asset/symbol resolver. One main owns job memory/table; side modules belong to one admitted ABI/graph. Verify all chosen executable bytes before running constructors. Parse dylink.0 dependencies/static memory/table sizes/alignments and check arithmetic/fit; bind GOT.mem/GOT.func, tags, TLS and exports by type/mutability/provider. No cross-job symbols, wildcard host implementation, unresolved-required-symbol success or dummy import. Preserve linker semantics when normalizing duplicate needed IDs (vips repeats all three dependencies).

Initial profile is eager-only, before threads/application readiness. Exact logical asset name resolves only to verified package bytes; reject remote/absolute/traversal/query substitutions, missing library, uploaded same-named Wasm and code read from user FS. locateFile alone is insufficient: audit sync XHR, readBinary, preloads and loader FS paths. Caller cannot set dynamicLibraries. Late dlopen/dlsym is unsupported until separately proven with epoch/link-table coordination.

Shared side imports' maximum 65,536 pages is not a per-library 4GiB allocation; check actual Wasm import type compatibility against the owning memory. Core vips min=max16,384 requires 1GiB for that graph. Tables without maxima require a finite supported allocation strategy/rebuild; no silent unbounded resource assumption.

Acceptance: real loaded main+side computation and constructors, exact positive result, wrong digest/ABI/kind/tag/symbol/memory bound and FS-shadow injection all RED before execution. Busy constructor terminates under host deadline. Dynamic-JS side fixture must fail, not fetch/eval/fallback. Static linking with new bytes may deliver a reduced image package but is not completion of this side-link stage. Threaded-link integration is gated again in A6 after A5.
acceptance_criteria: Real no-eval main+side output and fail-closed dependency/symbol/path/constructor checks. No caller-supplied code or resolver escape; baseline WASI unaffected. Build, focused/changed tests, npm test once before coordinator push, loaded browser evidence and independent different-model review.

title: [CAP-FB-20260905-EMSCRIPTEN-THREADS-01] Own pthread worker groups and measure shared-memory admission classes
description:
Intent: add real pthread computation with a group the responsive offscreen host can terminate while any native thread is stuck. A0-A2 supply compiler, typed memory policy and host. Work on a non-dynamic-link threaded fixture can proceed alongside A4; combined side-link/thread acceptance belongs to A6.

Prefer host-owned prewarmed worker handles and a narrowly reviewed Worker-compatible MessagePort facade in pinned glue. Prove transport against the chosen compiler; never assume a caller-supplied worker hook exists. A nested-worker design is acceptable only with actual evidence that root termination stops all descendants. Root.terminate alone is not group evidence. No Atomics.wait on the offscreen document; prewarm before any native synchronous join; admission-bound finite pool and hard exhaustion (PTHREAD_POOL_SIZE_STRICT=2 where supported), not hardwareConcurrency/unbounded late spawn. Bootstrap paths are fixed packaged assets; no Blob or request URLs.

CAP already configures COOP same-origin and COEP credentialless. Probe crossOriginIsolated, real shared memory and atomic handoff in actual offscreen/root/pthread contexts under shipped manifest/Chrome. Missing SAB/feature returns unsupported; a true single-thread fallback is a separate built graph, not no-op pthread emulation.

Keep WASI 32/128/256MiB tiers unchanged. Introduce explicit Emscripten shared classes, including fixed-1024 only if tested; stock vips needs fixed 1GiB, not a runtime INITIAL_MEMORY override. Count shared linear memory once per group plus worker/runtime/stack/JS/MEMFS overhead; report measured logical vs resident memory separately. Finite concurrent group scheduler, no cross-job mutable pools, clean OOM and no data truncation.

Host owns deadline/revocation. Invalidate epoch, terminate every root/helper, close staging/handles and delete heap/group references. Verify helper targets/heartbeats stop, later messages cannot publish, and next-job canaries are clean; do not promise immediate browser RSS reclamation. Test infinite root and pthread loops, startup pool exhaustion, unsupported isolation, cancellation and restart. This stage does not itself admit vips or prove threaded late dlopen.
acceptance_criteria: Real cross-worker atomic computation; all helpers stop on cancel/deadline even with stuck native root/helper; no offscreen event-loop deadlock or cross-job heap leakage. Exact-build shared-memory workload/pressure evidence for every enabled class; fixed1GiB otherwise remains unadmitted. Build/focused/changed/full-once gates, loaded Chrome evidence and different-model review before coordinator push.

title: [CAP-FB-20260905-EMSCRIPTEN-VIPS-01] Admit a confined source-rebuilt vips image tool with verified codecs
description:

The packaged npm artifact is a useful baseline only: core min=max1GiB shared, env/GOT imports, dynamic-code and Emval bridge are outstanding incompatibilities. title: [CAP-FB-20260905-EMSCRIPTEN-HOST-01] Add the single-thread offscreen runtime and authenticated tool dispatch
description:
Intent: execute the admitted ABI in a fresh worker using the existing offscreen document, not a new generic JS or npm loader. Requires typed graph admission.

Seams: extension/offscreen/offscreen.js, existing document creation/claims, extension/lib/wasm-stream-host.js sender checks/lifecycle patterns, wasm-executor.js exact settlement and identities, service-worker tool dispatch, tool-exec-preview.js and Settings managed tools. Broker selects runtime/adapter/operation/graph and authorizes current run and package capability. Exact cap:emscripten-run envelope carries only identity, scalar validated arguments and opaque file references. Reject caller-provided Module, hooks, JS, asset URLs, export names, locateFile, dynamicLibraries or memory/pool settings. Authenticate the real SW URL/id and reject tab/document senders even if extension id matches. Literal local imports rely on immutable installed package inventory; fetch-then-import in an unpacked tree is not an atomic integrity boundary.

No worker pool/module/heap/FS reuse, no main-thread fallback, no arbitrary JS globals exposed through native imports. Explicit unsupported error for unknown ABI/feature. title: [CAP-FB-20260905-EMSCRIPTEN-CUSTODY-01] Connect job-scoped files, fail-closed audit and sealed output publication
description:
Intent: complete user-visible single-thread execution with the same input ownership, output custody and live-run safeguards as managed WASI. This stage is a release prerequisite even when the raw Emscripten operation already works.

Seams: wasm-stream-files.js, wasm-stream-run-lifecycle.js, tool-stream-platform.js and current service-worker/durable-run authority, new host/adapter from A2. Start with private per-job MEMFS/stdio where supported; file-backed random access requires a reviewed synchronous-compatible handle backend. Inputs read-only; code/data mounts separate from user input/output; reject traversal, symlink escape and uploaded-code shadowing. This stage can enable a proven small single-thread package without waiting for vips/pthreads.

title: [CAP-FB-20260905-EMSCRIPTEN-ABI-01] Prove a pinned no-eval native ABI without ambient JS authority
description:

Screenshots/recording and native output values must correspond to the pinned build, not a dev-page substitute. No generic runtime-compatibility claim for unmeasured libraries.

title: [CAP-FB-20260905-EMSCRIPTEN-RUNTIME-01] Emscripten module runtime with reviewed glue, closed linking and killable pthreads
description:
Intent: deliver a second managed-Wasm execution runtime for admitted Emscripten libraries without changing the existing WASI security boundary. Paul/coordinator direction is Option B's CAP-authored WASI image tool first (e5o8), then this runtime. Design/static evidence can proceed now. Extend this existing epic; it remains under qazo and is not a duplicate catalogue/import system.

Measured baseline: wasm-vips 0.0.18 core vips.wasm is 5,084,535 bytes, SHA256 7ca144fb2db374b456059ca3891b762e19f713f6d230747a9f97953ebeb9bbfb. Imports: env89 + wasi_snapshot_preview1 10 + GOT.func1 (100 entries, 98 functions; env89 includes memory). Imported shared memory has min=max=16,384 pages = fixed 1 GiB. Three side modules require env/GOT, shared memory, function tables and dylink.0; the full four-Wasm graph is 11,895,030 bytes. The 4,614,586-byte figure is the compressed npm tarball, not core Wasm. Shipped ES6 glue contains two new Function and two eval sites, and imported Emval bridges can reach globalThis/Module properties. No Wasm instance or package JS has been executed for this design.

Design: new closed schema-2 emscripten-module-v1 runtime under the existing bundled lane. Bind JS adapter/glue/bootstrap, all Wasm/side modules and operation schemas into one inventory-verified graph. Do NOT widen BUNDLED_ALLOWED_IMPORT_MODULES or relax schema-1 memory/import rules. Import authority is symbol+kind+type+implementation, not an env wildcard. Trusted bundled glue is part of CAP's TCB; owner-uploaded glue is excluded, and a worker alone does not sandbox arbitrary JS. No eval/new Function, CSP widening, executable URL loading, Blob-script or main-thread fallback. Remove or strictly confine ambient Emval/JS bridges; prefer a thin native wrapper over unrestricted bindings.

Reuse the current singleton offscreen host, SW-only sender checks, registry/CAS/WAL/revocation, sealed stream/artifact custody and durable run authority. New operation-specific adapter registry selects literal local factories; callers never submit Module hooks or code paths. Fresh workers/FS/heap per job; fail-closed intent/final audit, host-owned deadline/cancel, live authority recheck before output publication, no stale outputs after revoke/restart.

Stages: A0 compiler/no-eval ABI proof; A1 typed manifest/graph admission; A2 single-thread offscreen host and real dispatch; A3 file/output custody and durable lifecycle; A4 closed eager side-module linker; A5 killable pthread WorkerGroup and shared-memory classes; A6 rebuilt vips admission/integrated linking+pthreads; A7 individually measured catalogue rollout. Explicit blocks edges, not title numbers, establish order. First implementation stage is blocked by e5o8 per Option-B-first direction; simpler packages need not wait for high-memory vips.

Memory: retain WASI tiny/default/large = 32/128/256 MiB. Upstream vips cannot fit by changing INITIAL_MEMORY at runtime. A separate shared-fixed-1024 class remains unadmitted pending exact-build loaded Chrome allocation/workload/pressure/cancel evidence; smaller variants require new native builds/digests. CAP already has COOP same-origin + COEP credentialless: test actual offscreen/root/pthread isolation, not just manifest strings. All helper workers must be host-owned or independently proven to die with the parent.

No-eval linking is an explicit uncertainty: Emscripten 6.0.0 settings comments call RELOCATABLE/dlopen unavailable, while the pinned linker uses makeEval abort sites for embedded side-module JS. Build and execute fixtures to resolve the combined configuration. If needed dynamic linking fails, keep that stage blocked; a new static-link codec variant is not evidence that side linking works.

Evidence/design: /home/paulkinlan/cap-evidence/astra/EMSCRIPTEN-RUNTIME-DESIGN.md; artifact pins, compile-only inspection, glue snippets and upstream source pins are beside it. CAP source baseline 35ad5264f1c8b3d7c261fb358a2dbf89d27e5741, clean worktree cap-astra-option-a-20260905. Design is a proposal, not admission or runtime success. Keep provenance/signature claims honest: current authority validates release inventory but signer verification is not implemented. Every native/package dependency and generated post-bundle code asset needs pinned provenance and recorded license notices; no private infrastructure snapshots in public evidence.

Real pthread/side-module work and full group termination are proven for enabled profiles. Rebuilt vips is admitted only after no-eval/ambient-bridge/memory gates pass. 2026-09-05 DESIGN (cap-wasm-catalogue lane) — empirical blocker found, options below.

EVIDENCE (npm wasm-vips@0.0.18, tarball sha512-AJyCvxZj/3qceKNnh+YyEobu/IaJFoPN7x7SxyyHmYBS3kASMqJqxQEuN0ZHKQDWsCJ8armfx4Tq3uKrNc+nMA==, registry.npmjs.org/wasm-vips/-/wasm-vips-0.0.18.tgz):

Imports: env x89 (Emscripten runtime) + wasi_snapshot_preview1 x10 (fd_close/fd_write/fd_read/fd_seek/fd_fdstat_get/random_get/clock_time_get/proc_exit/environ_get/environ_sizes_get) + GOT.func x1 (DYNAMIC LINKING). sha256 7ca144fb... (full pin at admission if pursued).
- vips-heif.wasm (3.48MB), vips-jxl.wasm (2.17MB), vips-resvg.wasm (1.16MB) are Emscripten SIDE MODULES (env x134-252 + GOT.mem/GOT.func) — the package needs a dynamic linker.
- vips.js glue references SharedArrayBuffer/pthread (6 sites) — threaded build.

BLOCKER: the bundled admission authority admits ONLY imports.allowed=[wasi_snapshot_preview1] (wasm-package-authority.js:37 BUNDLED_ALLOWED_IMPORT_MODULES) and the execution worker is a WASI preview1 runtime (wasm-execution-worker.js:22). wasm-vips's env x89 + GOT dynamic linking + pthread/SAB cannot pass the authority or run in that host. Admitting it as-is is INFEASIBLE without a new runtime class.

OPTIONS:
A. New 'emscripten-module' package/runtime class: execute the vips.js glue + side-module linking + pthread emulation inside the offscreen module worker. Large: a second wasm host architecture, new manifest semantics, COOP/COEP question for SAB. Its own epic, not this bead.
B. (RECOMMENDED) CAP-authored WASI image tool — the csvtool clean-room precedent (packages/bundled/evidence/csvtool): a small Rust CLI wrapper over the pure-Rust  crate compiled to wasm32-wasi: vips-class basics (info/resize/convert/re-encode jpeg/png/webp) via stdin→stdout. Fits the admission pipeline TODAY (deterministic cargo build, wasi imports only, memory32, reviewable evidence tree). Delivers Paul's actual need (image analysis/compression/resizing) inside the shipped trust model.
C. Route wasm-vips through the OWNER-SELECTED package path (bead tzc) instead of the bundled channel — the owner installs it explicitly; the bundled-reviewed-only policy stays untouched.

comments.text:
# Docs audit — 2026-09-05 (lane cap-arch-docs, bead chrome-agent-platform-5zl6, umbrella 9zw7)

**Audited tree:** `origin/main@14e2a817` (2026-09-05). Claims were verified against the code at
the tip via `git show origin/main:<path>` — not against the local checkout (which sits 10 commits
behind at `75364f28`). Read-only analysis; no product or doc files were modified.

**Scope:** `README.md`, `PRODUCT.md`, `PLAN.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, root trackers, and `docs/*.md`
(incl. `docs/plans/`, `docs/admissions/` presence, `docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md`,
`extension/background/routes/ROUTE_MAP.md`). `docs/admissions/*` and `docs/plans/rust-lane/*`
per-lane records (42 + 59 tracked files) were spot-checked for presence only — they are declared
per-lane authorities for still-open candidate work, so their internal state is owned by those lanes.

Every finding cites file:line at `origin/main`. Severities: **H** = actively misleads a reader
about the current product/process; **M** = stale but recognizably dated; **L** = cosmetic.

---

## A. Retired trackers still presented as the live authority (H)

The 2026-09-02 owner directive (AGENTS.md, "Task tracking: beads only") retired TASKS.md,
TASKS-DONE.md, KNOWN-ISSUES.md and docs/UI-FIXES-TRACKER.md. Both retired root files now carry a
correct RETIRED banner (TASKS.md:1-9, KNOWN-ISSUES.md:1-5). But the docs that point at them were
never updated:

1. **README.md:243** — the document map declares TASKS.md "**Task state, and the only authority
   for it.** … The entry always wins over any summary of it." Directly contradicts the beads-only
   rule; a new reader is sent to a frozen file.
2. **README.md:246** — KNOWN-ISSUES.md described as "Gate state and the few open findings… A thin
   view over TASKS.md". Retired.
3. **README.md:247-248** — docs/UI-FIXES-TRACKER.md and TASKS-DONE.md listed as live map entries
   with no retirement note.
4. **PLAN.md:41** — "Task state lives in TASKS.md (the authority)".
5. **PLAN.md:48** — "TASKS.md is the task authority".
6. **PLAN.md:76** — "archived to TASKS-DONE.md, so TASKS.md holds only live work".
7. **PLAN.md:229** — "The authority is the **Open work queue** table in TASKS.md (39 open)."
   (39 open is doubly stale: the file is retired, and live state is `bd ready`.)
8. **docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md:3** — the whole file is a redirect to root KNOWN-ISSUES.md, i.e. a
   signpost to a retired file. Should point at beads.
9. **docs/KNOWN-ISSUES-ARCHIVE.md:5, 9, 60, 117, 135** — repeatedly tells readers live findings
   "live in TASKS.md" / to look up CAP-FB ids in TASKS.md. The archive itself may stay, but its
   pointers are dead ends.
10. **docs/AGENT-MODEL.md:81** (status section) — "Residual: … tracked in KNOWN-ISSUES."
11. **docs/UI-FIXES-TRACKER.md:28** — references TASKS.md as the evidence authority. (The tracker
    itself is a legacy view per AGENTS.md; keeping it as history is fine, pointing from it at
    another retired file is not.)

## B. Stale quantitative claims (H — several are in the README a newcomer reads first)

Ground truth measured at `origin/main@14e2a817`:

| Claim | Docs say | Code says | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Browser tool count | README.md:56 "**125 Chrome tools**"; README.md:107 "the browser-tool count is 126"; PLAN.md:31 "**126**"; PRODUCT.md:196-198 "flat list of 126" | **138** browser tools (+ 3 developer-only cookie tools), 50 management, 188 capability rows | tests/chrome-tool-capabilities.test.ts:60-72 (`CHROME_TOOL_CAPABILITY_TABLE.length === 188`, 138 chrome-api, 50 management, `CHROME_TOOL_CAPABILITY_BOUNDS {browserTools:138, managementTools:50, totalTools:188}`); extension/lib/browser-tools.js has 138 `tool({` definitions |
| Capability table size | PLAN.md:32-33 "dropped to 155 … regrown to 160"; docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md:35,44 "159 → 155", "167 → 166" | **188** | same test as above |
| Bundled Wasm tools | README.md:70 "**28 bundled Wasm tools**"; PLAN.md:170 "**28 bundled Wasm packages ship**" | **31** admitted (sed, awk, jq joined the 28) | packages/bundled/README.md:1-3 ("31-tool execution tranche") listing all 31 admitted descriptors |
| Lazy provider definitions | README.md:62-63 "every run receives **exactly two definitions**, `search_tools` and `execute_tool`" | **Three**: `search_tools`, `list_tools`, `execute_tool` | extension/lib/lazy-tool-protocol.js:1464, 1478, 1491 (the three `tool({…})` definitions) |
| Unit tests | README.md:253 "**1779/0**"; PLAN.md:11 "**1779 pass / 0 fail**" | stale (2457 pass at the 2026-08-30 reanalysis; higher today) | REVIEW-2026-08-30.md; the number moves daily — the honest fix is to stop hardcoding it (see fix plan) |
| Chrome journeys | README.md:253 "**127/127**"; PLAN.md:12 "**127/127**" | stale (138/138 at 2026-08-30; current count differs) | REVIEW-2026-08-30.md |
| Chrome-lazy metadata counts | docs/tool-platform-architecture.md (§"Source-only Chrome lazy capability metadata") "the exact **nine** `browserToolset(false)` and **29** `managementToolset` names", "all 38 descriptors" | 138 + 50 | tests/chrome-tool-capabilities.test.ts:67-69 |

Note README.md is internally inconsistent (125 vs 126 in the same file) in addition to both being
stale.

## C. References to deleted surfaces/directories (M)

`extension/chat/` and `extension/memory/` no longer exist at tip (deleted; verified via
`git ls-tree origin/main extension/`). `extension/recipes/` is also gone (though
`extension/lib/recipes.js` still exists — the recipes→skills rename is an open P3, bead
chrome-agent-platform-l0r). Stale references:

12. **README.md:194** — the architecture tree lists `chat/` ("the conversation surface").
13. **PLAN.md:86** — "Landed and shipping" includes "NTP hub, side panel, **chat**, directory,
    **memory explorer**, options".
14. **PRODUCT.md:66-67** — "Twelve HTML surfaces ship; two of them — `chat/chat.html` and
    `memory/explorer.html` — are referenced by nothing at all and still ship to users." Both files
    were subsequently deleted (the "Subtract surfaces" action happened): **10** HTML files ship now
    (verified: artifact, artifacts, directory, ntp, offscreen, options, privacy, sandbox×2,
    sidepanel). The paragraph should record the deletion, not the dead weight.
15. **docs/CONSTITUTION.md** (§1 XSS bullet) — "chat/directory/memory render untrusted data with
    textContent/escaping" — two of the three named surfaces are gone.
16. **docs/UX-AUDIT-2026-08-28.md:73** — evidence row cites the `chat` surface (360px overflow).
    Point-in-time audit; acceptable as history, but any "still true" reading of it is broken.

## D. Stale status headers on design/plan docs (M)

17. **docs/tool-platform-architecture.md** — the worst offender for the architecture story:
    - Status line: "live bounded lazy-provider cutover is a **0.2.180 release candidate** … fresh
      browser acceptance plus independent release review remain pending." The cutover shipped long
      ago (tip is 0.3.229; PLAN.md describes the lazy provider as landed and shipping).
    - §"Live bounded lazy protocol": "bundled Wasm rows are **always projected as disabled
      catalog-only metadata. They receive no selection reference, validator, authorization
      callback, or provider dispatch closure**" — contradicted by
      extension/background/service-worker.js:1430 (`executableBundledToolRecords(…)` folded into
      every run's records with `closureGeneration: "task-execution-core"`) and by
      docs/UNIX-TOOLS-ADMISSION.md:5-9 ("available through the ordinary `search_tools` →
      `execute_tool` path"). packages/bundled/README.md:10 ("Model calls use the lazy selection
      authority and live run fence") agrees with the code. The doc is the odd one out.
    - Repeated "source-only / unreachable / no product file imports this" claims for the OPFS
      workspace, WASI execution host, and package authority slices — all three now have shipped
      execution paths (extension/lib/wasm-executor.js, wasm-offscreen-host.js, wasm-stream-*.js,
      opfs-tool-workspace.js consumed by the live pipeline).
    - §"Planned authority split" items 1-4 are described as future; all are landed.
18. **docs/AGENT-EXECUTION-ARCHITECTURE.md** —
    - Header says "Phases 1–4 all implemented and shipped" but §6 still reads "Phase 2 — move the
      agent-do run loop into the worker (**NEXT**)" (and Phases 3/4 as forward-looking). Internal
      contradiction.
    - §7: "The `chrome.offscreen` API requires no manifest permission — confirmed by this
      codebase… works with `permissions: []` and no `offscreen` entry." The manifest at tip
      declares `offscreen` as one of the four **required** install permissions
      (extension/manifest.json `permissions: ["alarms","offscreen","sidePanel","storage"]`).
      Either the doc's claim was wrong or the posture changed; as written it misinforms.
19. **docs/AGENT-DELEGATION.md:2** — "Status: implemented (**candidate on branch
    `cap-agent-delegation`**)." Delegation is merged: extension/lib/agent-delegation.js and
    `delegate_to_agent` (extension/lib/chrome-tool-capabilities.js:205) are on main.
20. **docs/THREAD-LOADING-REDESIGN.md:3** — "Status: DESIGN, awaiting owner review. **Nothing
    here is implemented.**" The thread-open work landed (`0.2.314`/`0.2.317`, PLAN.md:152-156:
    per-execution ordered log index + cursor pagination).
21. **PLAN.md:189-192** — "Python via Pyodide … The remaining step is the Pyodide runtime
    **binary**, a blocked Emscripten build." Pyodide shipped: official 0.26.4 core admitted and
    wired (extension/background/service-worker.js:9910 `setPythonRuntimeProvider(...)`;
    extension/lib/python-runtime.js:46-51 pins the SHA-256 of every runtime file; CHANGELOG
    0.3.127-0.3.130, 0.3.137). docs/PYODIDE-BOUNDED-BUILD.md carries the correct status note —
    PLAN.md never got it. (Same staleness in python-tool.js:9-10 header comment "Until the runtime
    is admitted, `pythonTool` fails closed" — code comment, not a doc, noted for completeness.)
22. **docs/CONSTITUTION.md** — the closing "**The current gate state** — 2026-08-15: independent
    review REJECTED the build twice … Re-review in flight." A three-week-old transient state
    presented as current, and it references the retired independent-review loop (see E-25).

## E. Process/terminology drift (M/L)

23. **README.md:115** — "The review loop (**sol / GLM / DeepSeek, independent sessions**) reviews
    every change." That fleet was retired 2026-08-27 (AGENTS.md "Review without a second model").
    The README promises a control that does not exist.
24. **README.md** doc map (lines ~241-251) omits **REVIEW-2026-08-30.md** — the current reanalysis
    that AGENTS.md ("The current review (2026-08-30) — read before picking up work") calls the
    required entry point — while listing the superseded REVIEW-2026-08-21.md.
25. **Chaos references (AGENTS.md hard rule: "No chaos references"):**
    - README.md:43 — "the chaos skill-loader pattern".
    - docs/HOOKS.md (catalog intro) — "The reference implementation (**the chaos extension**) wires
      11 of these…".
    - docs/usage-precedent-review.md — title and body: "precedent review (**CHAOS**)", "CHAOS
      contracts (present, read-only)" (multiple).
26. **Recipes terminology** — "recipes" persists in user-facing-adjacent docs where the rename is
    presented as done: docs/AGENT-PRODUCT-GAPS.md:41,45,72,93,110,118; docs/HOOKS.md (subscription
    model: "the recipe's prompt", "Background recipes subscribe"); docs/agent-deletion-lifecycle-
    design.md:18,22,142; docs/SYSTEM-PROMPTS.md (scopes: "recipe runs"). Caveat:
    `extension/lib/recipes.js` still exists and the rename completion is open (bead
    chrome-agent-platform-l0r), so these are partly *accurate*; the finding is that docs mix
    "skills" and "recipes" without telling the reader the rename is half-landed. docs/PRODUCT.md:95
    says "the files followed the UI where it was safe (`extension/recipes/` is gone)" — true for
    the directory, not the lib.
27. **docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md** — Q12 carries "**ANSWERED (2026-09-01)**" but remains in the "Open"
    section; PLAN.md:247 still lists Q12 among "Genuinely open". One of the two is wrong.
28. **docs/UX-AUDIT-2026-08-28.md, docs/MODEL-PRICE-AUDIT-2026-09-02.md,
    docs/inline-approval-audit.md, docs/SETTINGS-CLEANLINESS.md** — dated point-in-time audits with
    no "superseded/landed" status line. Not wrong, but indistinguishable from live docs. A one-line
    status header on each would fix the class.

## F. ROUTE_MAP.md drift (M)

29. **extension/background/routes/ROUTE_MAP.md** — titled "Slice 1"; its inventory lists only the
    kv / perm-lease / provider / activity / memory / fs-grant / agent-workspace modules and states
    "*All other routes (114)* — extension/background/service-worker.js (inline). To be modularized
    in subsequent slices." At tip the routes directory has **13 modules** — auth, mcp, scheduler,
    agent-schedule, agent-worker (and index) are unlisted — so both the inventory and the "(114)"
    count are stale. (Verified: git ls-tree origin/main extension/background/routes/.)

## G. Missing documentation (H for the architecture stage)

No doc exists at all for these shipped subsystems (the stage-2 ARCHITECTURE.md will cover them;
recording as gaps a reader hits today):

30. **A system-level architecture map.** The architecture is scattered across README's 12-line
    tree block + ~10 feature design docs, several of them stale (finding 17). Nothing answers
    "what are the processes, who holds authority, how do they talk" at current main.
31. **OPFS / memory architecture.** Origin-keyed stores, the one-OPFS-root-per-origin platform
    constraint and the isolation gymnastics around it, per-store bounds (8 MiB store / 256 KiB
    value / 64 MiB tree — cited only inside DURABLE-RUN-ARCHITECTURE.md), artifact custody, agent
    private workspaces — no home. AGENTS.md's "Agent private workspaces" section is the only
    workspace doc.
32. **The shipped Wasm execution path.** 13 `wasm-*`/`wasi-*` modules, the offscreen host, the
    stream host — tool-platform-architecture.md documents the pre-execution "source-only" slices
    and explicitly disclaims the execution path; UNIX-TOOLS-ADMISSION.md covers the admission
    profile. Nothing documents the runtime as shipped.
33. **Table/spreadsheet tools.** Seven `table-*.js` modules (core, formula, join-pivot,
    operation-worker, runtime, worker-host, tabular-diff) with no design doc.
34. **Messaging/route surface as a whole.** ROUTE_MAP.md covers a slice (and a stale one — F-29);
    the agent-worker protocol is documented (AGENT-WORKER-DURABILITY.md §5) but the overall
    routing/principal model lives only in code + ROUTE_MAP's three-paragraph preamble.
35. **Python execution as shipped.** PYODIDE-BOUNDED-BUILD.md is a build spec with a corrective
    status note; the shipped dispatcher (python-host.js, fresh classic worker per run, offscreen
    transport) has no architecture doc.

## H. Verified-current docs (no action)

Checked and found accurate/current: docs/CONSTITUTION.md (except findings 15, 22),
docs/SYSTEM-PROMPTS.md, docs/MCP-SUPPORT-DESIGN.md (includes its landed spike + injection
results), docs/PERMISSION-MATRIX.md, docs/AGENT-WORKER-DURABILITY.md, docs/AGENT-WORKER-PHASE4.md
(honestly records the client + lease removals), docs/PYODIDE-BOUNDED-BUILD.md (self-correcting
status note; minor: §5's "runtime lives in OPFS, not the bundle" line wasn't individually marked
superseded), docs/LOCAL-MODELS-ARCHITECTURE.md (honest removal log), docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md
(current except finding 27), docs/DURABLE-RUN-ARCHITECTURE.md (but see finding 36),
docs/durable-background-runs-design.md (explicitly marked HISTORICAL), docs/TOOL-PURPOSE-GROUPS.md,
docs/UNIX-TOOLS-ADMISSION.md, docs/wasm-tool-catalogue.md (all three new at tip).

36. **docs/DURABLE-RUN-ARCHITECTURE.md — mixed citation currency (M).** The header binds every
    citation to commit `dd41258f` / release 0.2.113 ("Source citations below resolve against
    `dd41258f`"), but the body has been updated with post-0.2.113 content (RUN_RETENTION_POLICY
    `run-retention-v2`, `perThread` 50 from CAP-FB-20260901-THREAD-RELOAD-FIDELITY-01,
    `compactExecution`). A reader cannot tell which line citations resolve at tip and which only
    at dd41258f. Either re-pin the header or split "snapshot evidence" from "living reference".

## I. Local (non-repo) observation for stage 6

37. `docs/.build/` — 309 MB of untracked Rust build residue (tokei target dir) on local disk. Not
    git-tracked (verified: `git ls-files docs/.build` is empty), so not a repo defect — but a
    cleanup candidate for the stage-6 inventory and possibly a `.gitignore` check.

---

## Fix plan (prioritized; each lands through the normal review flow — main is frozen)

**P1 — truth about process (cheap, high-traffic):**
1. README.md doc map + PLAN.md authority lines: point task/bug state at beads (`bd ready`,
   `bd list`), mark the four markdown trackers retired-in-place (findings 1-11).
2. README.md:115: replace the review-fleet claim with the 2026-08-27 labelled-review rule (23).
3. README.md doc map: add REVIEW-2026-08-30.md; demote REVIEW-2026-08-21.md to history (24).
4. Scrub the three chaos references (25) — AGENTS.md hard rule.

**P2 — truth about the product (numbers):**
5. README.md:56,62,70,107: 138 Chrome tools (or "≈140" with the test as the guard), three lazy
   definitions, 31 bundled Wasm tools. Consider replacing hardcoded counts with "see
   tests/chrome-tool-capabilities.test.ts bounds" so they cannot rot (6).
6. README.md:253 + PLAN.md:8-15 gate tables: either update to a measured current value with a
   date, or (better) state "gates are green at tip; the suite grows daily — see REVIEW-2026-08-30
   for the last full measurement" and stop hardcoding (6).
7. PLAN.md:170 (28→31), PLAN.md:32-33 (capability table 155/160→188), PLAN.md:189-192 Pyodide
   entry → shipped (21), PLAN.md:86 + README.md:194 + PRODUCT.md:66-67: drop/revise chat//memory
   explorer references (12-14), PRODUCT.md:196-198 flat-list-of-126 paragraph → purpose groups
   landed (docs/TOOL-PURPOSE-GROUPS.md) (6).
8. CONSTITUTION.md: refresh the closing gate-state section and the XSS bullet's surface list
   (15, 22).

**P3 — status headers and the tool-platform rewrite:**
9. docs/tool-platform-architecture.md: mark the pre-cutover sections HISTORICAL (the style
   durable-background-runs-design.md already uses) and add a "current state" header pointing at
   the shipped execution path — or fold the living parts into the stage-2 ARCHITECTURE.md and
   retire the rest to history (17).
10. Status-line fixes: AGENT-DELEGATION.md:2 (19), THREAD-LOADING-REDESIGN.md:3 (20),
    AGENT-EXECUTION-ARCHITECTURE.md §6/§7 (18), OPEN-QUESTIONS.md Q12 placement (27),
    ROUTE_MAP.md re-inventory (29), DURABLE-RUN-ARCHITECTURE.md citation-currency note (36),
    docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md redirect target (8).
11. One-line status headers on the four dated audits (28).

**Out of scope for doc fixes:** the recipes→skills rename completion (code work, bead
chrome-agent-platform-l0r); the missing architecture content (stage 2 of this umbrella fills
G-30..35).

**Suggested beads:** one bead per P1/P2 item group (1, 2-4, 5-8) + one for P3 (9-11), each with
the verification gate: `npm run build` clean + `npm run test:changed` green + a grep assertion
that the stale string is gone (the pattern already used by check:vocabulary).

title: Run-driven tool executions bypass the action ledger and the usage counters
description: Found during chrome-agent-platform-86oj migration: tool executions issued by a run's worker loop (lazy dispatch) never reach the bookkeeping that lives on the agent-worker.tool route bridge (executeWorkerTool in service-worker.js): the action ledger (what-happened rows, the Undo flow's data source) and the tool-usage counters (recordToolCall). The run's own record lands in the durable thread instead. Decide: should run-driven mutations ALSO ledger (owner-visible what-happened + Undo) and count toward usage? If yes, move the bookkeeping into the shared dispatch path; if no, document the split. The 86oj harnesses assert the thread record for now.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
Candidate ffc4b263 pushed to branch cap-beads-m6id (off main 27ec8926).

title: Page.captureScreenshot(fromSurface) hangs on a quiesced headless page — no frame gets scheduled
description: Found during 5ht (logs ~/logs/cap-5ht-gates/ runs 05-10): in headless Chromium with --disable-gpu, Page.captureScreenshot(fromSurface:true) issued when the page has no pending visual work waits forever for a frame that is never scheduled (deterministic, 5 consecutive runs, marker-bisected: the capture call never returns). Captures issued while a transition/animation is in flight succeed (frame source alive). Mechanism not fully isolated (a mouseMoved poke did NOT revive it; earlier settled-state captures after clicks DID work — the exact preconditions are murkier than 'settled'). Any script capturing evidence after the page has gone idle is exposed. Mitigations: keep a transition alive, capture immediately after interaction, or wrap captures in a bounded race. The ui-integration watchdog + dropped RTL capture is the landed instance.
notes: MERGED to origin/main — safeCaptureScreenshot with bounded race + rAF wake + fromSurface:false fallback; never wedges. Coordinator review PASS; full suite 3420/0.

title: Full suite is not --parallel-safe: dist-marker order dependence (build-bootstrap must precede bundled-tool-packages)
description:
Discovered while measuring deno test --parallel behaviour for chrome-agent-platform-9hoc.

Observed: the full suite runs SERIAL by default (deno test runs modules one at a time; 8x4s probe = 33s serial vs 4s --parallel). --parallel would cut the 345s gate massively, but it is NOT safe today:
- tests/build-bootstrap.test.ts runs 'node build.mjs --target=store' and regenerates the dist.complete marker (target=store) in extension/dist-versions/
- tests/bundled-tool-packages.test.ts + tool-exec-preview.test.ts validate that marker with expectedTarget store
- Alphabetical serial order self-heals (build-bootstrap < bundled-tool-packages). Under --parallel the validator can run before/while the regenerator runs -> false reds (measured: bundled-tool-packages + tool-exec-preview + security-suite-custody FAIL under --parallel, all PASS serially).
- Reproduced deterministically: deno test -A --parallel on the 7-file hazard set fails; the same files serial pass.
- Also observed: after a developer build (marker target=developer), bundled-tool-packages.test.ts alone fails 'expected store, got developer' — marker state is ambient and order-dependent.

Acceptance: make --parallel safe for the full suite (order-independent dist marker custody — e.g. the marker validators tolerate/regenerate a store marker themselves, or dist-marker tests serialize) OR document --parallel as out of scope and keep the serial gate. Subset picker (9hoc) already runs subsets serial to match gate semantics exactly.
close_reason: Resolved by the two-phase runner landed at 72c5857e: the 7 dist/artifact-mutating files run serially, the other 327 with --parallel. Full-suite --parallel of every file remains unsafe by design; a guard test pinning serial-set membership is filed as a follow-up.

title: Agents never clean up the tabs/windows they open — encourage + support lifecycle cleanup (tool descriptions, skills, and a cleanup affordance)
description:
Owner feature request 2026-09-02: when an agent plans with tab-opening tools (tabs.open / new tab, new window, etc.), it never cleans up after itself — tabs stay open long after the task ends. The tab count grows across tasks and the owner closes them by hand.

GOAL: agents tidy up after themselves — without breaking the cases where leaving a tab open IS the point (e.g. 'open this article for me').

WORK:
1. AUDIT the lifecycle-bearing tools: tabs.open, window creation, tabs create/select, capture flows, any tool that creates persistent browser state. List each with what it leaves behind.
2. TOOL DESCRIPTIONS: each lifecycle tool's description gets explicit cleanup guidance for the model: state what it opens, that the agent should close what it no longer needs (tabs.close) when the task that motivated it is complete, and that leaving things open should be a deliberate choice told to the user ('left the docs tab open for you').
3. SKILL: a first-party cleanup skill (e.g. browser-tidy) the system prompt/skill promotion can surface: after finishing a task, review what you opened; close scratch tabs; report what you left open and why.
4. RUN-END HOOK (the real teeth): on task/run completion, the run summary includes the tabs/windows the run OPENED (they're already tracked in the tool catalog/usage), so cleanup is one obvious step — and consider an optional owner setting: 'auto-close tabs opened by a finished task (except ones the agent flagged as keepers)'. Default OFF (owner trust), surfaced in Settings.
5. Falsification tests: description guidance present on every lifecycle tool (a test that walks the lifecycle tool list and asserts each description mentions cleanup); the run-end summary lists opened tab ids; the auto-close setting (if implemented) closes exactly the run's tabs and nothing else.

Related: chrome-agent-platform-jb0a/kmpq/p45y are unrelated; this is behaviour-shaping + tooling, not a cap.
close_reason: Closed

comments.text:
Implemented on branch cap-beads-4ffg (ee6028b0 + 44406f53; NOT merged to main).
1) AUDIT: docs/LIFECYCLE-CLEANUP.md lists every lifecycle tool + what it leaves behind; machine tables (LIFECYCLE_OPEN_TOOLS / LIFECYCLE_RELEASE_TOOLS) in extension/lib/lifecycle-cleanup.js.
2) DESCRIPTIONS: open_tab / duplicate_tab / create_window / restore_closed descriptions now carry cleanup guidance (state what opens, close what the task no longer needs via close_tab/close_window, leaving something open is a deliberate choice told to the user). duplicate_tab's copy id is now recorded in the Act-class opened set like open_tab.
3) SKILL: first-party 'Browser tidy' on-demand recipe in the shared catalog (extension/lib/recipes.js) — surfaceable via /skill, hub chips, Settings, and the skill-promotion layer.
4) RUN-END HOOK: runTask tracks per-run opened/released tabs+windows from the tool-result stream; on terminal SUCCESS the runtime appends a bounded note to the final summary listing the tab/window ids this run opened and left open (live re-checked so a tab the owner closed mid-run is never claimed open). description:
## [CAP-FB-20260902-BUDGET-VERDICT-ANSWERED-01] A run that calls tools AND writes its answer on its last allowed step is settled as "Budget reached" although the answer landed
- Feedback: 2026-09-02 — LOOP-CONTEXT-WINDOW-01 worker, live 30-tab run at `maxIterations=3`: the digest was written and persisted, yet the terminal read "Budget reached (9 of 9)" and the Continue card appeared, because the budget verdict rule is "the last step had tool calls".
- Updated: 2026-09-02 05:10 UTC
- Status: OPEN
- Resume: —
- Priority: P2
- Owner: unassigned
- Workspace: none
- Branch: none
- Base: —
- Candidate: —
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: A run whose final model step produced substantive final text (per `extension/lib/run-text-steps.js` `finalText`) settles `ok:true` regardless of whether that step also called tools; "Budget reached — Continue" appears only when the budget ran out with NO substantive final text. The live check `scripts/live-every-tab.ts` at `CAP_LIVE_MAX_ITERATIONS=3` settles ok with 30/30 cited. The status row's counter and the Continue card are otherwise unchanged.
  - Context: `extension/lib/run-budget.js` (RUN-BUDGET-EVERY-ITEM-01) sets `exhausted:true` on the last `budget` event when the last iteration still had tool calls; `extension/lib/agent.js` `onComplete` / the SW terminal settle read that flag and write `errorCategory:"budget"`. description:
## [CAP-FB-20260830-ON-DEVICE-PATH-01] Chrome's built-in model (Prompt API) handles text-only steps on-device, with a hosted model for planning and tools
- Feedback: 2026-08-30 — reanalysis 2026-08-30 product lane, finding 16. With no key, "summarise this page" cannot be answered at all, even on a Chrome that ships Gemini Nano; the Prompt API adapter cannot call tools and silently falls back to the demo provider.
- Updated: 2026-08-30 14:30 UTC
- Status: OPEN
- Resume: —
- Priority: P2
- Owner: unassigned
- Workspace: none
- Branch: none
- Base: `cf0da958`
- Candidate: —
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: on a Prompt-API-capable Chrome with no provider key, "summarise this page" and "group my tabs by topic" complete: the deterministic tool steps (read_page, list_tabs, group_tabs) run through the keyless path from CAP-FB-20260830-KEYLESS-FIRST-RESULT-01 and the text steps (summarise, name the groups) run on-device; each assistant bubble is labelled with the model that produced it ("On-device (Gemini Nano)" or the hosted model id such as `gemini-3.7-flash`); when the Prompt API is unavailable the transcript says so in one sentence instead of falling to the demo string. Done = a headed run on a named Chrome version shows both prompts working keyless, screenshots attached; the unit tests pin the routing.
  - Context: `extension/lib/models/prompt-api-model.js:52-64` flattens `tool-call` and `tool-result` content parts into text and always returns `finishReason:"stop"` (`:162`, `:200`), so the AI SDK loop can never receive a tool call from it. `extension/lib/provider.js:196-212` chooses the Prompt API when available and otherwise returns `createDemoModel()` labelled "demo (prompt api unavailable)". `isLocalProvider` (`extension/lib/provider-gate.js:42`) already exempts both from the host-permission gate. Existing tests: `tests/prompt-api.test.ts` (`createPromptApiModel` options, readiness error, `isPromptApiAvailable`, the fresh-session attestation boundary at `:81`) and `tests/prompt-api-tokens.test.ts`. What must NOT change: the attestation boundary (a fresh session per call bound to the exact system message); the secret-free provider config; the provider gate's local-provider exemption.
  - Reproduce today: (1) on a Chrome with `LanguageModel` available (chrome://flags "Prompt API for Gemini Nano" enabled; record the version), load the extension on a fresh profile; (2) Settings → Providers → choose "Chrome built-in" (the Prompt API preset in `PROVIDER_CHOICES`, `extension/lib/provider.js:45-98`); (3) hub: "summarise this page" — the run either answers without reading the page (no tool call is possible) or, if the model is not ready, the reply is the demo string "[demo model] Task received…".
  - Files: `extension/lib/models/prompt-api-model.js` (keep the text adapter; add `supportsTools:false` metadata); `extension/lib/provider.js` (`:196-212` — return a routed pair `{ planner, textModel }` when a hosted provider is configured alongside the Prompt API, otherwise the keyless deterministic assistant plus the on-device text model); `extension/lib/agent.js` (the step loop — after a tool result, if the next step is text-only and an on-device model exists, call it; the hook point is where the model is invoked per step); `extension/shared/components.js` (`message-bubble` — a `model` attribute rendered as a small label); `extension/lib/error-report.js` (a `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` category with the sentence "Chrome's built-in model is not available on this device — connect a model in Settings"). Do NOT touch `extension/lib/provider-gate.js` or the demo model.
  - Steps: (1) Land after CAP-FB-20260830-KEYLESS-FIRST-RESULT-01 defines the deterministic intent set; add a `textModel` slot to the resolved provider (`provider.js:196`) populated by `createPromptApiModel` when `isPromptApiAvailable()` is true. (2) In the loop, route a step to `textModel` only when the step has no tool definitions in scope (the deterministic assistant has already executed the tools) and the prompt is under the Prompt API context budget (`tests/prompt-api-tokens.test.ts` shows the token accounting). (3) Stamp every persisted assistant message with `modelId` (the thread store already carries provider ids for attestation — reuse that field) and render it on the bubble. (4) Replace the "demo (prompt api unavailable)" fallback with the `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` error when the owner explicitly chose the built-in model. (5) Record the Chrome version and the headed evidence in History; update `docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md` Q12 (recommended default remains `gemini-3.7-flash` hosted; on-device is the keyless complement).
  - Out of scope: the deterministic keyless assistant itself (CAP-FB-20260830-KEYLESS-FIRST-RESULT-01); the provider picker flow (CAP-FB-20260830-PROVIDER-DEFAULT-AND-KEY-FLOW-01); a tools-capable on-device adapter (not available in the Prompt API today — do not emulate tool calls by parsing text).
- Review: pending
- Gates: the falsification gates apply.
  - Unit: extend `tests/prompt-api.test.ts` with "the resolved provider exposes an on-device text model when the Prompt API is available and a hosted key is absent" and "a text-only step after tool results is routed to the on-device model; a step with tools in scope is not". Falsification: revert step 2, expect RED on "text-only step is routed on-device", restore, expect GREEN.

design:
# CAP-FB-20260830-ON-DEVICE-PATH-01 — implementation + gate plan (PREP, awaiting Paul's 4 sign-offs)

Worktree: ~/worktrees/cap-wasm-catalogue, branch on-device-analysis, rebased on origin/main@14e2a817 (clean).

## Implementation shape (from the accepted analysis)

1. **extension/lib/models/prompt-api-model.js** — add `supportsTools: false`
   metadata. Keep: fresh-session-per-call attestation boundary, verbatim
   system prompt, topK+temperature pair, estimateTokens, session destroy.
2. **extension/lib/provider.js** (`prompt-api` branch :283-299 + default
   branch) — resolved provider gains a `textModel` slot:
   `createPromptApiModel()` when `isPromptApiAvailable()`; the explicit
   built-in choice with the API unavailable returns a MODEL_UNAVAILABLE
   error path instead of the silent `demo (prompt api unavailable)` fallback.
3. **extension/lib/models/router-model.js (NEW)** — a LanguageModel proxy
   layered at the boundModel seam (agent.js:1158): per doGenerate/doStream
   call, inspect options — tools present → planner model; no tools AND
   estimated input (estimateTokens) under the Nano budget → textModel.
   Both lanes pass through the existing attestation observation unchanged.
4. **extension/lib/agent.js** — none, if the router proxy suffices (preferred);
   otherwise the per-step hook at the model-invocation point.
5. **extension/shared/components.js** — message-bubble: small model label
   (textContent only): "On-device (Gemini Nano)" / hosted model id /
   "Local (keyless)".
6. **extension/lib/error-report.js** — MODEL_UNAVAILABLE category:
   "Chrome's built-in model is not available on this device — connect a
   model in Settings".
7. **Persistence** — stamp assistant messages with modelId (reuse the
   thread-store provider id field used for attestation).

DO NOT TOUCH: provider-gate.js local-provider exemption, the demo model,
the attestation boundary, secret-free provider config.

## Unit gates (extend tests/prompt-api.test.ts + new tests/router-model.test.ts)

Existing anchors: prompt-api.test.ts:81 attestation boundary;
prompt-api-tokens.test.ts estimator.

New tests:
1. "resolved provider exposes an on-device textModel when the Prompt API is
   available and no hosted key is configured" (provider.js, mock LanguageModel).
2. "a text-only step after tool results routes to the on-device model;
   a step with tools in scope routes to the planner" (router-model:
   fake planner + fake textModel, assert which receives the call for
   options with/without tools).
3. "an over-budget text-only step (estimateTokens > Nano budget) routes to
   the planner even with no tools in scope".
4. "explicit built-in choice + API unavailable yields MODEL_UNAVAILABLE,
   never the demo model" (assert providerName/modelId, assert NOT
   createDemoModel's demo string).
5. "assistant messages carry modelId and the bubble renders it via
   textContent" (components test).
6. Regression pins: attestation boundary test (:81) unchanged and green;
   topK+temperature pair test unchanged.

## Falsification gates (mandatory before review)

- G1: implement test 2 first → RED (no router); implement router-model →
  GREEN. Record both runs.
- G2: test 4: temporarily restore the demo-fallback line in provider.js →
  RED; restore fix → GREEN. Record both.
- G3: the attestation test at prompt-api.test.ts:81 must stay green
  unmodified through every step (a changed assertion there = stop).
- G4: deleting coverage requires a guard — n/a (additive change).

## Browser gate (HEADED — Nano is unavailable under --headless=new)

- Record Chrome version; chrome://on-device or flags state; model downloaded.
- Prompt 1: "summarise this page" keyless → tools via keyless path, summary
  on-device, bubble labelled. Screenshot on-device-summarise.png.
- Prompt 2: "group my tabs by topic" → real groups + on-device group names.
  Screenshot on-device-group-tabs.png.
- Prompt-API-unavailable run: one-sentence transcript message (no demo
  string). Screenshot.
- `deno run -A scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` green unchanged (keyless lane).

## Full-suite gate (pre-push, once)

npm run build && npm test && chrome journeys green at tip.
Iterate with npm run test:file -- tests/router-model.test.ts /
tests/prompt-api.test.ts during development.

## Docs (same commit)

docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md Q12 (pending Paul's answer), CHANGELOG.md entry,
docs/DESIGN.md if the bubble label introduces a new component variant.

## Constraints

Untrusted page text inside the CAP-FB-20260830-UNTRUSTED-CONTENT-FENCING-01
envelope; truncated to the Nano budget via measureInputUsage where available,
estimateTokens otherwise. No keys in logs. Label via textContent. No fixed
debug port (headed run uses launchChrome()).

title: [CAP-FB-20260831-TOOL-PIPELINES-01] No way to chain/pipe tool steps into a small script (co-do-style)
description:
## [CAP-FB-20260831-TOOL-PIPELINES-01] No way to chain/pipe tool steps into a small script (co-do-style)
- Feedback: 2026-08-31 — owner: "I want the tools to create better scripts to chain a couple of steps together so we can pipe things... my co-do projects used to do this, we need it here too." Today each tool call is standalone; there is no way to compose a few steps (e.g. list files -> grep -> summarize) into one reusable, inspectable pipeline the way co-do did.
- Updated: 2026-09-01 18:15 UTC
- Status: OPEN
- Resume: slice 2 — wire `run_pipeline` as a lazy-protocol meta-tool + plan-strip per-step visibility (see the DESIGN-DECISION + slice-2 plan in History)
- Priority: P2
- Owner: coordinator session — slice 1 landed; slice 2 unclaimed (pick up from Resume)
- Workspace: active (local path private)
- Branch: `cap/tool-pipelines` (slice 1 merged; reuse for slice 2)
- Base: `origin/main@331989d5`
- Candidate: `ad6dd2a8` (slice 1)
- Shipping: `origin/main@c0021d99` (slice 1 — the pure core + design; NOT yet model-callable)
- Acceptance: a bounded, safe way to chain a few tool steps into one pipeline where a step's output feeds the next (a "pipe"), inspectable and reusable, without eval/new Function (MV3 CSP). Design and land a first slice: a `run_pipeline`-style tool (or a saved-skill "recipe" of ordered steps with a declared data flow) that runs N existing tools in sequence, passing each result to the next by an explicit binding, surfaces each step in the transcript/plan-strip, fails closed with the same gates as its constituent tools, and can be saved and re-run. This is a DESIGN task first: write the model (declarative step list with input bindings vs a constrained expression pipe), then implement the minimal version. Reuse the existing sandbox (`extension/sandbox/`, no eval), the lazy protocol, and the plan strip (PLAN-STRIP-CHECKPOINTS-01) for visibility. Reference the co-do pipeline model the owner used.
  - Context: `run_script` exists (sandboxed JS, owner-approved) but is not a legible pipeline of tools; skills/recipes (`extension/lib/recipes.js` / skills) are prompt templates, not data-flow pipelines. The gap is composing TOOLS with piped IO.
  - Files (design will refine): a new pipeline module + tool def in `extension/lib/`, the sandbox for any expression evaluation (no eval), the lazy protocol for step dispatch, the plan strip + transcript for visibility, a save path in skills/recipes.
  - Steps: 1. Write the design (data-flow model, safety, what "pipe" means concretely, how it differs from run_script and skills) in the entry + docs/DESIGN.md. 2. Implement a minimal ordered-steps-with-bindings pipeline over existing tools. 3. Visibility via the plan strip. 4. Save + re-run.
  - Out of scope: a full scripting language; anything using eval/new Function.
- DESIGN DECISION (2026-09-01, slice 1): DECLARATIVE steps with bindings, NOT an expression pipe. A pipeline = `{ name?, steps: [{ id, tool, args }] }`; an arg may carry a binding token `{ $ref: "<earlierStepId>", path?: "a.b.0.c" }` that a PURE path lookup (no eval) replaces with the referenced step's result. Chosen over a constrained expression pipe because MV3 CSP forbids eval/new Function and a declarative form is more legible + serialisable (saveable as JSON). Three safety properties: (1) the tool NAME is fixed per step, never bindable — untrusted content from an earlier step can only land in a later step's DATA position, never choose the tool; (2) each step dispatches through the run's normal tool seam (`LazyToolProtocol.execute`, `extension/lib/lazy-tool-protocol.js:830`) so its owner-approval card + untrusted fence apply exactly as a direct call, and the card shows RESOLVED args; (3) fail-closed — `$ref` may reference only an EARLIER step (linear, no cycles), an unresolved binding halts with a structured error, step count + args size bounded. Contrast with `run_script` (one opaque sandboxed-JS blob approved by source digest): a pipeline is a legible chain of NAMED existing tools, each re-gated + each visible on its own plan-strip row. Full write-up in `docs/DESIGN.md` (Tool pipelines section) and the `extension/lib/tool-pipeline.js` header.
- Review: author review 2026-09-01 (slice 1) — the pure core's falsification gate cleared (RED/GREEN recorded); slice 2 pending its own review.
- Gates: the falsification gates apply.
  - Unit: DONE (slice 1) — `tests/tool-pipeline.test.ts` (7): a 3-step pipeline pipes each result forward (bindings resolved by pure path lookup); a failing step halts fail-closed with a structured error; a broken binding halts fail-closed; validate rejects forward/self refs, duplicate ids, over-limit, unknown tools. FALSIFIED: breaking `resolveStepArgs` (bindings no longer resolved) turns the pipe test + the fail-closed gate RED (3 failed); restored → 7/7 GREEN.
  - Browser: SLICE 2 — a journey running a small 2-3 step pipeline (demo tools, e.g. `@demo-pipeline` chaining memory_set → memory_get) and showing each step in the plan strip. Requires the live wiring below.
  - Full suite: `npm run build:production && deno test -A tests/` green — DONE for slice 1 (2937/0 at `c0021d99`, incl. the 7 new tests). NOTE: `tests/review49-regression.test.ts` imports from a HARD-CODED `file:///tmp/cap-artifact-tx-current-main/...` path; when that scratch checkout is absent the 9 tests fail with "Module not found" (environmental, unrelated to any code change) — restore with `ln -sfn <repo> /tmp/cap-artifact-tx-current-main`. Flagged as a latent flake to fix (use `import.meta.url`, not an absolute /tmp path).
  - Constraints: no eval/new Function (MV3 CSP); each step keeps its own gates/approvals; untrusted data fenced; one name per concept.
- Blockers: Depends on CAP-FB-20260831-FS-GRANT-TASK-USE-01 for a compelling file-pipeline demo (grep is a natural pipe source); PLAN-STRIP-CHECKPOINTS-01 (DONE) for visibility
- Next (SLICE 2): wire `run_pipeline` as a 4th lazy-protocol meta-tool in `createLazyProviderToolset` (`extension/lib/lazy-tool-protocol.js:1308`) whose handler runs `runPipeline` with a `dispatchTool` adapter that, per step, calls `protocol.search({query: step.tool})` → picks the exact-name entry's `selectionRef` → `protocol.execute({selectionRef, arguments: resolvedArgs}, context)` → returns `{ ok: r.ok, value: r.result, error: r.error }` (reuses the PUBLIC seam, no security-core edits; the fence is preserved as data flows). Add its wire descriptor + output schema to `LAZY_PROTOCOL_TOOL_WIRE` (`extension/lib/lazy-tool-wire.js`) and UPDATE the 3 tests that pin the eager meta-tool set (`lazy-tool-protocol.test.ts`, `lazy-provider-cutover.test.ts`, `provider-gate.test.ts`). For plan-strip PER-STEP visibility, thread `onProgress` into the frozen lazy context (`extension/lib/agent.js` contextReader, ~:878) and emit `step-start`/`step-end` per pipeline step via `runPipeline`'s `onStep`. Then the browser gate: add a `@demo-pipeline` marker to `extension/lib/models/demo-model.js` issuing a `run_pipeline` that chains `memory_set` → `memory_get`, and a journey asserting both steps render in the plan strip and the piped result is correct. Save-and-re-run (a pipeline stored as a structured skill payload) is a SLICE 3 — today's skills/recipes store is prompt-text only and needs a new `steps` field.
- Recover: `git log --oneline --all --grep=CAP-FB-20260831-TOOL-PIPELINES-01`
- Next: slice 2 (live wiring) — wire the declarative pipeline core into the run so a pipeline definition executes end to end; slice 1 (design + core) landed at origin/main@c0021d99
- History:
  - 2026-08-31 19:20 UTC — filed from owner feedback (co-do-style piped tool chains); design-first.
  - 2026-09-01 17:45 UTC — CLAIMED by the coordinator (owner asked to start it). Design-first.
  - 2026-09-01 18:15 UTC — SLICE 1 landed at `origin/main@c0021d99`. Design decided + documented (see DESIGN DECISION above + docs/DESIGN.md). The pure gated core `extension/lib/tool-pipeline.js` (validate/resolve/runPipeline) + `tests/tool-pipeline.test.ts` (7, RED-proven) landed; full suite 2937/0. No behavior change yet (module unimported) and no version bump — it is NOT model-callable until slice 2 wires `run_pipeline` (the seam is identified + specified in Next). Slice 1 was scoped deliberately: the live wiring touches the security-critical lazy protocol + the eager tool surface (3 pinned tests) + needs onProgress plumbing for plan-strip visibility, which is a focused next increment rather than a rushed change. Entry stays OPEN.

title: [CAP-FB-20260830-MODEL-CALL-ECONOMY-01] A 19 KB system prompt on every call and an agent-do nudge that costs one extra call per turn
description:
## [CAP-FB-20260830-MODEL-CALL-ECONOMY-01] A 19 KB system prompt on every call and an agent-do nudge that costs one extra call per turn
- Feedback: 2026-08-30 — reanalysis 2026-08-30 product lane finding 15, editing lane finding 8, live lane finding 11. "Open a tab and tell me its title" costs six provider calls and ~28k input tokens; the last call of every tool-using turn exists only to answer "Continue working on the task".
- Updated: 2026-08-30 14:30 UTC
- Status: OPEN
- Resume: —
- Priority: P2
- Owner: unassigned
- Workspace: none
- Branch: none
- Base: `fc2255be`
- Candidate: —
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: The composed hub system prompt is under 6 KB (measured by a unit test on the registry), the agent-do continuation nudge is never sent after a step that already produced final text, a scripted provider that re-calls a tool on every nudge stops within 3 iterations with a visible "stopped after N steps" marker, and the two-turn artifact journey shows exactly 3 provider calls for the create turn.
  - Context: the prompt is composed by `composeSystemPrompt` in `extension/lib/system-prompts.js` (line 637; base + owner override + role + skills + runtime constraints layers) from `PROMPT_REGISTRY` (133) whose base content is `extension/lib/master-skill.js`; the file is 51,851 bytes and the run-log attestation records `composedBytes:17848` with `prefixMatch` (`extension/lib/agent.js:505`, journalled at `service-worker.js:2539`). The nudge is inside the bundled `agent-do@0.7.0` loop (`node_modules/agent-do/dist/src/loop.js:743-747` and the second copy at 1141, both bundled into the SW — `grep -c "Continue working on the task" extension/dist/background/service-worker.js` = 2): after every iteration with `hasToolCalls` it pushes a user message "Continue working on the task. If you are done, respond with your final summary without calling any tools." and calls the provider again with the whole transcript, even when that iteration already ended in final text. agent-do exposes the stop hook: `hooks.onStepStart` may return `{decision:"stop"}` (loop.js 619-629; `types.d.ts:364`), and `onStepComplete` receives `{step, hasToolCalls, text}` (loop.js 733-738). The product wires both at `extension/lib/agent.js:763` (`onStepStart`) and `:779` (`onStepComplete`, which already forwards `{type:"text", text, hasToolCalls}` to the UI), and configures `maxIterations` (402, default 12) and `innerStepLimit` (745). The lane evidence used gpt-4.1 and gemini-2.5-flash; the current model IDs to target are gpt-5.6-sol, gemini-3.7-flash, grok-4.6, glm-5.3 and claude-sonnet-5 — re-measure on those. What must NOT change: the protected constraints layer ordering (system-prompts 700-745), the attestation/`prefixMatch` bookkeeping, `innerStepLimit`.
  - Reproduce today: (1) build; (2) run the editing lane's scripted OpenAI-compatible provider pattern (promoted to `scripts/lib/scripted-provider.ts` by CAP-FB-20260830-SUITE-HONESTY-01; until then, its scratchpad `fake-provider.ts`) that answers `search_tools` → `execute_tool(create_asset)` → final text; (3) count HTTP requests at the fake provider — 4 where 3 did the work, the 4th body ~20 KB carrying the nudge; (4) with the demo provider on the hub, note the sidebar preview "Task received (19582 chars)" — that number is the prompt size; (5) script the provider to always answer a nudge with another tool call — observe 12 iterations / 25 calls and repeated agent bubbles with no user turn between them.
  - Files: `extension/lib/agent.js` (763-790: the hook wiring — add the stop predicate), `extension/lib/agent-loop.js` (58-66: mirror the predicate for the worker path so both loops agree), `extension/lib/system-prompts.js` (`composeSystemPrompt` 637; add a `promptBudget` measurement helper), `extension/lib/master-skill.js` (the prose to cut; keep the tool-name list but move per-tool usage rules into the tool `description` strings in `extension/lib/management-tools.js` and `browser-tools.js`), `tests/agent-do-logging.test.ts` (extend) and a new `tests/prompt-budget.test.ts`, `KNOWN-ISSUES.md` (only if agent-do proves unconfigurable — it is not; the hook exists). Do NOT touch `extension/lib/provider.js` error mapping (CAP-FB-20260830-PROVIDER-ERROR-TRUTH-01).
  - Steps: (1) Stop predicate: in `agent.js` `onStepComplete` remember `lastStep = {hasToolCalls, text}`; in `onStepStart` return `{decision:"stop"}` when `lastStep.hasToolCalls && lastStep.text.trim().length > 0` (the step both called tools and wrote its final answer — the nudge would only ask for a repeat). Also count nudged iterations and stop at 3, emitting a progress event `{type:"stopped", reason:"iteration-cap", steps}` that `extension/shared/conversation.js` renders as a muted status line "Stopped after N steps" through the existing `conversation-run-status` element (`components.js:5297`) — never as another agent bubble. (2) Prompt budget: add `measurePromptLayers(scope)` in `system-prompts.js` returning bytes per layer; unit-test the hub composition is under 6,144 bytes. (3) Cut the manual: in `master-skill.js` remove the per-tool inventory prose (the tool descriptors are already shown to the model by `search_tools`/`list_tools`, lines 44-77 explain that mechanism — keep those), keep the artifacts model section (260+) to three sentences. (4) Provider caching: for Anthropic set the system block `cache_control: {type:"ephemeral"}` through the AI SDK provider options in the model factory; for OpenAI-compatible endpoints the stable prefix is enough — assert `prefixMatch` stays true in the run log. (5) Re-measure with the scripted provider (call count) and once with a real key on gpt-5.6-sol and claude-sonnet-5 (tokens, cost) and record in History.
  - Out of scope: the nudge summary overwriting the real answer on persist (CAP-FB-20260830-TRANSCRIPT-FULL-ANSWER-01); streaming (CAP-FB-20260830-TRANSCRIPT-STREAMING-01); first-classing the top tools to remove `search_tools` round trips (record as a follow-up in this entry's History, do not do it here).

Falsification: revert step 1, expect RED on "no continuation after a step that produced final text", restore, expect GREEN.
  - Browser: the keyless two-turn artifact journey in `deno run -A scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` (from SUITE-HONESTY-01) — check "artifact create turn is exactly 3 provider calls" (the scripted provider counts requests) and "runaway tool loop shows 'Stopped after 3 steps'" with screenshot `thread-stopped-after-steps.png` showing the status line and no repeated bubbles.
  - Full suite: `npm run build && deno test tests/ && deno run -A scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` green (2457 / 138 at `fc2255be`; re-count).

description:

- Feedback: 2026-08-30 — reanalysis 2026-08-30 perf lane, findings 6, 9, 10 and 13; security lane finding 8. The worker bundle is 82 percent over the constitution's stated budget and nothing in the build fails when it grows; the Python runtime would fetch ~10 MB from a CDN with empty integrity pins.

- Status: OPEN
- Resume: —

- Branch: none
- Base: `fc2255be`

- Acceptance: The store-target service-worker bundle is at or under 3.0 MB with a build-time size gate that fails above it and prints the top contributors; the hub and side panel load one bundled module each; no `cdn.jsdelivr.net` string ships in any bundle (Pyodide is either bundled-and-pinned or deleted); cold-start busy window at or under 80 ms.
