Contributors (security lane): zod 1,063 KB, three provider SDKs plus gateway ~730 KB shipped unconditionally; `service-worker.js` imports `BUNDLED_INVENTORY` and `BUNDLED_TOOL_PACKAGE_ROWS` at lines 68-69 (data modules totalling 1,668 lines across `extension/lib/bundled-*.js`, used only by `tool.preview.run` and the Tool library) and `ai`/`zod` at 498-499. The agent worker bundle has no caller (`extension/lib/agent-worker-client.js` is imported by nothing; `reconcileAgentWorkers` at 7789 runs against an alive-set that can never fill) — that cut is CAP-FB-20260830-DEAD-CODE-CUT-01. `build.mjs` builds three entries (SW 285-296, options 297, worker 302-318), scrubs `new Function` (320-338) and has no size check or metafile. The hub loads ~41 unbundled modules (~1.1 MB) per tab. `extension/lib/python-runtime.js:13-24` pins URLs with `jsIntegrity: ""` and `wasmIntegrity: ""`, and `verifyIntegrity` (line 36) returns the text unchecked when the pin is empty; `python-tool.js` always reports unavailable today. Cold start today is 114-117 ms busy, so this is hygiene rather than a felt delay — do not trade behaviour for bytes. What must NOT change: `components.js` stays the single unbundled source that `scripts/sync-gallery.mjs` copies to `docs/` (`check:gallery`); the eval scrub and seam scan.
  - Reproduce today: (1) `npm run build:production`; (2) `ls -l extension/dist/background/service-worker.js` → over 4.5 MB; (3) `grep -c cdn.jsdelivr.net extension/dist/background/service-worker.js` → non-zero; (4) open the hub through `launchChrome()` and list `chrome-extension://` script loads from the page target (`Network.enable` + `responseReceived`) → ~41 module fetches.
  - Files: `build.mjs` (add `metafile: true` to the shared esbuild options at 275-279, a post-build size report, and the gate; add NTP and side-panel entries beside `OPT` at 282/297); `extension/background/service-worker.js:68-69` (dynamic-import the inventory data inside the `tool.preview.run` and tool-library routes) and 498-499 (provider adapter imports — grep `@ai-sdk/` and import the adapter only inside the provider factory in `extension/lib/provider.js`); `extension/ntp/ntp.html` and `extension/sidepanel/sidepanel.html` (point at `dist/ntp.bundle.js` / `dist/sidepanel.bundle.js`); `scripts/build-test-extension.mjs` (mirror every new entry — it rebuilds the SW and options into the isolated test copy at its lines 44-62 and must build the same entries); `extension/lib/python-runtime.js` + `extension/lib/python-tool.js` (delete, or bundle per `docs/PYODIDE-BOUNDED-BUILD.md` with non-empty sha384 pins); `docs/CONSTITUTION.md:92` (state the number the gate enforces). Do NOT split `components.js`.
  - Steps: (1) Metafile + report: in `build.mjs` write `dist/build-report.json` from `result.metafile` and print the top 15 inputs by bytes for the SW; commit this alone so the contributors are visible. (2) Gate: after the scrub, `stat` the SW and fail when the store target exceeds 3,000,000 B (developer target: warn only, source maps are external so sizes match); add the same assertion as a unit test reading the built file so CI sees it. (3) Move `bundled-inventory-data.js` / `bundled-tool-packages.data.js` behind `await import()` inside the two routes that use them (esbuild splits dynamic imports into `dist/chunks/*` — set `splitting: true, outdir` for the SW build or keep `outfile` and accept the inline chunk; verify the manifest still lists the SW as `type: module`). (4) Provider adapters: import `@ai-sdk/anthropic|openai|google|openai-compatible` lazily per configured provider inside the model factory; zod stays (agent-do needs it) but audit module-scope `z.object` construction in `extension/lib/management-tools.js`/`browser-tools.js` for lazy factories only if the report shows it matters. (5) Bundle NTP and side panel: new esbuild entries with the same `shared` config, `format:"esm"`, no node shims; keep `components.js` imported by relative path so the gallery sync is unchanged. (6) Pyodide: delete `python-runtime.js`, `python-tool.js`, their tests and the tool descriptor, OR land the bounded build with pins — record the choice in History; add the "no cdn.jsdelivr.net in dist" assertion either way. title: [CAP-FB-20260830-GENERATED-UI-BOOTSTRAP-SYNTAX-01] The generated-document preference bootstrap is a JavaScript syntax error
description:
## [CAP-FB-20260830-GENERATED-UI-BOOTSTRAP-SYNTAX-01] The generated-document preference bootstrap is a JavaScript syntax error
- Feedback: 2026-08-30 — reanalysis 2026-08-30 editing lane, finding 5. Every generated page the agent renders throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ')'` in its sandbox frame, so the documented theme/locale projection into generated UI has never worked.
- Updated: 2026-08-31 09:15 UTC
- Status: OPEN
- Resume: —
- Priority: P2
- Owner: unassigned
- Workspace: none
- Branch: none
- Base: `fc2255be`
- Candidate: —
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: The injected preference bootstrap parses; a rendered frame posts `cap:preference-ready` and its `documentElement.lang` equals the owner's locale; a unit test parses both injected scripts and is RED on today's string.
  - Context: `preferenceBootstrapScript(nonce)` at `extension/shared/components.js:355-366` joins these fragments: `"(function(){var nonce=…;"`, `"function apply(p){if(!p)return;"`, `"if(p.locale){try{…}catch(e){}}"`, `"window.addEventListener('message',…apply(d.preference);});"`, `"try{window.parent.postMessage({type:'cap:preference-ready',…},'*');}catch(e){}"`, `"})();"`. The `if(p.locale){…}` closes only the `if`; `function apply(p){` is never closed, so the listener and the ready post sit inside `apply`, and the final `})();` closes `apply` and then hits `)` with no open expression. title: [CAP-FB-20260830-HUB-POLLING-01] Every open new tab polls the service worker every 5 s for the life of the tab
description:
## [CAP-FB-20260830-HUB-POLLING-01] Every open new tab polls the service worker every 5 s for the life of the tab
- Feedback: 2026-08-30 — reanalysis 2026-08-30 perf lane, finding 5. An idle new tab wakes the service worker twice every five seconds (and Settings re-renders Usage every 1.5 s), so the worker never idles while a hub tab is open.
- Updated: 2026-08-30 14:30 UTC
- Status: OPEN
- Resume: —
- Priority: P2
- Owner: unassigned
- Workspace: none
- Branch: none
- Base: `fc2255be`
- Candidate: —
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: An idle open hub generates zero service-worker routes over 60 s, the shield/console badges and the Settings Usage panel still update within 1 s of a real change, and the service worker is allowed to reach its MV3 idle teardown.
  - Context: `extension/shared/diagnostics-client.js` `startDiagnosticPolling(intervalMs = 5000)` (line 78) sets `setInterval(refreshDiagnostics)` (80); `refreshDiagnostics` (55-75) sends `diagnostics.list` and `security.state` to the SW (routes at `extension/background/service-worker.js:7202` and `:7253`) only to set a `count` attribute on `<error-console>` and `<security-shield>` (defined at `components.js:6942` and `:7002`). It is started unconditionally at `extension/ntp/ntp.js:3617` (imported at 75-76). `extension/options/options.js:2942` runs `setInterval(() => { if (document.visibilityState === "visible") renderUsage(); }, 1500)` for the whole Settings lifetime; `renderUsage` (2043) calls `usage.get` (route 5641). Measured: `route diagnostics.list` + `route security.state` from each hub tab every 4,999 ms; three tabs = six wakes per 5 s; the 500-entry cap-log ring dropped ~1,000 entries per 3 minutes, mostly this polling. The hub already holds a long-lived `agent-progress` runtime port (SW `service-worker.js:617-654`), which is the push channel to reuse. What must NOT change: the badge semantics (count + `attention` attribute), the Usage panel refreshing after a run completes or a clear.
  - Reproduce today: (1) build; (2) launch through `launchChrome()`, open the hub, wait 60 s doing nothing; (3) read the SW console via CDP `Runtime.consoleAPICalled` on the service-worker target (or `observability.dumpTrace`) and count `[cap:sw:route] diagnostics.list` / `security.state` lines — 12 each per minute per tab; (4) open Settings → Usage and count `usage.get` — 40 per minute.
  - Files: `extension/shared/diagnostics-client.js` (78-90: replace the timer with a subscription), `extension/ntp/ntp.js:3617` (call site), `extension/options/options.js:2942` (timer) and `renderUsage` (2043), `extension/background/service-worker.js` (broadcast on `pushDiagnostic`/security-event append and after `usage` record/clear — grep `securityEvent(` and `usage.clear` 5645; the `agent-progress` port registry at 617-660). Do NOT change the `diagnostics.list`/`security.state`/`usage.get` route contracts (Settings and tests read them).
  - Steps: (1) In the SW, maintain a small `diagnosticsRevision` counter; increment it wherever a diagnostic or security event is appended and after any usage write/clear, and `chrome.storage.session.set({ "cap:diagnosticsRevision": n })` (session storage is already used for bridge nonces; `onChanged` fires in every extension page without a port). (2) In `diagnostics-client.js`, replace `startDiagnosticPolling` with `startDiagnosticSubscription()` that (a) calls `refreshDiagnostics()` once on start and on `visibilitychange` → visible, and (b) listens to `chrome.storage.session.onChanged` for the revision key and refreshes on change; keep the exported name `startDiagnosticPolling` as a deprecated alias for one release so no other importer breaks (grep shows only `ntp.js`). (3) In `options.js`, delete the 1.5 s interval; call `renderUsage()` on section activation (already at 2807) and on the same revision change; keep the "Retry" button. (4) Unit + journey per Gates.
  - Out of scope: the hub header status/shield/console redesign (CAP-FB-20260830-HUB-CHROME-POLISH-01 decides whether the badges stay on the hub at all — land this entry's push mechanism regardless, it is what the Settings home for those badges will use); Settings section lazy rendering (CAP-FB-20260827-SETTINGS-MONOLITH-01).
- Review: pending
- Gates: the falsification gates apply
  - Unit: add `deno test tests/diagnostics.test.ts` case "diagnostics client refreshes on revision change and never installs an interval" — stub `chrome.storage.session.onChanged` and `setInterval` (assert `setInterval` is not called), fire a change, assert `send` was called with `diagnostics.list` exactly once. Falsification: revert step 2 (restore the `setInterval`), expect RED on "never installs an interval", restore, expect GREEN.
  - Browser: `deno run -A scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` new check "hub: idle 60 s produces zero diagnostics/security/usage routes" (count `[cap:sw:route]` console lines on the SW target during a 60 s idle window) and "hub: the shield badge updates within 1 s of a security event" (trigger `securityEvent` through an existing route that produces one, e.g. a forged-owner `management.pending-approvals` as the journey already does at ~858, then assert the `count` attribute changes). Screenshot `hub-shield-badge-updated.png`.
  - Full suite: `npm run build && deno test tests/ && deno run -A scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` green at the tip (2457 / 138 at `fc2255be`; re-count).
  - Constraints: no fixed debug port; MV3 — no persistent timers that defeat idle; the revision key carries an integer only (never event content, which is diagnostics-scrubbed elsewhere).
- Blockers: —
- Next: add the revision counter + session-storage write in the SW, then swap the client to the subscription.
- Recover: `git log --oneline --all --grep=CAP-FB-20260830-HUB-POLLING-01`

description:
## [CAP-FB-20260830-ARTIFACT-QUICK-FIXES-01] Small artifact defects: New tab opens twice, an empty id masks the real error
- Feedback: 2026-08-30 — reanalysis 2026-08-30 editing lane, findings 9 and 13. One click on "New tab" opens two viewer tabs; an agent that forgets the artifact id is told "requires owner approval" and retries the same call twelve times.

- Priority: P2

- Workspace: none
- Branch: none
- Base: `fc2255be`

- Acceptance: One New tab click yields exactly one `artifact/artifact.html` target, and `asset.update` with an empty or unknown id returns "update_asset needs an existing id (use list_assets)" before the approval gate; both assertions are RED on the current tree.
  - Context: (a) `ArtifactCard` (`extension/shared/components.js:2144-2262`): `set preview` (2148) re-renders and re-wires; the base `attributeChangedCallback` (606-614) also re-renders + re-wires on any observed attribute change; `_wire` (2234-2255) adds `open-tab` listeners to the fresh nodes; the page adds `card.addEventListener("open-tab", …)` in `wireCard` (`extension/artifacts/index.js:99-107`) which calls `chrome.tabs.create`. Measured: one genuine `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` click → two viewer tabs. The bisect is between a doubled `_emit` (component) and a doubled page listener (index.js sets attributes at 56-63 THEN calls `wireCard` at 68 — if `wireCard` runs twice on a re-render path, that doubles). (b) `asset.update` route (`service-worker.js:5710`) builds `canonicalOperationTarget("asset", {origin, id})`, which yields no target for `id:""`, so `requireOwnerApproval` (3288-3290) returns "This operation requires owner approval." — the readable message already exists in `artifacts.js:712` but is never reached. What must NOT change: the approval gate for valid ids.
  - Reproduce today: (1) build; seed an artifact; open Artifacts; count `Target.getTargets` pages matching `artifact/artifact.html` before/after ONE click on New tab → 0 → 2. (2) From the lazy protocol send `update_asset {origin:"master", id:"", content:"x"}` → `{"error":"This operation requires owner approval.","ok":false}`.
  - Files: `extension/shared/components.js` (`ArtifactCard._wire` 2234), `extension/artifacts/index.js` (`wireCard` 99; the render loop 50-78), `extension/background/service-worker.js` (`asset.update` 5710), `tests/artifact-newtab.test.ts`, `tests/artifacts.test.ts`, `scripts/chrome-journeys.ts`.
  - Steps: (1) Add a journey check that counts viewer targets after one click (RED). (2) Make `_wire` idempotent with a per-wire `AbortController` (`{signal}` on each `addEventListener`, abort the previous at the top of `_wire`) AND guard `wireCard` with a `WeakSet` of wired cards; re-run the journey (GREEN) and note in History which side was doubling. (3) In `asset.update`, before `canonicalOperationTarget`: `if (typeof id !== "string" || !id) return {ok:false, error:"update_asset needs an existing id (use list_assets)"}`; after the gate, map `updateAsset`'s "asset not found" to the same sentence. (4) Unit tests.

Falsification: revert step 2, expect RED on "exactly one"; revert step 3, expect RED on "readable message"; restore both, GREEN.

title: [CAP-FB-20260830-FINGERPRINT-SURFACE-01] Every website can fingerprint the extension
description:
## [CAP-FB-20260830-FINGERPRINT-SURFACE-01] Every website can fingerprint the extension
- Feedback: 2026-08-30 — reanalysis 2026-08-30 security lane finding 7. Any web page can detect that the extension is installed by fetching one of its web-accessible files or by reading a named global the detector defines.
- Updated: 2026-08-30 14:30 UTC
- Status: OPEN
- Resume: —
- Priority: P2
- Owner: unassigned
- Workspace: none
- Branch: none
- Base: `cf0da958`
- Candidate: —
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: `web_accessible_resources` no longer exposes `artifact/artifact.html`, `artifact/artifact.js` or `sandbox/artifact-preview.html` to `<all_urls>` (extension pages do not need a web match; if one is ever needed, `use_dynamic_url: true`); the MAIN-world detector hook is a per-document unguessable name (or a Symbol on a private object) rather than a non-configurable named global; a `fetch` of the resource from a web page fails and the global is absent, asserted in the browser.
  - Context: `extension/manifest.json` `web_accessible_resources` (the block at ~`:91-101`) lists the three files with `"matches": ["<all_urls>"]`. A page can `fetch("chrome-extension://<id>/artifact/artifact.js")` or iframe the viewer; `extension/artifact/artifact.js:14-16` reads `id`/`origin` from the query string and `:53` calls `send("asset.get", { origin, id })` for whatever it is given (the SW's sender check limits what a page can reach, but the existence probe succeeds). `extension/content/webmcp-detect-main.js:92-97` defines `globalThis[HOOK_KEY]` with `writable:false, configurable:false` on every page in the MAIN world; the WebMCP acceptance suite (`scripts/webmcp-acceptance.ts`) depends on the hook for the relay handshake. What must NOT change: the relay's HMAC/nonce handshake (`extension/content/bridge-auth.js`, `webmcp-detect-relay.js`); the artifact viewer's own extension-page use.
  - Reproduce today: (1) build, launch headless with the extension; open any http(s) page; (2) in the page: `fetch("chrome-extension://" + <id> + "/artifact/artifact.js").then(r => r.status)` → 200; (3) `typeof globalThis.__capWebmcpDetectBootstrap` → "function" (read `HOOK_KEY` in `webmcp-detect-main.js` for the exact name).
  - Files: `extension/manifest.json` (delete the `web_accessible_resources` entry, or restrict `matches` to nothing web-facing and set `use_dynamic_url: true`; verify the artifact viewer still opens from `artifacts/index.html` and the ntp — `git grep -n "artifact/artifact.html" -- extension`); `extension/content/webmcp-detect-main.js:92-97` and the isolated-world relay that calls the hook (`extension/content/webmcp-detect-relay.js`) — pass the hook name via the relay's nonce channel so it is per-document; `scripts/webmcp-acceptance.ts` if it references the global by name. Do NOT touch the bridge auth.
  - Steps: 1. Browser checks first (Gates) — RED. 2. Manifest change; confirm the viewer and preview still work from extension pages (`npm run test:chrome`). 3. title: [CAP-FB-20260828-AMBIENT-SITE-TOOLS-01] Site tools should be available on the tab, not pre-registered in Settings
description:
## [CAP-FB-20260828-AMBIENT-SITE-TOOLS-01] Site tools should be available on the tab, not pre-registered in Settings
- Feedback: 2026-08-28 — product owner, restating the product thesis: "WebMCP is that every single website can be a tool that can be used in the future because that's what the web is". Today the product makes you enroll a site first, which is a configuration step in front of the most distinctive thing it does
- Updated: 2026-08-28 02:00 UTC
- Status: ABANDONED
- Priority: P2
- Owner: unassigned
- Workspace: none
- Branch: none
- Base: `d551074b`
- Candidate: `extension/lib/site-adapters.js` + `tests/site-adapters.test.ts` — the pure adapter format. Source-only; nothing is wired to a route, a page or the bridge yet
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: **(1) Availability follows real tools, not registration.** Starting a task on a tab whose page actually offers tools makes those tools available to that task WITHOUT a prior enrollment step. "Actually offers tools" means exactly one of: the page declares WebMCP tools, or the existing bridge INFERS tools from functions exposed in the page's global scope, including their input semantics. A site with neither is not shown and is not interactable — the product never implies a site is usable when it is not. **(2) The registry persists and is a history, not a live-tab list.** A site that has offered tools stays recorded with what it offered and when, so the owner can see and reference it with the tab closed; registration is not conditional on the tab being open. **(3)** Starting a task on such a tab does not require a prior enrollment step — the owner approves the tool's USE in the moment (the in-context approval path that already exists since `0.2.303`), rather than pre-registering the origin in Settings. Enrollment remains available as an explicit, persistent choice for sites the owner wants standing access to, and the existing per-tool first-run approval, origin-keyed memory and grant scoping are unchanged: this changes WHEN the owner is asked, not WHETHER, and grants no new authority. The Settings → Site agents list becomes a management view of standing enrollments rather than the way you get any site tools at all
- Review: fresh-session review; this touches the enrollment/authorization boundary, so a security-focused pass over the grant scoping is required, plus real-browser verification on a genuine WebMCP page
- Gates: full unit suite; Chrome journeys green; `npm run test:webmcp` acceptance; the security suite; a11y pass on the in-context approval
- Blockers: —
- Next: nothing. Superseded by "auto WebMCP" when the owner returns to it — see the successor note in History
- Recover: `git grep -n "enroll" -- extension/lib/site-agents.js extension/options/options.js | head`
- History:
  - 2026-08-28 06:15 UTC — **ABANDONED by owner decision.** Owner: "I don't want webmcpExpose, I want you to find JS defined functions on a page and expose them... but lets just drop this and ensure that webMCP code paths work and not general. We will get back to 'auto webmcp' later." The adapter approach answered the wrong question: the owner does not want to hand-author a description of a site, they want the platform to DISCOVER a page's callable functions itself. That is the blind global-scope inference the round-28 review removed, so bringing it back is a security question in its own right and gets its own task when the owner returns to it — not a variant of this one.
  - 2026-08-28 06:15 UTC — the adapter format and its 18 KATs are REMOVED from the tree rather than left shipping unwired, because an unreferenced module is exactly the dead-code class already tracked as `CAP-FB-20260828-DEAD-COMPONENTS-01` and `-DEAD-SURFACES-01`. Nothing is lost: the complete design, the closed five-op vocabulary and every property test live at `origin/main@4ed8cf8a` (`0.2.328`) and can be restored with `git checkout 4ed8cf8a -- extension/lib/site-adapters.js tests/site-adapters.test.ts`. The reasoning that produced it — why an adapter had to be declarative rather than code (MV3 CSP plus prompt-injection escalation) — applies to any future auto-discovery design and is recorded in that commit message.
  - 2026-08-28 03:30 UTC — **owner decision on the fork, then the first increment landed as source.** The owner's description of inference ("look at exposed functions in the global scope") describes REMOVED behaviour: blind `window.*` enumeration was cut by the round-28 review because every enumerable global function became a tool, and today inference requires the page to set `window.webmcpExpose`. So in the wild almost nothing qualifies. Presented three options; the owner chose **owner-authored site adapters**: the owner (or an agent, as a proposal) declares a site's tools, so any site becomes usable without waiting for its author, and nothing is inferred blindly.
  - 2026-08-28 03:30 UTC — `extension/lib/site-adapters.js` (pure) + 18 KATs. **An adapter is DECLARATIVE, not code**, forced by two constraints: MV3 CSP means the bundle has no `eval`/`new Function` so we could not execute authored JavaScript without breaking the extension's central security claim; and a model that can author executable page script has escalated from "calls approved tools" to "runs arbitrary code in the page". So there is a CLOSED five-op vocabulary — `callGlobal`, `readText`, `readAttribute`, `click`, `fill` — and the worst a malicious proposal can express is an operation the owner can read and refuse. Four properties are asserted directly and each was FALSIFIED (the property test shown failing against a deliberately weakened module, then restored): the vocabulary is closed (unknown kinds AND unknown fields both refuse); an op may only reference a parameter the tool DECLARES; nothing is executable until an explicit owner act, and `ownerApproved` must be exactly `true` (truthy is refused) with re-validation so tampered stored bytes cannot be approved; and no path interprets a string as code. Also: `callGlobal.fn` must be a bare identifier — no dotted paths or bracket access — and an origin is one exact origin with no wildcard, path, query or credentials.
  - 2026-08-28 03:30 UTC — **the tests caught two real bugs in my own design, both the same class.** `approveAdapter` deliberately re-validates the stored document rather than trusting its bytes, which only works if canonical output is valid input. Canonicalisation writes `label:""` and `description:""`, and the bounded-string helper rejects the empty string — so every adapter without a label, and every adapter containing a description-less tool, was impossible to approve. Fixed, and pinned by an explicit round-trip property test that also asserts canonicalisation is idempotent. A third: the selector filter banned `>`, which is the CSS child combinator, so ordinary selectors like `#buy > .cta` were rejected.
  - 2026-08-28 02:40 UTC — **owner constraints on the design, recorded before implementation.** (a) Sites must be registrable and visible with the tab CLOSED — the registry is a durable history of sites that have had functionality, not a view of currently-open tabs; killing the tab must not lose the record of what that site could do. (b) A site is only visible and interactable when it genuinely has tools: either declared WebMCP tools, or tools INFERRED through the existing bridge by inspecting functions exposed in the page's global scope and deriving their input semantics. Sites with neither must not appear as usable. So this is not "every site is an agent" — it is "every site that actually offers tools is usable without a setup step, and we remember which ones did".
  - 2026-08-28 02:00 UTC — captured from the owner's restatement of the product thesis, and from a gap between that thesis and the shipped UI. The product's most distinctive claim is that the web itself becomes the toolset. The shipped flow is a configuration model: Settings → Site agents, a "Discovered open pages — click to add site" box, a curated enrolled list, and a hub card that reads "No Site Agents yet. Find tools from an open tab to add one." Every one of those puts a setup step between the user and the capability. This is the largest gap between what the product IS and how it presents itself, and before now it was not tracked as anything — the existing site-agent entries (`SITE-DISCOVERABILITY-01`, `PROACTIVE-TAB-DISCOVERY-01`, `SITE-AGENT-SHOWCASE-01`) all improve the enrollment flow rather than question whether enrollment should be the front door.

description:
## [CAP-FB-20260825-KEYBOARD-COMMANDS-01] No keyboard shortcuts anywhere
- Feedback: 2026-08-25 — independent gap review found the manifest declares no `commands`, so a power-user tool aimed at people who return to it repeatedly across a day cannot be reached or driven from the keyboard
- Updated: 2026-08-25 17:10 UTC
- Status: DONE
- Resume: —
- Priority: P2
- Owner: claude-opus-5 implementer session
- Workspace: active (local path private)
- Branch: detached candidate on `origin/main`
- Base: `784cd7f7275a7f63db856ee4231e523700bc861b`
- Candidate: this commit
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: a small, deliberate set of shortcuts — open the hub, start a task, open the side panel, focus the composer — declared in the manifest, remappable through Chrome's own shortcut settings, and discoverable in-product; the set is small enough to be memorable rather than exhaustive; no shortcut fires a destructive or permission-granting action; nothing conflicts with a common browser default
- Review: author self-review 2026-08-25 (findings recorded in History and fixed); **no independent review** — the product owner asked the author to review directly
- Gates: 18/18 loaded-MV3 checks on a fresh profile — `chrome.commands.getAll()` reports all three with real bound chords; `#compose` focuses the composer on BOTH the already-open-tab path and the fresh-tab boot path; no command injects task text; the side-panel command finds `sidePanel` ungranted and fails closed without requesting it; Settings lists the chords Chrome actually reports. Plus 6 unit tests, full unit suite, gallery drift, changelog and tasks-schema gates
- Blockers: —
- Next: an independent pass on the permission and payload constraints if one becomes cheap; otherwise closed
- Recover: `git grep -n "KEYBOARD_COMMANDS\|hubUrlForCommand" -- extension && python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('extension/manifest.json'))['commands'])"`
- History:
  - 2026-08-25 17:10 UTC — **AUTHOR SELF-REVIEW, not the independent review the lifecycle requires.** The product owner asked for the review directly, so it was done by the same session that wrote the change. Recorded as such: a self-review cannot cover what the author was blind to, which is the whole point of the different-model rule. Four defects were found across the three changes and fixed in one commit; details in each entry below. An independent pass is still worth having on the permission and payload constraints.
  - 2026-08-25 17:10 UTC — self-review found one defect. **MEDIUM:** the side-panel command's permission guard did not guard — `chrome.permissions?.contains?.(…).catch(…)` yields `undefined` when `contains` is missing and `.catch` on `undefined` throws, so the fail-closed-with-a-reason path could never run in precisely the situation it existed for. Rewritten as try/catch with an explicit `=== true`; the active-tab lookup had the same shape and was fixed with it. Re-verified 18/18 in a loaded extension afterwards. Fixed in `6320fd8`.
  - 2026-08-25 14:10 UTC — implemented and verified in a real loaded extension. Three commands: `open-hub` (`Alt+Shift+H`), `new-task` (`Alt+Shift+K`, lands on the hub with the composer focused) and `open-side-panel` (`Alt+Shift+S`). The acceptance named four; "start a task" and "focus the composer" collapse into the same action, so shipping a fourth redundant chord was rejected rather than padded to match the wording.
  - 2026-08-25 14:10 UTC — **the browser run caught two real defects that source review would not have.** (1) Chrome SILENTLY DROPPED `Alt+Shift+A`, `Alt+Shift+N`, `Alt+Shift+T` and `Alt+Shift+C` — a dropped `suggested_key` produces no error and no binding, so the shortcuts would simply never have fired. The shipped chords were chosen by probing what Chrome actually binds, not by reading a reserved-key list. (2) `#compose` did nothing when a hub tab was already open: setting the hash is a `push` navigation and `shouldDispatchForNavigationType` deliberately suppresses those, so the router never saw it. A `hashchange` listener now handles that one focus-only route; it touches no view state, so it cannot race the dispatcher.
  - 2026-08-25 14:10 UTC — constraints enforced in code, not just documented: no command is destructive; none calls `chrome.permissions.request` (a key chord is not a gesture aimed at a specific grant, so a prompt from one would be a consent dark pattern); the side-panel command checks `permissions.contains` and fails closed with an actionable diagnostic; no command carries a payload, so a shortcut can never inject task text. Settings renders `chrome.commands.getAll()` rather than the manifest's suggested keys, so it stays truthful after an owner remaps or clears a binding.

  - 2026-08-25 09:40 UTC — opened. Verified absent: `extension/manifest.json` contains no `commands` key.

title: The quiet-window harness pins are satisfied by their own import bindings — re-anchor the refusal handler they name
description:
Carved out of chrome-agent-platform-wzez (CLOSED, census delivered and independently verified) as the
audit's actionable tail. Coord assignment 2026-09-07 21:59Z: "take the 3 DEFEATABLE quiet-window
re-anchors as your bead (small, closes the class)". Owner: qwen (01a07d6e). Sequenced AFTER
chrome-agent-platform-c9y8's verdict — this bead touches tests/quiet-window.test.ts only, so there is
no file overlap with c9y8, but the guard extension is what makes these three pins visible to the
committed guard, so landing order matters for the story even if not for the merge.

THE FINDING (census row, mutation-confirmed as mutant W2). Three source-text pins in
tests/quiet-window.test.ts, inside the loop at :327 that walks the harnesses declaring themselves
load-sensitive:

    const src = Deno.readTextFileSync(`${ROOT}scripts/${file}`);
    assert(src.includes("QuietWindowRefusedError"),      `${file} must handle the refusal`);        // :328
    assert(src.includes("ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_EXIT"),   `${file} must exit with the environmental code`); // :329
    assert(src.includes("ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_MARKER"), `${file} must print the marker line`);     // :330

The loop currently has exactly ONE member: `declared` is
`Object.entries(HARNESSES).filter(([, e]) => e.loadSensitive !== undefined)` over
scripts/lib/harness-registry.ts, and only `"chrome-journeys.ts"` declares loadSensitive (verified by
hand at 4c89bd9d — harness-registry.ts:65 is the single occurrence). So all three pins judge
scripts/chrome-journeys.ts, where each token occurs exactly TWICE: once as an import binding at
:34-36 and once in live code at :136-139.

That makes all three DEFEATABLE on the census ladder: live > 0 and shadow > 0, so deleting the live
construct leaves the import behind and the pin stays green.

PROVEN, NOT INFERRED (mutant W2, house discipline, restored + re-hashed + empty git status):
delete the five-line refusal handler at scripts/chrome-journeys.ts:136-140 —

    if (e instanceof QuietWindowRefusedError) {
      console.error(e.message);
      console.error(`${ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_MARKER} ${JSON.stringify(e.sample)}`);
      Deno.exit(ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_EXIT);
    }

leaving `throw e;` and the three imports. Each token drops from 2 occurrences to 1 (import only).
`deno check --no-lock scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` reports 625 errors both at baseline and with the
mutant, i.e. no new syntax or type error (esbuild is unusable in this environment — rc=1 at baseline
too — recorded rather than hidden). Result: tests/quiet-window.test.ts went 13/0 -> 12 passed / 1
FAILED.

THE IMPORTANT HALF: the kill came from :347 "mkax: the REAL journey gate refuses with exit 75 under
artificial load" — an EXECUTING gate that runs the real harness under artificial load and asserts the
environmental exit code. The test that HOLDS the three substring pins, "mkax: load-sensitive harnesses
DECLARE themselves, and the declaration is honoured in source", PASSED with the handler deleted. So the
property is NOT a live hole, and this bead is hygiene, not firefighting: three pins that name a safety
property (an environmental refusal must reach a THIRD exit code with a greppable marker, never be
re-read as a product red) cannot see the deletion of the construct they name, and are backstopped only
by a slower, load-dependent, Chrome-launching gate.

Lesson recorded on wzez and worth repeating here: DEFEATABLE means "a shadow can satisfy this pin",
NOT "this feature is deletable". Only a whole-suite mutant separates those, which is why this bead
exists at P3 and not P2.

WHAT TO DO. Re-anchor the three pins on the CONSTRUCT, parsed rather than grepped, following the shape
ecke landed for bundled-inventory-data (816aae8e) and uodl landed for recordServerToolUsage /
buildTemplateSelect:

1. Pin the handler SHAPE, not the three words: the refusal must be caught by type, must print the
   marker, and must exit with the environmental code — e.g. a single anchored regex over the catch
   body covering `instanceof QuietWindowRefusedError` … `ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_MARKER` …
   `Deno.exit(ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_EXIT)`, or three assertions each anchored on its own construct
   (the instanceof test, the marker print statement, the exit call) rather than on the bare identifier.
2. KEEP IT GENERIC. The assertion runs once per member of `declared`, and a second harness can declare
   itself load-sensitive at any time, so the anchor must describe the required shape (catch the typed
   refusal, print the marker, exit with the code) and must not hardcode chrome-journeys.ts's
   surrounding lines. A pin that only matches today's single member is a pin that silently stops
   covering the next one.
3. Decide explicitly whether the three bare-word pins stay as provenance (the ecke/template-cards
   precedent) or are replaced. If they stay, they stay DEFEATABLE by construction and the committed
   guard will not flag them (live > 0), so say which it is in a comment rather than leaving both nets
   ambiguous.
4. Note for whoever implements: regex literals carrying a backtick or a quote are safe here — the
   guard tokenises regex literals properly (that was the audit's defect #5, and 222 regexes across 21
   target files depend on it).

ACCEPTANCE.
* Mutant W2 RE-RUN and killed BY THE PINS: with the five-line handler deleted, the test that holds
  them — "mkax: load-sensitive harnesses DECLARE themselves, and the declaration is honoured in
  source" — must FAIL, not merely the executing exit-75 gate at :347. Name the killing assertion and
  its message in the report, per house discipline.
* The restored tree must go green again (13/0), with the pristine hash of scripts/chrome-journeys.ts
  re-verified (4f8c205f2e1862d67c1c57799e58e9e3ed38fc9f33dc373865038f4d2aec1272 at 4c89bd9d) and an
  empty `git status --porcelain`.
* Generality proven, not asserted: a second mutant that adds a FAKE harness member declaring
  loadSensitive without the handler shape must be caught by the re-anchored pin, or the pin must be
  documented as single-member-only with the reason. Otherwise the re-anchor is a pin on today's file
  rather than on the declaration rule.
* Repo gates: `npm run build:production` BEFORE `npm run test:changed` in a fresh worktree (the
  store-map tests read the STORE dist.complete marker; a developer-only build leaves it stale and they
  fail with "marker indexed source authority is stale" — environment, not coverage), then `npm test`
  once before push. Post-commit, re-run `npm run check:changelog` and
  `npm run test:file -- tests/changelog.test.ts` — the bump hook writes the changelog entry AFTER the
  gates.
* CAUTION for stage 2: this file's own suite launches Chrome (the exit-75 gate at :347), and
  tests/security-suite-custody.test.ts flocks the machine-global
  /tmp/cap-serialized-chrome-acceptance.lock on a 20s self-timed budget, so a concurrent lane running
  Chrome KATs can red it for everyone. Its failure is NOT a kill. Re-run at rest before believing it.
* Independent review by a different model; push an explicit SHA, never the local main ref.
* NO mass rewrite: three pins in one file. The census's WEAK-STRING rows, build-artifact class and
  interpolated-token class are DECISIONS batched to coord/Paul and are explicitly not part of this bead.

EVIDENCE. cap-evidence/uodl/census-4c89bd9d/CENSUS.md §6 (adjudication + W2), mutation/
mutation-results.json (both mutants, full discipline record), census-attribution.json rows for
tests/quiet-window.test.ts:328-330 (DEFEATABLE, live=1 shadow=1 each, with occurrence lines). The
extended guard from chrome-agent-platform-c9y8 now attributes these three pins, so after this bead
lands they should stop appearing as DEFEATABLE in any future census re-run.
notes:
CLAIMED by qwen (01a07d6e) per coord's assignment 2026-09-07 21:59Z, but implementation is HELD until chrome-agent-platform-c9y8's review verdict lands (glm-flash-1 is running it; coord: 'Route the commit when glm's verdict lands'). No file overlap with c9y8 — this bead touches tests/quiet-window.test.ts only — so the hold is sequencing, not a conflict. Preparation staged meanwhile: the re-anchor must stay GENERIC (the loop walks whatever harnesses declare loadSensitive, today exactly one) and the acceptance includes a second mutant that adds a fake loadSensitive member WITHOUT the handler shape, so the pin is proven to cover the declaration rule rather than today's single file. Mutant W2 is already written and proven in cap-evidence/uodl/census-4c89bd9d/mutation/mutation-results.json (delete the 5-line handler at scripts/chrome-journeys.ts:136-140 -> the pin-holding test 'mkax: load-sensitive harnesses DECLARE themselves...' PASSED while the executing exit-75 gate at :347 killed it, 12/1). Pristine hash to re-verify on restore: 4f8c205f2e1862d67c1c57799e58e9e3ed38fc9f33dc373865038f4d2aec1272.
IMPLEMENTED, BOTH MUTANTS KILLED, GATES GREEN — CANDIDATE 07c05d45 on cap-beads-lrok (qwen, 01a07d6e, 2026-09-07). Committed locally, NOT pushed; awaiting independent review by a different model. One file changed: tests/quiet-window.test.ts (+27/-3). No product source touched — scripts/chrome-journeys.ts is unchanged and its hash re-verified (4f8c205f2e1862d67c1c57799e58e9e3ed38fc9f33dc373865038f4d2aec1272). Base 37c71f14 (origin/main at branch time). Worktree /home/paulkinlan/worktrees/cap-lrok, clean; setup npm ci + deno install + npm run build + npm run build:production all rc=0.

THE CHANGE. The three bare-word pins are replaced by three anchored pins that must be satisfied INSIDE the refusal handler:
  /instanceof\s+QuietWindowRefusedError\s*\)/                                                  -> "must catch the refusal BY TYPE — an import binding is not a handler"
  /instanceof\s+QuietWindowRefusedError\s*\)[\s\S]{0,400}?ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_MARKER/        -> "must print the greppable marker from inside the refusal handler"
  /instanceof\s+QuietWindowRefusedError\s*\)[\s\S]{0,400}?Deno\.exit\(\s*ENVIRONMENTAL_REFUSAL_EXIT\s*\)/ -> "must exit with the environmental code from inside the refusal handler"
The import block cannot satisfy any of them (no `instanceof`, no `Deno.exit(`), and the 400-char bounds mean a marker printed in an unrelated statement cannot either. Three separate assertions keep three separate messages, so a failure names which half of the refusal is missing. The imports stay unpinned on purpose — provenance is the module's job, these prove USE. Nothing in the anchors is specific to chrome-journeys.ts, so the pin stays generic across whatever harnesses declare loadSensitive.

W2 — THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION, MET. Delete the five-line handler at scripts/chrome-journeys.ts:136-140, leaving `throw e;` and the three imports. Count-verify: block unique; each token 2 -> 1 occurrence (import only); diff 1 file, 5 deletions. Parse differential for a .ts target: `deno check --no-lock scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` -> Found 625 errors at BASELINE and 625 with the mutant (no new syntax/type error); esbuild is unusable in this environment (rc=1 at baseline too), recorded rather than hidden. RESULT: the pin-holding test "mkax: load-sensitive harnesses DECLARE themselves, and the declaration is honoured in source" now FAILS at :299 with "chrome-journeys.ts must catch the refusal BY TYPE — an import binding is not a handler". Before this change that test PASSED under W2 and the only kill came from the executing gate at :371. The executing gate still fails too, as expected. Restored, hash re-verified, tree clean, restored run 13/0.

W4 — GENERALITY, PROVEN. Two targeted edits make scripts/a11y-audit.ts a second declarer with no handler: `requireQuiet: true` added to its launchChrome call (:48) and a `loadSensitive` reason (>40 chars, marked as a mutant fixture) added to its scripts/lib/harness-registry.ts entry (:70). Both halves of the set-equality assertion then agree, so the loop is reached. RESULT: FAILS at :299 with "a11y-audit.ts must catch the refusal BY TYPE — an import binding is not a handler" — the anchored pin covers the DECLARATION RULE, not today's single member. Notable: the executing exit-75 gate PASSED under W4 (12 passed / 1 failed), because it only runs chrome-journeys — so a new declarer with no handler is caught by these pins and by nothing else. That is coverage the re-anchor adds rather than duplicates. Both edits reverted; both hashes re-verified; tree carries only the intended test-file change.

GATES. Restored tree: tests/quiet-window.test.ts 13 passed / 0 failed (3s). npm run test:changed rc=0 (425 files, parallel phase GREEN in 35s, wall 122s). npm test rc=0: serial 15 files 154/0 in 87s, parallel 410 files 4007/0 in 30s, 425 files total, wall 117s. Post-commit per the bump-writes-the-entry-after-the-gates lesson: npm run check:changelog "changelog in sync" and npm run test:file -- tests/changelog.test.ts 9/0. Bump 0.3.318 -> 0.3.319. Fresh-worktree trap honoured: build:production ran BEFORE test:changed, otherwise the two store-map tests in tests/bundled-tool-packages.test.ts red on a stale store dist.complete marker (environment, not coverage).

LANDING NOTE: three unpushed candidates now share the base 37c71f14 and each took a version — c9y8 is at 0.3.320 (rebased, then bumped by its review-fix commit), canon at 0.3.319, lrok at 0.3.319. Whichever lands second and third need the routine renumber; no content conflicts (c9y8 touches tests/substring-pin-honesty.test.ts, canon touches AGENTS.md, lrok touches tests/quiet-window.test.ts — three disjoint files).

SCOPE DISCIPLINE: this closes the census's actionable tail. The WEAK-STRING rows (bundled-tool-packages:314/315, chrome-slot-semaphore:418), the build-artifact class and the interpolated-token class are owner DECISIONS batched to coord/Paul and are deliberately untouched. After c9y8's guard extension lands, these three pins stop being `.includes` pins at all (they are regex pins now), so the three DEFEATABLE rows disappear from any future census re-run.

FOR THE CLOSE (coord, 2026-09-07 22:39Z: 'The W4 finding is the piece that makes this more than hygiene — worth calling out in the bead's close'). W4 IS NOT A DUPLICATE OF THE EXECUTING GATE, AND THAT IS THE POINT: when a SECOND harness declares itself load-sensitive without a refusal handler (mutant W4: requireQuiet:true added to scripts/a11y-audit.ts plus a loadSensitive reason in scripts/lib/harness-registry.ts, so both halves of the set-equality assertion agree and the loop is reached), the re-anchored pin FAILS naming that file — while the executing gate 'mkax: the REAL journey gate refuses with exit 75 under artificial load' PASSES (12 passed / 1 failed), because it only ever runs scripts/chrome-journeys.ts. So before this change a new declarer with no handler was caught by NOTHING: the three substring pins were satisfied by whatever imports the new file happened to carry (or passed vacuously if it carried none of the three words... they would fail, but only as a word check, not as a handler check), and the executing gate never looked at it. After this change the declaration RULE is pinned for every member of declared, present and future. That converts the bead from hygiene (three weak nets backstopped by a slower gate) into added coverage (the only net that scales with the registry). REVIEW ROUTED: cap-arch-docs (gemini, different model) at candidate 07c05d45, with both mutants as falsification paths and an explicit invitation to attack the 400-char bounds for a shape that satisfies the anchors without actually exiting 75. Deliberately NOT self-rebased: hand-resolving a CHANGELOG/version collision is merger's routine, and moving a sha mid-review is what made the c9y8 handoff confusing.

title: Decode filesystem file-URL roots in Chrome acceptance harnesses
description: During nwhc/browser preparation, scripts/chrome-journeys.ts:13 and scripts/kat-wasi-tranche2.ts:7 were read and still derive ROOT via new URL("..", import.meta.url).pathname. URL.pathname retains percent encodings; the source-pinned nwhc same-expression Node counter demonstrated /cap%20checkout/ != decoded /cap checkout/. These unchanged harness expressions are susceptible to the same filesystem-root problem with spaces/nonASCII paths. No Chrome run from a spaced checkout has been performed; this is a source-level portability finding, not an observed browser gate RED or execution escape. Existing current379 checkout has no such characters. Scope: use standard fileURLToPath for these filesystem roots and add persistent spaced/nonASCII path controls. Preserve canonical launcher, port0, waitForServiceWorker, registered lock/semaphore/quiet-window settings, exact behavior/assertions, evidence/cleanup boundaries, and WASI caller arguments. Do not modify the active admission candidate for this follow-up; no blocking dependency on woem or current Chrome set. title: Census the 203 unattributed source-text substring pins — population count, not fixes
description:
Follow-up carved out of chrome-agent-platform-uodl, which is complete and landed. SCOPE IS A CENSUS, NOT A FIX CAMPAIGN. The uodl audit attributed 654 source-text .includes(X) pins to a target file and adjudicated them; 203 further source-like .includes calls were NOT attributed and are absent from every number the audit reported. They reach their variable through a helper function, a destructured return, or an interpolation the scanner declines to guess. This is the audit's honest boundary and the largest remaining coverage hole: the true population is bigger than 654, so any claim of the form 'the repo has N weak substring pins' is currently unbounded from below.

WHY IT IS A SEPARATE BEAD. uodl's acceptance forbade mass-rewriting the corpus, and its findings were proven by mutation one at a time. Extending attribution is a different kind of work: it is measurement, and it must not become a rewrite. Splitting it keeps that boundary explicit.

title: Audit the repo's source-text substring pins — an includes() assertion is satisfied by a comment or an import, and two proven instances let a dropped ?toolautosubmit and a removed withTimeout bound survive the full suite
description:
A proven-weak pin pattern, found by the caller mutation sweep (er6x) and worth
auditing repo-wide because it is cheap to detect and silently defeats the guard
it claims to hold.

THE PATTERN: a test reads a source file and asserts
`sourceText.includes("<token>")`. That assertion is satisfied by ANY occurrence
of the token in the file — including a COMMENT describing the behaviour and an
IMPORT that is never used at the relevant call site.

TWO PROVEN INSTANCES, both in tests/kat-bistro-finalizer.test.ts against
scripts/kat-webmcp-bistro.ts, both surviving a FULL `npm test` run:

1. `assert(scriptText.includes("?toolautosubmit"), "KAT must append
   ?toolautosubmit")`. Mutant U1 removed `?toolautosubmit` from `URL_BISTRO`, so
   the demo no longer auto-submits its tool step — the entire reason the harness
   exists. The pin still passed, because the file's HEADER COMMENT says "Bounded
   execution with ?toolautosubmit, CDP interception, and clean process
   lifecycle". A comment about a guarantee satisfied the guarantee's pin.
2. `assert(scriptText.includes("withTimeout"), "KAT must bound execution with
   withTimeout")`. Mutant U16 removed the `withTimeout(...)` wrapper from the
   success invocation, leaving it UNBOUNDED. The pin still passed, because the
   import line and the teardown field both contain the word. A bound that no
   longer existed was reported as present.

Both are now killed by anchored pins (er6x): match the DECLARATION or the CALL
SITE and parse it — `const URL_BISTRO = "..."` then `new URL(...).searchParams
.has("toolautosubmit")`, and `const strRes = await withTimeout(...)` with the
numeric bound captured and range-checked.

SCALE, measured on ea037b90 — NOT a claim that all of these are vulnerable:
1119 `.includes(` assertions across the test files that read a source file, the
largest concentrations being tests/components.test.ts (74),
tests/conversation-status-ui.test.ts (68), tests/bundled-tool-packages.test.ts
(56), tests/durable-runs.test.ts (50), tests/kat-bistro-finalizer.test.ts (43).
Most are legitimate: many assert on HTML or generated content where the token
genuinely cannot appear in a comment, and many are checking that user-facing copy
exists. The vulnerable class is narrow and mechanically detectable.

THE AUDIT, which is the point of this bead. For every source-text `.includes(X)`
pin, resolve the target file and check whether X ALSO occurs inside a comment or
an import line of that file. Where it does, the pin can be satisfied without the
guarded code existing at all, and it must be re-anchored to a declaration or call
site. That is a static analysis over the test corpus — no browser, no mutation
runs needed to produce the candidate list. Then confirm the interesting hits the
cheap way: mutate the guarded construct, run the pin, and see whether it notices.
er6x's driver (cap-evidence/bistro-caller-sweep/caller-sweep.py +
kill-verify-caller.py) is a working template for that confirm step.

ACCEPTANCE.
  * A written inventory: every source-text substring pin whose token also appears
    in a comment or import of its target file, with the file, the line, the
    token, and where else it occurs.
  * A severity ranking — pins on SAFETY or HONESTY guards (exit codes, receipt
    announcement, error capture, bounds, path sanitization, evidence location)
    outrank pins on copy or layout, because a silently defeated safety guard is
    how a false GREEN ships.
  * Re-anchored replacements for the safety-critical hits, each proven by
    mutation: the mutant the old pin missed must now be killed.
  * A lintable rule or a scanner test so the pattern does not come back — e.g. a
    committed guard that fails when a source-text `.includes(X)` pin has X
    occurring in a comment of the target file. Note the repo already has static
    tree-scanning guards of exactly this shape (tests/durable-root.test.ts,
    tests/harness-debug-port.test.ts), so the mechanism is established.
  * Do not mass-rewrite the 1119. Fix the vulnerable class; leave the rest alone.

Related: er6x (the caller pins this was found by), 2b6a (the finalizer sweep; its
own lesson was "a test NAME is not coverage" — two committed tests named for
guards their injected seams did not actually exercise). This bead is the third
instance of the same underlying theme: the shape of a pin is not the same thing
as what it proves.
acceptance_criteria: A written inventory of every source-text substring pin whose token also occurs in a comment or import of its target file, with file/line/token/other-occurrence. A severity ranking with safety and honesty guards (exit codes, receipt announcement, error capture, bounds, path sanitization, evidence location) above copy and layout. Re-anchored replacements for the safety-critical hits, each proven by mutation. A committed scanner guard so the pattern cannot return. Do NOT mass-rewrite the 1119 includes() assertions — fix only the vulnerable class.
notes:
uodl audit — split-before-mutation done, 3 real false greens found, 2 were LIVE HOLES. Commit 991bf5e2 on cap-launch-sweep-r2 (worktree), gates green, NOT pushed, awaiting independent review.

SEVEN MORE SCANNER DEFECTS (#5-#11), each found by reading what the scanner PRODUCED. #5 is dominant: the mask never tokenised REGEX LITERALS. 222 regexes across 21 target files carry a quote/backtick in a character class (main-world.js:372 /https?:\/\/[^\s"'<>)]+/gi), and each opened a bogus string span. In main-world.js the cascade ran 372->447 and labelled 'function describePageError(...) {' at :420 as a STRING. 489 of 654 pins (75%) live in files with a provably corrupted mask, so the whole P1-P7 ranking was built on sand. Fixed with jstoken.py: real tokeniser (regex-vs-division by previous significant token, quotes stop at a raw newline, ${} interiors are expressions), 33 unit tests.
#6 every export line counted as an import shadow, but 'export async function f()' IS the construct (3 false VACUOUS in the P1 safety list). #7 message extraction matched only "tok", "msg", not the dominant assert(x.includes("tok"), "msg"), so it returned empty and blinded the whole intent analysis. #8 thrown-Error messages counted as shadows: wrong for error CODES (throw new Error("result_stage_write_no_progress")), for fixture payloads (webmcp-errors.html throws the credential it tests), and for refusals (build.mjs) — 6 false VACUOUS; narrowed shadow to console.* narration only. #9 SAFETY_WORDS contains \.\. and every relative import specifier contains ../, so all 7 import pins were ranked SAFETY on a module path. #10 bound names read from the pin's token, so a multi-line import's tail (} from "x") has no braces and webmcp-lazyauth:197 was filed UNCOVERED though the next line pins the call site. #11 BOTH implementations scanned raw test-file text, so the committed guard matched pins inside its own documentation — a re-anchor comment quoting the old assertion. CORRECTION TO THE PRIORITY CALL. The handoff named the SECRET-REDACTION guard (webmcp-honest-errors:31/:33) as highest-value first target. It is NOT a defect. api[_-]?key|token|secret|password occurs in the regex literal it guards -> LIVE -> SOUND. describePageError is a function declaration -> LIVE -> SOUND. redactSecretText is comment-only BUT its own message says 'the port declares its source of truth (keep-in-sync pointer)' — the pin is about the prose on purpose, and the redaction is pinned by the sibling assert(MAIN.includes("function redactBridgeText(")) which is live. * U-E1: delete 'await recordServerToolUsage(billing);' from service-worker.js -> npm test 3977 passed / 0 failed. The provider-server usage record could be removed ENTIRELY and nothing in the repo noticed. provider-server-tools.test.ts:507 pinned the word ESTIMATE, which occurs in that file exactly once, in the comment at :4077.
* U-I1: make the buildTemplateSelect binding dead in ntp.js, import left in place -> also survived the full suite. This is the U16 shape.
* U-U1p (the bead's own U1) survives kat-bistro-finalizer.test.ts 27/0 and is killed by er6x's anchored pin at kat-bistro-caller.test.ts:46 — two-sided proof that the anchored replacement works and the leftover net did not.

THE security-suite-custody DEATHS WERE NOT KILLS. U-U1p and U-I1 each reported one unexpected full-suite failure, the same test, which PASSED under U-E1 and is green in the pristine at-rest baseline. Mechanism read out of the test's own header rather than assumed: its supervisor takes an exclusive flock on the MACHINE-GLOBAL /tmp/cap-serialized-chrome-acceptance.lock and its child's 20s budget counts its own time, so another lane holding the lock starves it. U-U1p's stage 1 ran two Chrome-launching KATs immediately before stage 2; U-E1's stage 1 launched no Chrome. GUARD: tests/substring-pin-honesty.test.ts fails when a source-text .includes(X) pin has no live occurrence of X. Carries its own tokeniser because a naive comment-stripper inherits #5 and would cry wolf on sound pins until disabled. TEETH PROVEN: a probe pin appended to vocabulary.test.ts reddened it naming tests/vocabulary.test.ts:347 with the shadow evidence; removed, green. Runs ~235ms.

title: Three equivalent mutants in the KAT finalizer record redundant or dead code — recorded so they are not mistaken for unpinned guards
description:
Three of the 47 mutants in the guard-by-guard sweep of
scripts/lib/kat-finalizer.ts survived the committed suite AND survived a
19-input divergence probe against pristine — they change no observable
behaviour on any input tried. They are recorded here as code hygiene, explicitly
NOT as coverage gaps: no test is missing, because there is nothing for a test to
pin. They are filed so that nobody later "fixes" them, mistakes them for
unpinned guards, or removes the redundancy without knowing it is redundancy.

B2 — `resultData.state = "RED"` inside the kat.log-write catch is a DEAD
  ASSIGNMENT. The payload is built afterwards as
  `JSON.stringify({ ...resultData, state: finalGreen ? "GREEN" : "RED" })`, so
  the spread always overwrites `state` with the value derived from finalGreen.
  The line can never reach the receipt. The adjacent `finalGreen = false` in the
  same catch IS load-bearing and IS pinned (mutant B1 was killed).

H1 — `finalGreen = false` inside the PUBLISH-failure catch is redundant. That
  catch ends with `exit(1)` and then an explicit
  `return { state: "RED", exitCode: 1, ... receiptPath: null }`, so finalGreen
  is never read again on that path. The explicit return is what makes a returned
  exit seam unable to yield GREEN, and it is pinned (mutants H2/H3/H4/H5 were
  all killed).

A2 — `!poisonDetected` in the isGreen conjunction is redundant TODAY because
  teardownChromeAndProfile sets poisonDetected = true and calls
  recordCleanupError("poison_slot_detected") in the same branch, so a poisoned
  slot always also makes cleanupError non-null and `!cleanupError` already
  forces RED. This one is DEFENCE IN DEPTH rather than dead code, and it is
  worth a deliberate decision: if the coupling between the poison flag and
  recordCleanupError is ever broken, poison detection silently stops forcing
  RED and nothing in the suite would notice (mutant A2 survived both the suite
  and the probe). The cheap fix is a regression that pins poisonDetected
  INDEPENDENTLY of cleanupError — which requires a teardown seam that reports a
  poison detection without a cleanup error, i.e. pinning the coupling itself.

None of the three is a defect. All three are recorded so the sweep's
classification is complete and auditable: 47 mutants = 29 killed by a committed
assertion + 15 genuine coverage gaps (sibling bead) + 3 equivalent mutants
(this bead).
acceptance_criteria: No code change required for B2/H1 (dead/redundant assignments, both provably unobservable). A2 needs a deliberate decision: either keep the poison/cleanupError coupling and pin it with a regression that would fail if the coupling broke, or drop the now-redundant !poisonDetected term knowingly. Record the decision on this bead.

title: A failed receipt publication leaves kat.log on disk still claiming GREEN, contradicting the finalizer's own report-order comment
description:
scripts/lib/kat-finalizer.ts carries a report-order invariant comment that the
landed code does not implement. The comment says:

  // Report-order invariant (coordinator 2026-09-06): no failure may leave an
  // authoritative GREEN result.json. kat.log is written FIRST — a log-write
  // error folds into the final RED result; result.json is written LAST; if
  // the result write fails there is NO valid result (exit 1) and the
  // misleading kat.log is removed best-effort. Teardown has ALWAYS completed
  // by this point.

The publish-failure catch removes only the staged temp:

  try { await removeReportFile(tmpPath); } catch { /* best effort */ }

Nothing removes kat.log. So after a FAILED publication the evidence directory
holds a kat.log that says the run was GREEN, beside a result.json that either
does not exist or belongs to an earlier run.

PROVEN on the real Deno filesystem with EVERY filesystem seam at its production
default (cap-evidence/finalizer-sweep/probe-katlog-residue.ts, output in
probe-katlog-residue.log). The publication is made to fail without touching
permissions: result.json is a NON-EMPTY DIRECTORY, so the atomic rename rejects
with a real OS error. Observed:

  reportError  : "Is a directory (os error 21): rename '<tmp>' -> '<outDir>/result.json'"
  state        : RED            exitCode: 1        receiptPath: null
  exit seam    : called with 1
  dir listing  : ["kat.log", "result.json"]
  kat.log      : "PASS: bistro_loaded\nPASS: order_submitted\nRESULT: 2/2; GREEN\n"
  staged temp  : removed (no .tmp left behind)
  error log    : "FATAL: Failed to publish the KAT result: Is a directory (os error 21): rename '[path]' -> '[path]'"

So the finalizer's own behaviour is CORRECT and fail-closed — RED, exit 1, no
receipt attributable to the run, no orphan temp, and the paths in the log are
masked. The defect is the surviving non-authoritative artifact plus a comment
that claims it is cleaned up.

WHY IT MATTERS EVEN THOUGH kat.log IS NOT AUTHORITATIVE. The receipt-authority
rule is that a path is authoritative only via a non-null receiptPath, and the
caller only prints `KAT receipt:` on that. That holds here. But kat.log is the
human-readable artifact a person or a log-scraping script reads next to the
receipt, and it asserts `RESULT: 2/2; GREEN` for a run that published nothing.
A stale prior result.json in a reused outDir makes it worse: the directory then
reads as a clean GREEN run with a GREEN log and a GREEN receipt, none of which
belong to this invocation.

ACCEPTANCE — this needs an owner decision, so it is filed rather than fixed:
either (a) remove kat.log best-effort in the publish-failure catch, making the
code match the comment, and pin that with a regression that asserts the
directory holds no GREEN-claiming kat.log after a failed publication; or (b)
correct the comment to state that kat.log is deliberately retained as
non-authoritative diagnostic residue, and pin THAT instead so the choice is
explicit. Either way the comment and the code must agree, and whichever
behaviour is chosen must be pinned by a test. Do not leave the contradiction.

No Chrome involved. Found while reading the module for the guard-by-guard
mutation sweep (see the sibling bead for that sweep); it is a reading + real-FS
finding, not a mutation survivor.
acceptance_criteria: The comment and the code must agree, and whichever behaviour is chosen must be pinned by a regression: either remove kat.log best-effort in the publish-failure catch and assert no GREEN-claiming kat.log survives a failed publication, or correct the comment to state that kat.log is deliberately retained as non-authoritative diagnostic residue and pin that. Real-Deno-FS proof already exists (result.json as a non-empty directory makes the atomic rename reject with os error 21 while every filesystem seam stays at its production default).
close_reason: Failed publication cleans up misleading kat.log; pinned by tests/kat-finalizer-log-residue.test.ts, landed @ 7dbc2ede

title: Chrome KAT profiles live inside the repo .cache, so any whole-tree copy races a live browser
description:
Found while de-serializing the Chrome gates (chrome-agent-platform-uzik).

Observed: tests/cdp-client.test.ts:301 copied the whole worktree with `cp -a <repo>/. <scratch>/.` to build a failing-build fixture. During a full `npm test` the copy failed:

  cp: cannot stat '/home/paulkinlan/worktrees/cap-beads-uzik//./.cache/kat-bgagent-delete-1788697263982/Default/DIPS-journal': No such file or directory

The `.cache/` directory (gitignored, ~62 MB) holds live Chrome profile dirs created by ~25 KAT harnesses as `${ROOT}.cache/kat-<name>-${STAMP}`. Chrome creates and unlinks journal/lock files inside a profile while it runs, so a whole-tree copy taken during a live KAT fails on a file that vanished mid-copy. Under the old machine-wide lock this was unlikely to overlap; with bounded-concurrency slots (uzik) it is reachable, and it reads as a defect in whatever test happens to be copying the tree.

Interim fix landed in uzik: that test now copies with `rsync -a --exclude '/.cache/'` (the child never needs gitignored scratch).

Real fix / acceptance: browser profiles should not live inside the repository at all. Move the `${ROOT}.cache/kat-*` profile convention to the durable root (`durableDir()` from scripts/lib/durable-root.mjs) or a per-run temp dir, so no build, copy, package, or archive of the repo can ever include a live Chrome profile. Acceptance: (1) no `--user-data-dir` under `${ROOT}.cache` remains in scripts/ (extend tests/chrome-profile-isolation.test.ts to assert the profile root is outside the repo); (2) a whole-tree `cp -a` of the repo during a live KAT run succeeds; (3) full suite green.
close_reason: Chrome profiles moved out of repo to ~/cap-evidence/cap-chrome-profiles/ via chromeProfileDir, landed @ 9c1900f8

comments.text:
Candidate pushed: branch cap-beads-9t1b @ fc4cf9ec4e8d49631f6fb02178a71b02d9136aa3 (parent ea037b90). 37 files: scripts/lib/chrome-profile-dir.ts (new), tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts (new), scripts/kat-runner.ts, AGENTS.md, and 33 migrated harnesses.

ACCEPTANCE MAPPED
1. No --user-data-dir under ${ROOT}.cache remains. 32 harness profiles migrated to chromeProfileDir(name) → ~/cap-evidence/cap-chrome-profiles/<name>-<pid>-<ms>-<rand> (durable root, on disk, refuses RAM-backed, refuses anything inside the repo). tests/chrome-profile-location.test.ts scans EVERY launch site in scripts/ (40+ found) for repo-relative forms (${ROOT}, import.meta.url, leading ../) and fails on any; a second test drives the helper's own guarantees (outside repo, on disk, unique per call, name validated so ../escape cannot smuggle a profile back, isInsideRepo resolves the deepest existing ancestor so a symlink INTO the tree still counts as inside).
2. A whole-tree cp -a during a live browser run succeeds — driven for real in-suite: launch Chrome with the extension and a chromeProfileDir profile, confirm the profile is live (entries present), then run the exact failing command cp -a <repo>/. <dst>/. and assert exit 0. Also asserts the tree holds no Chrome profile SIGNATURE (Default/, SingletonLock, Local State, GrShaderCache) at depth 1 or 2.
3. Full suite green: npm test 3898/0 (serial 99/0 + parallel 3799/0, 397 files, 89 s); npm run test:changed fell closed to the full suite; build clean; check:vocabulary OK.

REAL KAT EVIDENCE: deno run -A scripts/kat-runner.ts --only=narrow-toggle → exit 0, 20 passed / 0 failed in 7 s, profile at ~/cap-evidence/cap-chrome-profiles/kat-narrow-toggle-153446-1788701655274-f2b3. The runner's new pruneChromeProfileDirs() call ran without touching it.

FALSIFICATION (4 guards reverted individually, each RED, all restored byte-identical): one KAT's profile moved back inside the repo → static guard RED (4P/1F); helper pointed back into the repo → 2P/3F (helper guarantees + live-copy signature check); uniqueness dropped (fixed suffix) → 4P/1F; prune ignoring age → 4P/1F (a fresh profile must survive). Baseline 5/0 before and after.

SCOPE BOUNDARY (deliberate, stated in the commit): KAT EVIDENCE dirs (screenshots, verdicts) still live under .cache/. A file written once is not a directory a browser churns, and moving them would change evidence paths other lanes read. That is why the in-repo check targets the Chrome profile signature rather than banning .cache/kat-* — a legitimate evidence dir must not fail the guard (it did fail my first draft of that assertion, which is how I noticed). If you want evidence dirs out of the tree too, that is a separate bead with a migration of ~30 OUT defaults.

HYGIENE: harnesses have never cleaned up profiles, and the durable root is not a dump — pruneChromeProfileDirs({olderThanMs: 6h}) runs once per kat-runner run (a live browser is minutes old, so it can never be touched; removal failures are reported, not fatal).

MERGE HEADS-UP: this is the THIRD branch off ea037b90 whose post-commit bump produced 0.3.274 (with 57mu and mkax). Second/third lander needs the bump re-run. Overlap risk is low: this branch touches 33 KAT harness bodies + kat-runner (one added prune call + import), while uzik touches kat-runner's runOne and chrome-launch; mkax touches chrome-launch/chrome-journeys/registry. kat-runner is the only shared file — uzik rewrites runOne's flock wrapper, this adds a prune call above the KAT loop; both belong.

Depends on nothing; uzik's interim .cache exclusion in tests/cdp-client.test.ts stays valid (harmless once no profile is in the tree).

- Feedback: 2026-08-30 — reanalysis 2026-08-30 security lane, findings 9 and 17. Nothing in the product tells the owner what leaves the machine (provider calls, skill imports, the model-driven fetch) or that the provider key sits unencrypted in the profile, and the full factory reset has no browser-driven proof.

- Status: OPEN
- Resume: —
- Priority: P3
- Owner: unassigned
- Workspace: none
- Branch: none
- Base: `fc2255be`

- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: A one-screen "What this extension sends and stores" page is reachable from Settings and states outbound destinations, stored data classes (including that the provider key is stored unencrypted in the profile), the host-access posture, and how to wipe; a `factory-reset` journey seeds every storage class, runs the reset from the Settings button and asserts `enumerateStorageTargets()` is empty afterwards.
  - Context: no telemetry or analytics endpoint exists (security lane grep of every literal host). Outbound today: provider APIs (api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, generativelanguage.googleapis.com, api.deepseek.com, a user-supplied OpenAI-compatible base URL), `extension/lib/skill-import.js` (api.github.com / raw.githubusercontent.com on an explicit import), the model-driven `cap:fetch` (RUN-SCRIPT-FETCH-APPROVAL-01 gates it), the dormant Pyodide CDN (BUNDLE-BUDGET-01 removes or pins it). Stored: `chrome.storage.local` (`providerConfig` including the key — `extension/lib/provider.js` `kvGet/kvSet("providerConfig")`; enrollment, grants, hooks, threads, usage, scheduled tasks), OPFS (per-origin memory, durable runs, artifacts/scripts), `chrome.storage.session` (bridge nonces), IndexedDB (fs grants), Cache. Wipe: Settings → Data & memory per-store Clear (`scripts/data-memory-clear.ts` acceptance) and the factory reset — `extension/lib/factory-reset.js` `FACTORY_RESET_STORAGE_CLASSES` (14), `enumerateStorageTargets` (27), `executeFactoryReset` (104), wired to `#factory-reset-btn` in `extension/options/options.js:2495-2600` with a destructive confirm at 2588. Gap: the reset has unit coverage only — `grep -n factory scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` → nothing. Key hygiene positives to state: write-only Settings input, redacted reads, diagnostics scrubber, storage-hook key-names-only. What must NOT change: the reset semantics; the statement must be generated from the same lists the code uses where possible (e.g. render `FACTORY_RESET_STORAGE_CLASSES` labels rather than a hand-typed copy) so it cannot drift.
  - Reproduce today: (1) build; Settings has no privacy/data statement page (grep `options.html` for "sends" / "stores" → nothing); (2) `grep -n "factory" scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` → no journey.

Do NOT move keys to `chrome.storage.session` in this entry (optional follow-up; record the owner's decision).
  - Steps: (1) Factory-reset journey first: seed a provider config (demo, no real key), one thread, one artifact, one fs grant fixture (the KAT's OPFS handle), a hook deny, then click `#factory-reset-btn` with a genuine gesture, confirm, and assert `enumerateStorageTargets()` (call through a test-seam route or by reading each class from the page) returns empty and the first-run guide is back. title: [CAP-FB-20260829-PROVIDER-SET-NO-BASEURL-01] Saving a preset provider without a base URL yields a config that can never run
description:
## [CAP-FB-20260829-PROVIDER-SET-NO-BASEURL-01] Saving a preset provider without a base URL yields a config that can never run
- Feedback: 2026-08-29 — the one real observation left from the withdrawn `CAP-FB-20260829-SILENT-PROVIDER-RUN-01`
- Updated: 2026-08-29 UTC
- Status: OPEN
- Priority: P3
- Owner: unassigned
- Workspace: none
- Branch: none
- Base: `84991bdd`
- Candidate: —
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: saving a provider that HAS a known preset base URL (`anthropic`, `openai`, `gemini`, `deepseek`) without supplying one stores that preset rather than an empty string, so the permission preflight can derive a real origin; the BYO-endpoint provider, which has no preset, still requires one and says so
- Review: falsification — the assertion must go red against the current route, which stores `baseURL: ""`
- Gates: unit suite; the provider journeys
- Blockers: —
- Next: default `baseURL` from the provider descriptor in the `provider.set` route when the chosen provider has one
- Recover: `git grep -n "provider.set" -- extension/background/routes/provider.js`
- History:
  - 2026-08-29 — measured. `provider.set` with `{ provider: "anthropic", apiKey, model }` and no `baseURL` stores `baseURL: ""`, even though `extension/lib/provider.js` carries `https://api.anthropic.com/v1` as that provider's preset. The permission preflight then derives no origin and the run fails with *"provider permission preflight failed closed: configured provider origin is invalid"* — which blames the origin rather than the missing default. Supplying the base URL explicitly produces the correct message instead (*"the configured provider's exact origin is not granted"*). Low priority because the Settings UI fills the preset, so this is reachable mainly by the route; but a config that can never run should not be storable when the product already knows the right value.
